A new directive, set to be implemented in the coming months, aims to ensure charities can effectively manage their resources and demonstrate a sustainable financial outlook.

The directive requires charities to maintain an annual operating surplus of at least $1 million, with $1 million generated from donations and the remainder from government grants. Charities must also prioritize their spending and make up any budget shortfalls.

The government is also revising guidelines for charity commissioners, ensuring they are qualified to provide services and are transparent in their fees. This change aims to address concerns about the large sums of money being donated to charities and the need for public confidence in their use of funds.

Diane Lebouthillier, Minister of National Revenue, emphasized the importance of clarity and transparency in the charitable sector. "There's a lot of confusion when it comes to charities in Canada, and I think part of those concerns are the very large sums of money that are being given to charities. The public needs to have confidence that the charities we are supporting are making proper decisions with funds that are supposed to go to help the poor and disadvantaged."

Charities, which raise and spend over $3 billion annually in Canada, have expressed concerns about the need to continue raising funds without government permission to remain tax-exempt. However, officials believe existing rules provide charities with the necessary latitude to manage their spending.

The directive aims to ensure charities meet both their values and the expectations of Canadians, while maintaining transparency and accountability in their use of public funds.

A document outlining the recommendations and considerations for adopting ISO C++20, scheduled to become a standard in 2013, is available in PDF format. The ISO C++ committee has reached consensus on two proposals for the standard, focusing on changes to the standard library and language features. The working group will discuss the proposals with the committee after completing its work on the standard. The committee's working group process involves three steps: drafting a proposal, implementing it, and discussing the final proposal. Feedback is solicited throughout the process, and the current proposal has received comments on multiple occasions.

The C++ language provides fundamental facilities for software engineering, including type-safety, polymorphism, abstraction, and modularity. The Standard Template Library (STL) provides a flexible and efficient set of types and functions. The STL does not provide an implementation of all capabilities but offers a convenient mechanism to provide these capabilities via C++ implementations.

The Standard Library was developed through the same process as the Standard Template Library (STL) for design and implementation. The original proposal to change the C++ language from C++03 to C++11 was made in 2003, and the initial draft of the "C++ Concepts Technical Specification" appeared in the same year. It was later updated and published in January 2006. In December 2008, the committee adopted the "C++0x" style of draft language for the next major version of the standard.

The proposal to make changes to the Standard Library as a stand-alone library was initially made in the fall of 2009 but was not formally approved until the spring of 2010. To summarize, C++0x uses the same process as for the Standard Template Library. The process for C++14 is different, focusing on a new programming model for object-oriented programming, including support for generic programming.

The relationship between these two proposed changes to the Standard is that the new programming model is specified using concepts, while the current proposal adds language features needed by such a programming model. The intent of all these concepts is to describe a new programming model, and the standard library and other related aspects will grow as needed to support the proposed model. In the next few days, members of the committee will discuss these concepts and their relationship to the Standard and proposed additions to the "C++0x" draft language. If an item is submitted to the committee making a change to the language and/or standard library, there will be a new committee resolution to do so.

A Florida woman has initiated a legal action against the Jacksonville municipality, contesting a recently enacted ordinance aimed at banning plastic bags within the city. There are no exemptions for specific bag types or sizes, including those used for bulk items, whereas individual bags are exempted, as per the council's definition. The ordinance is designed to prevent large plastic bags, commonly associated with bulk grocery purchases, from being freely distributed in the city.

In response, the Jacksonville-based LGBTQ rights organization, Florida Gays & Lesbians Anti-Defamation Commission (FGLAC), has filed a federal lawsuit challenging the city's plastic bag ban. The brief argues that the ordinance violates the First Amendment, the Equal Protection Clause of the 14th Amendment, and Florida's Unfair Trade Practices Act, which prohibits discrimination in various industries, including food services.

FGLAC cites the example of a Florida doctor who owns a clinic operating out of a warehouse, but refuses to pay for bags to transport medical waste, claiming that plastic bags are a natural product and should not be treated differently than other public goods.

This is only the second time in recent history that a lawsuit has been filed against a city over its plastic bag ban. The previous case, filed in Austin, Texas, was dismissed by the Texas Supreme Court in September due to the ordinance's potential repeal.

The current case is being appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court in an attempt to overturn Jacksonville's ordinance for the second time in less than three years. The city's legal team has stated that they are confident that the evidence will show that the City of Jacksonville illegally discriminated against its citizens for political reasons.

As I reflect on my new book, The Human Surge, I'm struck by the phenomenon of military veterans sharing their war experiences in a candid and intimate way. This trend, which I've dubbed "the human surge," has the potential to be a turning point in how we view war.

The human surge is characterized by veterans' willingness to speak openly about their personal stories and the people they met during their service. In the end, the human surge is a reminder that war is not just about the soldiers who fight it, but about the families and communities who are affected by it. It's a call to action, urging us to come together and support those who have served, and to work towards a more compassionate and understanding world.

A glimpse into the creative process of Luke Skywalker's character development

As I reflect on my experience watching Star Wars: The Force Awakens, I'm reminded of the profound impact it had on me. The film's narrative is woven from the threads of a rich tapestry, and I'm thrilled to share my insights with you. Michael Kogge, the writer, received a call from Disney to take on the story of Luke Skywalker. When Lucasfilm approached Kogge, he shared his thoughts on how his own character would have evolved if he had grown up under Yoda's tutelage. This introspection sparked a series of reflections that I'm honored to share exclusively with you.

My journey with Star Wars began when I was 8 years old, watching A New Hope with my cousins. The scenes featuring Yoda's voice and spirit left an indelible mark on me. I remember thinking that Yoda's voice made the scene where Luke lost his hand seem like a horror movie. As I grew older, I began to appreciate the complexity of the Star Wars universe, recognizing that there's more to the story than just the characters we know.

When I turned 16, I discovered Rogue One, and the entire Star Wars universe opened up to me. I realized that there's so much more to the story than what we see on screen. It's like trying to solve a puzzle with only a few pieces; once you start searching for the missing pieces, the entire picture comes into focus.

George Lucas's connection to Star Wars is deeply personal. As the creator of the mythos, he introduced us to Luke Skywalker. With Rogue One, I gained a deeper understanding of his role in the story. At LucasCon, I visited the Skywalker family estate, built when George Lucas was 15 years old. His parents, Philip and Dianne, had a strong influence on his life, and it's fascinating to see how their values shaped his creative journey.

As I delved deeper into the story, I began to appreciate the simplicity and complexity of the original narrative. A young Rebel pilot, Luke Skywalker, leads a group of rebels on a perilous mission to steal Death Star plans. As he navigates this path, his past comes to the forefront, and he discovers that he's not always who he seems. For a generation raised on science fiction, this is a unique story.

George Lucas has spent his life telling this story through the Star Wars universe. To understand what it would be like to grow up under his guidance is a rare and extraordinary experience. I created a video to share my thoughts on how Luke came to be, and it resonated with many viewers.

The response was overwhelming, and I started receiving emails asking if I was serious about taking on a Luke Skywalker story for Star Wars: The Force Awakens. I said yes, and set a date for April 1st, 2016.

This journey has been a life-changing experience, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to share my insights with you.

Fritzl was arrested in 2015 and initially surrendered to U.S. authorities in June 2013, reportedly for his own protection. He has been cooperating with the investigation, but the details of his cooperation remain unclear. The U.S. Attorney General, Loretta Lynch, announced the charges against Fritzl, stating that he would be brought to justice and that the case would serve as a lesson to others who engage in child sex trafficking.

The case has been under diplomatic review, with the Philippines maintaining jurisdiction over Fritzl due to his citizenship. However, U.S. authorities have jurisdiction due to the international nature of the crimes. Fritzl was indicted in New York in 2016, accused of engaging in an "international sex trafficking conspiracy" that involved the sexual trafficking of girls from the Philippines.

The indictment details Fritzl's alleged involvement in the ring, including his role as the founder and executive director. He is accused of traveling to the Philippines with a victim and operating a club where he provided drugs, alcohol, and prostitutes to his "girlfriends." He also allegedly helped them obtain false identities and passports, and concealed their assets in the United States.

Lynch praised Fritzl's willingness to cooperate with the investigation, stating that he demonstrated integrity and a commitment to serving children. However, she also emphasized the severity of his crimes, stating that they were a classic example of predatory business tactics. The case is expected to proceed in U.S. courts, with a hearing date yet to be set.

A breakthrough in drone technology is taking flight, as a Dutch research team has secured a permit to conduct on-ground trials of an autonomous drone capable of operating in all weather conditions and navigating diverse terrains. The license was granted earlier this month, marking a significant milestone in the development of this innovative drone.

The University of Twente's researchers, in collaboration with Urban Air, a pioneering drone manufacturer, have been given the green light to start testing the drone on October 13th, as reported by De Telegraaf, a prominent Amsterdam-based newspaper.

"We're on a mission to revolutionize the skies," says Ramin Turovsky, Urban Air's director. "This technology will enable drones to work seamlessly in open spaces, indoors, and even underground."

The drone, still unnamed and in design stages, relies on a cutting-edge "batteryless radar system" and "ultra-wideband radar," a radio technology that requires only a single antenna, unlike traditional systems.

The drone is expected to carry a payload of 100 grams and operate autonomously for up to 24 hours without human intervention. Urban Air claims that the drone can function independently in certain situations and withstand rain and snow, although actual testing under these conditions has yet to take place.

The license enables the team to begin testing the drone in the second half of 2015, although the exact type of drone remains unclear.

Guns in UK households

Between 1996 and 2013, the number of UK households with a gun rose from 2.1 million to 4.1 million, an increase of 15%. On average, a gun weighs around 3.7 kilograms and costs approximately US $600. Estimates suggest there may be even more guns in private hands in Scotland, where 3.9 million guns were reported in 2011.

Gun ownership in the UK is predominantly male, with 85% of gun owners being men and 14% being women. The highest income bracket for gun ownership is £60,000, followed by those earning less than £30,000. Interestingly, the proportion of gun owners increases to 89% if household income is between £30,001 and £60,000. In contrast, the lowest proportion of gun owners was found in those earning above £70,000.

Demographically, the majority of gun owners are men, with almost six out of ten men owning a gun compared to just over half of their female counterparts. The age range with the highest proportion of gun owners is between 30 and 49 years old.

According to a survey, nearly all gun owners (96%) reported owning a gun mainly due to fear of violence or fear of someone who may harm them. A further 13% owned guns for sport, while 5% owned them for protection. There is some variation in gun ownership in Scotland, where a higher proportion of men own guns compared to other countries like the US and China.

A recent study has led a diverse group of researchers to develop a novel approach to creating self-replicating materials with specific purposes.

A new method that utilizes a polymer to attach biological cells to biological materials has the potential to revolutionize the production of sensitive detection devices. This groundbreaking research was recently published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Scientists have long sought to harness the power of biological materials in molecular manufacturing processes. Biomimicry has been touted as a promising solution, as cells and biological materials can work together to create complex new materials. However, researchers have faced significant challenges in producing functional bioplastics of any size with specific purposes.

The research team at the University of Michigan explored the properties of pectin, a protein that acts as a glue, binding protein building blocks, nucleic acids, together. When an RNA molecule is packaged in pectin, it is capable of carrying its genetic code.

"We needed a way to enable biological cells to attach to each other, so that a cell grown in a lab would bind to another cell also grown in a lab," said study co-author Mark Lutz, chair of the U-M department of chemistry and co-director of the Molecular and Bioengineering Institute at the U-M Medical School.

Lutz collaborated with researchers from Rice University and the University of California at Berkeley. Lutz's team applied a polymer to a pectin coating, discovering that the adhesive held onto the polymer, which could then stick to itself and subsequently to a cell or a drug. The researchers then used this method to create a cell, which attached to a small, protein-filled vessel filled with cancer virus. The cells were subsequently injected into a patient, and the virus was used to deliver DNA for research.

"The polymer is significantly easier to manufacture in bulk than natural pectin," he said. "We hope this work opens up new opportunities in manufacturing large biological constructs."

"By using a synthetic polymer made from our polymerized pectin with an additional polymer-reacting agent, we were able to develop a three-state pectin surface to which cells could attach and then release their own RNA into the bloodstream," said Rice University chemical engineers John Gentry and Junyi Zhang, co-authors of the paper. "We believe this method has a wide range of potential applications, including the molecular manufacturing of functional synthetic cells capable of sensing in vivo the concentration of specific molecules."

The researchers plan to apply this hybrid approach to other areas of biology.

"We believe that this work could have a wide range of useful applications, not only in nanotechnology but also in the field of nanomedicine," he said.

The research was supported by a National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship, a U-M Postdoctoral Fellowship, a National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship in the Bioengineering program, and National Institutes of Health awards.

In the spring of 2011, Dick Cheney was sipping coffee at his Wisconsin lake house when the topic of Barack Obama came up.

The president, Cheney mused, "has a knack for saying sorry first" when it comes to America, "and for showing the world who we are."

Cheney's tone was laced with a mix of disappointment and frustration, as if he was grappling with the world's gullibility towards the president he once admired.

Cheney's point about Americans' penchant for apologizing resonates, and it's true that we often prioritize making amends. Our greatest thinkers, from ancient sages to American founding fathers, have all emphasized the importance of apologies in our discourse. However, they diverge on how to achieve this goal.

What sets Cheney and I apart is our differing views on what constitutes a good apology. Let's take a look at what some of these thinkers had to say on the subject.

Plato believed that saying "I'm sorry" is imperfect, as it doesn't convey genuine thoughtfulness. Instead, we should strive for more nuanced expressions of regret.

Theophrastus of Tyana saw apologizing as a perfect act, as it requires both sincerity and generosity. He advocated for gestures of charity and kindness to follow an apology.

Confucius emphasized the importance of opening one's heart through apology, but cautioned that it's impossible to apologize for one's ignorance or evil ways. He advocated for showing compassion over mercy.

Madison, in Federalist No 13, highlighted the significance of apologies in shaping our political relationships with the world.

The Declaration of Independence serves as a defining document for our global interactions. When we reflect on our lives and the people we've admired, we're acknowledging our tendency to apologize, albeit imperfectly, in times of need.

A US soldier strolls along a highway in western Afghanistan during the summer of 2011. The Pentagon and Congress are engaged in a contentious debate over the continuation of US troops in Afghanistan beyond 2015, as the Afghan president has vowed to take the fight to the Americans.

The Pentagon is facing a heated discussion over the financial burden of a prolonged campaign against the Taliban, as the Afghan president has pledged to seek an exit from the US military presence and establish an international coalition against Islamic militants after 2015.

Afghan President Hamid Karzai has stated that he will request the NATO coalition to cease hostilities by the end of the year. However, the NATO alliance has indicated that it expects the Afghan government to be capable of assuming its role in the war. The two sides have been negotiating for months regarding the financial contribution the alliance will provide to support the Afghan military's fight against the militants.

Under the terms of a US-Afghan security agreement, all US forces in Afghanistan must remain for at least two more years. Since the Pentagon claims it has the capability to conclude the war in Afghanistan by the end of 2014, the financial burden for US forces will need to be borne by Afghanistan's coffers.

However, Karzai has stated that the United States has failed to uphold the terms of the agreement and that he will not accept Afghan soldiers serving as first responders. He emphasized that Afghan forces should bear the brunt of the fight against the Taliban.

"If someone desires to leave the country, he should do so with his army, police, and justice system," Karzai told the New York Times. "If someone wishes to remain, they cannot continue to say to soldiers, 'I cannot assist you, I cannot halt the bombing.'"

Karzai has been in Washington for months attempting to negotiate the terms of a peace agreement, and in an open letter to President Obama, he stated that he will request the US to withdraw from Afghanistan before his tenure concludes next year.

"We implore you, Mr. President, to sign a political solution by the end of this month, rather than waiting until the end of 2015. This time, we wish to utilize a special arrangement," he wrote.

Karzai insisted that his country will never be secure until Afghan forces assume the lead in that country's future. There are approximately 2,500 US service members in Afghanistan, including some special forces operatives, but the majority of the US force is comprised of foreign forces like Afghan soldiers, guards, and trainers.

The United States has spent more than $150 billion over the past decade to assist Afghan forces in combating the Taliban – some estimates suggest as much as $200 billion during that time.

Karzai's office informed The Washington Post late last month that he would seek assistance in ending the war throughout 2014.

The Obama administration has not been eager to conclude the war under Karzai's leadership and has not disclosed how much of the $25 billion it has already spent will need to be repaid by the United States to aid Afghanistan through 2016.

In an interview about the fight to avoid becoming the next Sudan, Obama stated this week that he expects any exit plan to be in place well before 2015 to provide US forces sufficient time to complete their mission in Afghanistan.

"In our case, we do not have an exit from Afghanistan. I do not believe we have an exit from Iraq. And the same is true for Afghanistan in the foreseeable future," Obama said in the interview.

President Trump issued a decree on Monday to propel a project to erect a barrier along the U.S.-Mexico border. The decree instructed the Department of Homeland Security to launch a nationwide inquiry into individuals who enter the United States illegally and subsequently request a waiver to re-enter, with the condition that the waiver request is accompanied by a waiver of any criminal or civil penalties related to the original entry request. The administration claimed the move would enhance U.S. security by deploying more personnel to the border.

"The United States will not tolerate any unauthorized entries into our nation," Trump stated during the signing.

The American Civil Liberties Union released a statement criticizing Trump for attempting to circumvent Congress and implement an immigration policy through executive decree.

The president stated he would initiate his decree by implementing a federal hiring freeze, which is already in effect for most federal agencies, and would take steps to enforce existing immigration laws, including the expansion of existing programs to identify and deport individuals without legal status.

The decree will complement a series of actions already announced by the administration aimed at combating illegal immigration, including hiring additional Border Patrol agents and increasing the cost of visas for individuals who enter the country illegally.

Immigration advocates claimed Trump's decree is merely the beginning. They have already begun preparing their legal defense strategies.

The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services will begin issuing "deferred action" applications, commonly referred to as work permits, to DACA recipients, who are typically 18 years old when their DACA status expires in March 2019. This means that approximately 1.6 million individuals without legal status will no longer be at risk of deportation but may be eligible to work or receive federal aid. They will also be eligible for a DACA renewal in March 2021.

Furthermore, the administration will issue new regulations to protect Dreamers from deportation. These regulations will include new requirements for employers who hire employees without legal status.

The government has already begun issuing legal protection documents for Dreamers.

"This is not the end of our fight to protect Dreamers and the 11 million individuals without legal status in our country," said Cecillia Wang, director of policy, campaigns, and programs for the American Civil Liberties Union, in an interview with the Washington Post.

"We will not surrender. There are many individuals who will be unhappy with this executive decree, and it appears President Trump may be forced to reverse course in the future."

A West Virginia state senator has introduced a bill aimed at limiting a transgender student's bathroom choices in high school. Senator Jay Davis, a Republican, claims the bill is not about targeting gender identity but rather ensuring that a biological boy who identifies as a girl uses the correct restroom. Davis filed the bill on August 16, which would prohibit transgender students from using school bathrooms that align with their gender identity. He argues that allowing a biological boy to use the girls' bathroom could lead to confusion and potential issues in the boys' bathroom.

The bill requires students to demonstrate a legitimate, medically-justified, and personal interest in using a separate restroom. Dan Becker, a representative from the American Civil Liberties Union of West Virginia, believes the bill is part of a larger anti-trans movement in the state. Becker argues that the bill is targeting transgender children, who already face discrimination and marginalization.

Senator Davis responded by questioning the need for transgender students to use the bathroom that aligns with their gender identity. He also expressed concerns about transgender adults taking advantage of public showers, locker rooms, and restrooms. The student's family has expressed concerns about privacy, and Davis believes the student should be allowed to transition at their own pace.

The West Virginia House State Government Committee has scheduled a hearing on August 23 to discuss the bill.

The forthcoming Star Destroyer - a behemoth of a ship, in my opinion - is about to make its cinematic debut. I'm excited to share with you the early concept art and storyboards that brought this massive vessel to life. I'm deliberately withholding the identity of the Star Destroyer that's closest to your heart, but I'm hoping you'll appreciate the journey it took to get there.

At the end of 2015, the design for this colossal starship was first conceptualized for the upcoming film Star Wars: Episode VIII. Fans of The Force Awakens will recall that the filmmakers aimed to explore the various ships from the original trilogy, imagining how they might have evolved if they had continued on their original trajectory.

These early design sketches offer a glimpse into the first iteration of the new Star Destroyer. The original hull features a prominent deflector dish, as well as several forward deflectors that weren't present in the original film. The shape of the original hull bears a striking resemblance to the Death Star, the iconic battle station from the Star Wars franchise. These designs include the main hull (bottom) and side hull, with large engines along the bottom of the main hull, set against a crisp white background.

As concept artists refined their ideas during the summer of 2015, they experimented with various interpretations of the hull design, resulting in a range of fascinating concepts. Some of these early versions are showcased in this image, featuring a complex deflector design, smaller engines, and intricate red/white detailing on the side pods and bow. Additional design elements include white/red lights and ports for deflector plates.

After several months of refinement, the concept artists continued to iterate on the design, making incremental changes to the hulls. The second and third iterations exhibit a more aggressive design, with subtle differences in detail. I think they look particularly striking with the red/white trim and prominent deflector dish. The fourth iteration, however, eschews the dish and adopts a simpler, more aggressive design.

In February 2016, the final ship concept was solidified, revealing the exact shape of the new Star Destroyer. This design is larger than the original concepts, which is evident in the early concept art. This size difference might explain why the larger ships appear more impressive in the film Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back.

A recent image has circulated online, showcasing a revised version of the new Star Destroyer with minor adjustments. The current iteration of the Star Destroyer is a substantial design, as you can see. It's larger than the original design above.

That's a glimpse into the Star Destroyer concept designs for Episode VIII. I'd like to emphasize that I didn't create any of these designs myself. I'm curious to know which one resonates with you the most. What struck me during this process was the challenge of crafting a design that captured the same essence and aesthetic as the original Star Destroyer from the classic Star Wars film series. This is just the beginning of our journey to explore the new Star Destroyer.

The government is under pressure to establish a national database for firearms dealers to prevent illegal weapons from entering the wrong hands. The Council of Canadian Cities and Communities, representing over 100 cities and towns across the country, has called for a national registry as part of a report on gun violence prevention strategies.

The report aims to promote municipal involvement in addressing violence against women and girls. Jennifer Wong, the council's executive director, emphasized the need for action, stating, "The gun registry is a valuable tool that should be explored. We need to think about where the information is, who owns it, and how to ensure access."

The report recommends establishing and maintaining a registry for firearms transactions and sales, building upon existing provincial registration programs. This registry could help track firearms in circulation, identify and seize weapons owned by suspects, and aid law enforcement in tracking firearms used in crimes.

Paul Vandal, senior vice-president of the Council of Canadian Cities, noted that understanding the flow of firearms is crucial in preventing mass shootings. "When you have to account for the many shootings that happen each year, that information is critical. That's why we're asking for data to better understand what we can do to make this system safe."

The debate should focus on creating a safe and effective system for reporting firearm crime, ensuring the registry is accessible and used at the local level, and providing for a meaningful review. A government report published last month also recommended creating a national registry, and Ottawa is considering implementation options.

New Democratic MP Murray Rankin has tabled a motion calling for the registry's establishment and improved oversight. The federal budget has allocated $6.7-million for a national gun registry study and evaluation program, examining the need for and advantages of different registry forms.

Public Safety Minister Steven Blaney's director of communications, David Houlihan, stated, "The budget recognizes that there are various approaches to improving gun registration. Our government has committed to establishing a national registry and will continue to work within the framework established last year."

A University of London Crime Lab report concluded that gun registration is not effective in preventing crime, citing difficulties in administration and potential misuse.

The University of Queensland recently conducted a survey to analyze the most popular animal names on the internet. The results revealed that the pig is the second most popular animal name in Australian internet culture, closely following the cat.

1. Cat (12.1 million users)

2. Horse (10.9 million)

3. Dog (7.2 million)

4. Kangaroo (6.5 million)

5. Pig (6.4 million)

6. Donkey (6.3 million)

7. Dog, fox, and bear (5.7 million)

8. Dog, fox, and dog (5.3 million)

9. Pig, pig, pig (4.7 million)

10. Pig (4.5 million)

The survey also found that the most common animal name used by Australians to describe themselves is the cat, while the pig is the least common name, accounting for only 1.9% of online Australians.

Associate Professor Joanne Webster of the university's school of media and communication commented on the findings, saying that the pig has played a significant role in Australian internet culture and has been a favorite among Australians for a long time.

The survey's results also revealed that Australian internet users are highly aware of Australia's unique animal language and that the pig is not a common animal name globally.

Associate Professor Julia Halliday-Smith, who conducted the survey, noted that the results were unexpected, given the global popularity of pigs.

Despite the pig's strong presence on the Australian internet, the researchers found that Australians are more likely to be offended than the global public.

The researchers hope that their findings will spark discussions among Australian internet users, similar to those that occurred globally when the United States banned certain words from internet chatrooms.

The findings are published in the International Journal of Communication.

The notion that the first page of the New Testament, comprising Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, is the infallible word of God has been a subject of debate among many. The credibility of this sacred text has been questioned by some due to perceived errors and misconceptions. I aim to address these concerns and explore the topic further in this article.

A friend recently brought this issue to my attention after reading "The Bible Doesn't Know It All: Why Your Favorite Version is Wrong" by Kevin DeYoung, a professor of philosophy and theology at Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. DeYoung's work critiques various aspects of the Bible, including the New Testament. I will outline the basics and then delve into the meat of the matter.

The Basics

The concept of inerrancy typically encompasses six core principles: the historicity of biblical stories, the inspiration of literary works, the meaning of God's commandments, historical facts, the historicity of Jesus Christ, and the authority of the New Testament. Additionally, scriptures are often viewed as the word of God as received by the original audience.

The term inerrancy has also been employed to justify or downplay other historical and theological claims within the Bible. For instance, it is often used to explain the lack of historical authenticity of the gospels or to deny theological statements attributed to Jesus.

Determining the infallibility of the Bible is a complex task. Many Christians believe that the biblical stories speak for themselves and are therefore error-free. However, this raises questions about what it means for the Bible to "speak for itself." Does it mean that the Bible speaks only for itself or for a specific culture or time period?

In reality, Christians have always sought to understand the Bible's words within the context of Christian truth. The Bible cannot speak for itself because it is the Word of God, revealed to prophets and apostles. While God instructed them to write what they would deliver to the world, the Bible's words are not self-explanatory.

Not all language is included in the Bible, and what is included is not necessarily comprehensive. When people say "it doesn't matter," they often mean that what is not said does not matter. However, if a book or language is not included in the canon of Holy Scripture, it is essential to consider the implications for the books that are included.

The Errors of Inerrancy

If the Bible is assumed to be infallible solely because it does not contain everything or nothing, then the books it does contain must be understood within the context of Christian truth.

The Enigmatic Purpose of the Bible

Many individuals assume that Jesus is a personal, unconditional teacher who provides answers to our daily concerns. While this is true for numerous people, it is crucial to question whether the Bible contains all the answers. The truth is, it doesn't even come close.

Let's delve into the origins of the Bible. If something has always been true, and it can be scientifically proven like gravity, why not explore the Bible's beginnings or ask where it originated? Or, why didn't it address these matters?

To gain a deeper understanding, we must examine what we believe we will find in the Bible. The answer is straightforward: there is no actual "Bible." Instead, there is a narrative that recounts events and the people involved. What we discover in the Bible is merely a way to grant us permission to continue following the story.

This concept is explored in Christopher Hitchens' book, "The Bible is Not What it Seems." He notes that the book is a historical account that spans over a thousand years. There is no actual history of the Jews, Romans, Moses, David, Jesus, the Temple, the apostles, or any other event. It is a series of "history lessons."

However, Hitchens' point is that the story of Jesus is not the actual story.

The Real Story

The real story of Jesus can be found in the 4 Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. It also includes the story of the first and second temples, the building of the tower of Babel, and the Jewish rejection and conversion to Christianity. The story revolves around the death and resurrection of Jesus, and it is based on an event that actually occurred. It is a story about a man.

It is essential to recognize that the real story has been lost for centuries, but there are still valuable insights to be gained.

The Christian religion became official in the first century. This fact explains many of the discrepancies found in Christianity today. For instance, in our modern world, there are numerous "Christians" who claim to be "just like" Jesus, but they disagree on significant details. It appears that these differences primarily arose because, in the first age of the Christian story, there was no authority to settle these disputes, and many people simply created their own stories as a means of doing so.

Many Christian leaders believe that the Bible contains the "best" version of the Christian story and, therefore, are not open to change. In "The New Testament and the Question of Canonization" (2000), Gerald T. Hommel argues that the earliest followers of Jesus accepted a collection of writings called Q, which is recognized as part of the New Testament. If other early Christians accepted the Q documents as part of the New Testament, we can trace the beginnings of the canon.

Is it canon? The New Testament is the Christian Bible, but not necessarily the one attributed to Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. It is crucial to remember that the Q documents are not part of the New Testament canon.

The Bible is not the "one book and no other" version.

A more significant point is that the Bible is not the "one book and no other" version. There have been numerous variations, and in some cases, the Q documents are no longer available because they were never canonized. The basic story of Jesus and his ministry remained largely the same over at least the first 500 years of his ministry, which we now know to be the time of Jesus' murder, crucifixion, and resurrection.

The story of Jesus changed little as the years went by because people continued to create their own accounts and question what Jesus did. Many believed that Jesus simply showed up one day, performed a miracle at the wedding of Cana, and people assumed Jesus was the Messiah.

This is not reflected in the Christian Bible. The story told in the Bible is that Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate.

The stories that follow are not about an innocent virgin who was killed for sin.

I believe, however, that it is true, and I will leave it to my readers to decide, whether or not Jesus was married—or even whether or not he married. There is one story that is common to most Christian sources that I can provide for this question.

A spatial index is a clever way to store and query data that describes objects situated in a geometric space. Its primary function is to facilitate spatial queries, which retrieve data based on the spatial connections between objects. For instance, a spatial index could be employed to rapidly identify all objects within a specific radius of a designated point, or to locate the closest object to a given point.

Spatial indexes are frequently utilized in geographic information systems (GIS) and other applications that handle spatial data. They can be implemented using a range of data structures, such as quadtrees, R-trees, and k-d trees. The selection of data structure hinges on the specific requirements of the application, including the nature and scale of the data, the types of spatial queries that will be executed, and the desired level of performance.

Spatial indexes can significantly enhance the performance of spatial queries by minimizing the number of objects that must be examined. For example, if a spatial index is employed to store a large dataset of points, a query to identify all points within a specific radius of a designated point can be satisfied by examining only a limited subset of the points, rather than the entire dataset. This can greatly reduce the time and resources required to execute the query.

Detroit, Michigan - In a significant move, automakers are rapidly developing self-driving technology following Google's substantial investment. However, they are not waiting for regulatory clearance to test these vehicles on US roads. 

Ford's latest Mustang model, unveiled at the Detroit auto show, is displayed at the Ford showroom in Dearborn, Michigan. 

The Federal Highway Administration has announced that it will release guidelines for testing self-driving vehicles on public roads by August 2019. Nevertheless, the agency has yet to approve rules for self-driving vehicles on US roads, and many automakers are proceeding without regulatory approval. 

Recently, General Motors, Volvo, and other major car manufacturers have been testing their self-driving technology on public roads or testing sites with government agencies and the public. 

GM is conducting self-driving tests in Austin, Texas, with the city government and local authorities. Ford is testing self-driving technology in San Francisco with local officials, while Volvo is testing its technology in Sweden. 

"Companies are following the same regulatory process as the states have developed their regulations," said GM spokesman Greg Martin, declining to comment on specific operations or policies of individual companies.

The auto industry quickly adopted self-driving technology after Google introduced it to the public in 2009. The US Transportation Department required manufacturers to have a human driver in vehicles with self-driving technology for at least 60,000 miles a year, and then submit plans to show they have fully automated car technology by January 2018.

For instance, the Federal Highway Administration has determined that autonomous vehicles are safe with a human sitting on the steering wheel at all times and must have a steering wheel and pedals under federal safety standards by at least 2019, and a fully autonomous vehicle by at least 2027.

However, self-driving technology testing in Arizona, California, and Texas is expected to be a matter of months, and some US states will likely develop their own rules to ensure these cars can be used on public roads.

Texas Department of Transportation spokesman Mark Linscope said state officials are working on developing self-driving vehicle rules but had no further comment. 

Automakers claim they will continue to explore Google's technology, but their appetite for autonomous vehicles is unlikely to diminish, and many see them as the future of personal mobility.

Google plans to unveil an autonomous vehicle at the North American International Auto Show next week, according to several sources familiar with the company's plans. The ride-hailing giant is reportedly considering California as a potential location.

The technology could benefit consumers who are currently restricted from using self-driving vehicles because the rules in various states allow human drivers to monitor the software but not have to be in control unless there is an emergency or malfunction.

"The market for the vehicles is likely to increase over time because they will be much safer and allow for more convenient travel," said Scott Griffith, vice president of Ford's product strategy in North America.

"There is a great opportunity for Ford to provide customers with the safest, most cost-effective vehicle in transportation."

The California Department of Motor Vehicles is the only state entity that will allow fully autonomous car development if it approves the self-driving vehicle rules from the Federal Highway Administration, according to Robert McElroy, director of research and innovation at IBISWorld.

"It seems quite likely that CA will approve for all kinds of different types of vehicles for their public roads. The self-driving car is on the table. Right now the states are not. There's a lot of regulatory hurdles, and people are still figuring out the technical aspects," McElroy said.

"But eventually it has to happen."

(Reporting by Alistair Bell; Editing by Jeffrey Benkoe)

A few years ago, I started exploring the Star Wars universe. Watching Star Wars Rebels has been a thrilling experience, and I've been eager to learn more about the Force. I went back to reading the original Star Wars book, The Jedi Path: A Manual for Living a Life of Balance, and have been thoroughly enjoying it.

I recently had a fascinating conversation with a friend about Star Wars Rebels. He mentioned being excited about the show, but I didn't grasp what he was enthusiastic about until now.

Here's a snippet from our conversation:

"I'm a huge Star Wars fan. I've loved the series since its inception in the mid-1990s... I've always wanted an animated show."

I was intrigued to learn more about the show's development. Apparently, there was a disagreement with George Lucas in 2008 regarding the use of prequels in the animated series. This led to the project being kept off Disney's public schedules.

George Lucas had concerns about creating an ongoing narrative in the same continuity as the original trilogy. He was worried that focusing on the prequels would make the original trilogy seem irrelevant. Disney asked him to produce a standalone series, but George refused, citing his desire to tell the story in chronological order.

It's remarkable to see how much nostalgia and love for the original Star Wars stories drives the Rebels animated series. Lucas's passion for these stories is palpable, and it's clear that he values the opportunity to bring all the stories together in a single sequence.

In some ways, the Prequels played a significant role in shaping Lucas's creative vision. It's intriguing to think about what could have happened if he had continued working on the Prequels.

This document provides a comprehensive guide on setting up a simple Java application and utilizing it locally. A typical application comprises two primary components: a web application and an embedded server. The web application is responsible for serving web pages, while the embedded server manages embedded resources. Applications are usually deployed to a server via various protocols, with HTTP/1.1 being the recommended standard.

The server can be hosted on a web server, a web host, or a networked web server. Web applications are typically hosted on a web server.

The following sections outline a detailed description of how to set up applications for a web server.

1.1.1. Setting Up the Web Server

A web application runs on a web server, which serves as the primary server for the application.

Web servers are designed to facilitate the deployment of applications. They contain software that enables communication between the server and web application clients, either directly or through various protocols. The software in web servers performs a range of tasks, including:

Handling networking, management, and administrative tasks

Enabling communication between the server and clients

Installing, configuring, and running web application frameworks

Managing applications and databases

Handling client requests and connections

Authenticating and authorizing users

Providing file sharing and network file serving

1.1.2. Configuration and Deployment

Web servers typically have default configurations that can be customized. You can adjust these settings to enable your server to run a web application:

Hosting the application on a web server, which is the most common configuration

Specifying the application's default folder

When creating your application, consider the following:

Hosting and running your application on a non-standard web server

Configuring your application to work on a popular web server

The following sections offer configuration options for different types of applications.

1.1.2.1. Hosting a Web Application on a Typical Web Server

As seen earlier, most web applications serve content on standard web servers like Apache, Nginx, or Lighttpd. Apache allows web applications to communicate with each other.

By default, an application server is configured to provide various services, including:

Handling large applications

Enabling priority settings for applications

Configuring different types of applications for various priority settings

If your application is an application server, you can enable HTTP/2 to improve performance. You can also use the -proto http2 command line option to enable HTTP/2, which removes support for HTTP/1.1.

An application server can also enable features useful to developers, such as caching or HTTP proxy. To learn how to configure application servers for caching, proxy, or both, refer to the documentation on various application server types.

Palo Alto, California, December 9, 2016 - The Bay Area Air Quality Management District and California Air Resources Board jointly announce that the air quality index has reached an unprecedented level this year, with a score of 96.97 on Wednesday evening. This marks a significant increase from last year's levels, which were already concerning.

Air Resource Board Chairwoman Kristine Grow expressed her concerns, stating, "We're seeing more pollutants this year than we did last year, and they're going to remain at high levels for a while because of the drought." The air quality index measures particulate matter, tiny particles smaller than 10 micrometers that pose the greatest health hazard to people.

The "Dome Summit" event, scheduled to take place in Oakland on Thursday, aims to educate the public about air quality and its health effects. More than 25,000 people are expected to attend. Grow emphasized the importance of raising awareness about air pollution, particularly its impact on children's health.

The California Air Resources Board's Air Quality Index combines two measures: the PM 2.5 value and the ozone index. The air quality index has improved significantly since 2000, with average annual concentrations dropping below 100. However, this year's "Dome Summit" may be one reason for the increase.

Grow explained, "We're seeing increases in both pollutants. If it gets hotter and drier, the air gets dirtier, and that's when it comes into contact with particulate matter." The Bay Area has not experienced a drought this long in years, and a warm, dry winter has not helped.

The Bay Area has seen a surge in particulate matter pollution since the 1960s, largely due to urbanization and traffic on highways. However, the rate of particulate matter and ozone pollution has dropped significantly in the last 30 years.

Jennifer Sass, senior scientist for the Healthy Air Council, emphasized the importance of addressing air pollution. Life's complexities can have a profound impact on one's well-being, and navigating mental health challenges can be a daunting task. Fortunately, many people who face mental health issues are able to recover and lead fulfilling lives. To better understand the most common mental health concerns and how to identify them in oneself or loved ones, consider the following:

1. Depression: This pervasive mental health issue can manifest physically, causing:

A shift in appetite habits

Increased sleep needs

Irritability

Long-term depression can make it challenging to be alone, but therapy can be effective in managing symptoms.

2. Bulimia: Characterized by feelings of being overly full or bloated, bulimia can lead to physical changes that make daily life more difficult, including:

Increased sensitivity to sunlight

Fatigue

Loss of appetite

Diarrhea and vomiting

Severe cases of bulimia require professional help.

3. Addiction: Whether related to substance use or other compulsive behaviors, addiction can have a profound impact on mental health. Understanding the signs and symptoms of addiction can be crucial in seeking help.

4. Anorexia: This eating disorder can manifest physically, causing:

Loss of appetite

Vomiting

Sudden, unexpected weight loss

Fatigue

Low self-esteem

Changes in sleep patterns

Feelings of worthlessness

Untreated anorexia can lead to isolation, shame, and hopelessness.

5. Bipolar disorder: Characterized by rapid mood shifts between depression and mania, bipolar disorder can be challenging to understand and manage. If you or a loved one is struggling with mood control, professional help is essential.

6. Traumatic brain injury: A serious injury to the brain can cause physical symptoms, including:

Severe headaches

Muscle aches

Difficulty concentrating

Changes in vision

Symptoms can range from mild to severe and may require physical therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, music therapy, or medication.

7. Substance abuse: The devastating impact of substance abuse on mental health is well-documented. Recognizing the signs and symptoms of addiction, including changes in appetite, fatigue, irritability, and insomnia, can be crucial in seeking help.

Other researchers suggest that when people witness a "typical mass shooting" – one in which four or more people are killed – it can deter individuals from seeking help for mental health issues. Summary:

- Establishes a system for verifying residency status.

- Prohibits individuals from:

- Encouraging, accepting, or attempting to encourage non-residents to:

(1) Obtain a driver's permit,

(2) Register a vehicle,

(3) Register to vote in California, or

(4) Apply for a veterans' enrollment card.

- Allows, but does not require, the department to maintain an official list of individuals without legal residency in the state.

- Prohibits individuals from knowingly providing:

- A driver's permit,

- A voter registration card, or

- Proof of residency under:

(A) Section 8 of Article VI of this Code.

(B) Section 8 of Article V of this Code.

- Prohibits individuals from knowingly charging a fee for providing non-residents with:

(1) An immigrant visa or a recognized visa document.

(2) A document allowing a non-resident to appear in a naturalization application.

(1) To provide required information for non-resident registration,

- Specifies that fees received from entities providing identification cards shall be deposited into the Taxpayer Assistance Account.

- Provides for the imposition of fines and civil penalties for violations.

- Treats any payment received under this Act as a debt to the state and provides for its collection.

- Authorizes payment of costs and attorney's fees incurred by the state's attorney's office.

- Permits a board of examiners to establish and administer a program determining voter qualifications for citizenship status.

- Requires identification card applicants to comply with provisions relating to driver's license duties and requirements.

On November 10, a federal jury delivered a verdict in the trial of Jeffrey Sterling, a former CIA contractor accused of leaking classified information to a journalist. The jury found Sterling guilty of three counts related to the alleged leaks.

Sterling's legal team has filed a motion requesting a judgment of acquittal, citing concerns about the government's legal theory and the evidence presented in court. The motion argues that the prosecution's theory is flawed and that the charges should be dismissed.

The government's legal theory is problematic because it could potentially criminalize whistleblowers who act in good faith. The government's argument is akin to saying that a car is safe even after it has exploded, as long as the explosion occurred within the vehicle.

The media coverage of the case has focused on Sterling rather than the actual conduct at issue. Even if we could prove that Sterling took steps to protect classified information, he could still be convicted under the government's theory. This is because the government is asking jurors to imagine that Sterling had malicious intent, rather than a legitimate interest in the publication of the information.

It is unlikely that the government has been out of touch with the public debate and reporting in the national security community. The U.S. government frequently publishes operational details and intelligence assessments related to counterterrorism operations.

Imagine a vibrant, flavorful sauce that's perfect for topping your favorite dishes. Pico de gallo is a traditional Mexican condiment made with a medley of ingredients, including tomatoes, onions, garlic, and cilantro. But what sets this recipe apart is the addition of shredded cheese, adding a creamy texture and richness to the dish.

This pico de gallo is part of our ongoing series, "Flavors of the World," where we explore new and exciting recipes from around the globe. To stay up-to-date on the latest recipes, be sure to sign up for our newsletter and follow us on social media.

Prep Time: 10 minutes | Cook Time: 5 minutes | Total Time: 15 minutes | Servings: 4

Ingredients:

* 1 medium tomato
* 2 large onions
* 1/2 cup minced garlic
* 1 teaspoon white vinegar
* 1/2 teaspoon salt
* 1/2 cup olive oil
* 1/4 cup chopped cilantro
* 1/2 cup shredded cheese

Instructions:

1. Begin by washing and cutting off any black bits from the tomatoes. Then, puree the tomatoes in a blender or food processor until smooth.
2. Add the onion, garlic, vinegar, salt, and olive oil to the blender. Cook and stir until well-combined.
3. Stir in the remaining ingredients, including the shredded cheese.
4. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
5. Pour the sauce over your favorite dish and heat through.

Tips and Variations:

* For a lighter consistency, you can strain the sauce through a sieve or cheesecloth before serving.
* Experiment with different types of cheese for a unique flavor profile.

To strike a balance in the debate about taxing Bitcoin, let's explore alternative financial systems.

In the pre-World War I era, taxation was rare. Most countries operated under a single national tax law, except for the two warring superpowers. The British Empire, with its vast influence, imposed significant taxes. However, international money transfers required intermediaries, often banks, which are now under scrutiny for money laundering. Authorities may prosecute, convict, or imprison banks holding private information.

As the US is a major trading partner, it's likely that Bitcoin will generate revenue for some countries. If the US adopts laws similar to those for other currencies, Bitcoin's volume may decrease, but its value may increase.

Bitcoin is already considered a secure and efficient financial system, with more liquidity than national central banks and exponential growth in value.

Given these circumstances, it's possible that a country might impose a tax on Bitcoin. However, a more effective approach would be a sales tax or an actual tax.

Taxing Bitcoin requires compromises, such as creating a commodity-backed currency, establishing tax havens, or implementing strict compliance measures. Countries that have attempted this, like the Netherlands, Belgium, and Israel, are not considered economic powerhouses.

Developing countries should prioritize establishing a legitimate, effective, and stable financial system to compete with Western capitalism. Recognizing Bitcoin as a legitimate form of money or supporting a legal industry that builds and supports it would be beneficial for governments, especially emerging ones.

I recently spent a few weeks with my parents in Washington County, Pennsylvania, and had the chance to sit down with our new landlord, Dennis. We had a lovely conversation at the kitchen table, and I was asked about my apartment, the state of the economy, and what my parents had done for me. Dennis was kind and thoughtful, and when he mentioned that I was lucky to have a good apartment, I felt truly grateful.

That evening, I took a walk in the middle of the night and started thinking about my future. I wondered if my parents would be alive next month and what I wanted to do with my life.

I reflected on the past few years and remembered what they would say as they left. They would say, "we took a risk, but we're happy." I cherish those words and consider them their legacy to me. If they were here now, they'd be smiling and sharing what they're grateful for, not dwelling on their thoughts. I'm glad they gave me that opportunity.

As for what I'll be doing for the rest of my life, I'm still figuring that out. My father left home when I was 14, and his mother would often say that there's a "good time to grow up." I remember visiting my family at the hospital when I was young, and they were all excited – the family was together, and I was growing up.

When I was around 11, I lived with my father, but it wasn't ideal. My parents had made a choice between us, and I was the youngest one living with my dad and step-mom, who's now my mother-in-law. I was a quiet child, even quieter than my dad. At school, we would share classrooms, and I remember sitting with my teacher, being very quiet and not making a peep, until one day we had a party and I was thrilled.

It's amusing to me now that people often talk about me in the same way I was talked about as a child. I went to school the same way I did the day I met my school friends and the day I met my dad. The most important thing was having a good friendship with a girl at school. I remember being quiet during that period, and my friend was shy. My teacher asked her something, and I didn't quite hear what she said, but I remember it because she asked me, "how are you?" and I replied, "fine."

I had a big crush on a girl at school, and it was awkward. I didn't want to make her stand out, but I hated school so much that I didn't care about anything else except sitting quietly in class and doing my homework. My mom was proud of me, and I remember her going through similar experiences before she lost my dad. Her mother was wealthy, and she sent me to a nice private school. Then I got the call that she'd found a new girlfriend, and it made me sad, so I didn't take a picture with her.

I went to middle school, but I didn't like it. It had the best teacher in the school, though. I remember one day he had me in a room with other students and asked, "what's your name?" and I replied, and he said, "Kenny." I said, "what? Kenny what?" At that point, I just remember turning off the recorder. That was the happiest day of my life – from middle school to the teacher.

Then I went to middle school, and it wasn't great. I got into fights all the time, and I had no control over them. There were always fights at school, and one day it got to the point where I felt exhausted. The next day, my teacher told me I was too upset to come out anymore, and I didn't want to leave a fight I'd already won. I'd made my choice.

Professor Alley highlighted the significance of the Antarctic ice sheet's mass loss, stating that it has been accelerating over the past few decades. The researchers also emphasized the importance of considering the impact of sea level rise on major cities and island nations. They warned that if all the sea level rise were to occur, many cities would be at risk of flooding, and some island nations could potentially disappear.

The study's findings are supported by recent data, which shows that the oceans have experienced significant melting over the past decade. The researchers also discussed the impact of the Greenland ice sheet's melting, which is responsible for releasing a significant amount of freshwater into the oceans. They estimated that Greenland will lose around 10 billion tonnes of ice this year, equivalent to filling the Nile River over 100 times.

The study's findings have significant implications for our understanding of climate change and its impact on our planet. The researchers emphasized the importance of continued research into the relationship between changes in land ice and global sea levels.

The notion that one can't accurately gauge a person's character based on superficial traits is a misconception. Through personal experience, we've learned that appearances can be deceiving, just as a book's cover doesn't always reflect its contents. The best we can do is judge someone based on their actions and the consequences that follow. These traits are often referred to as Characteristic Profiles.

Characteristic Profiles are crucial because they determine what we perceive as "good" and "bad" in a character. These profiles are dynamic and influenced by our individual perspectives. In a game, Characteristic Profiles are essential in shaping our characters' personalities and behaviors.

Players have the autonomy to decide which Characteristic Profiles they want to adopt. Others may need to either acquire them at the expense of experience points or navigate the complexities of the game world to achieve their desired profiles. If a character's profiles are chosen randomly, they often prove ineffective.

Characteristic Profiles play a vital role in shaping a character's personality. If you're playing a virtuous character, you likely enjoy the actions you take and the choices you make. You should strive to utilize these profiles to your advantage. Conversely, if you're playing an antagonistic character and don't utilize their profiles, it's not because you're inherently bad – it's simply because you don't resonate with those traits.

The same applies to a character's relationships with friends and foes. Their friends and allies can influence their Characteristic Profiles, and vice versa. When interacting with NPCs, a character can learn to appreciate and even desire the behaviors that align with their profiles. Similarly, when dealing with characters who don't mesh with their own profiles, they can develop an aversion to those relationships.

A character's Personality is developed through their Characteristic Profiles, which in turn influence how others perceive them and how they interact with the world. By accessing the Characteristics tab, players can view and edit their profiles, which will be listed in the right-hand column. They can either enter new profiles or create new ones, taking care to remember their Characteristic Profiles.

Characteristic Profiles can be acquired or modified, but only by the player themselves. If a player is uncertain about what a Characteristic Profile is or how to create a new one, the Game Master may offer guidance and support.

A Characteristic Profile can take the form of a Skill, Profession, or Style. Skills have a number of ranks, similar to abilities, and may be influenced by a character's class sheet. Professions are skills centered around materials, tools, or technology, and can be used to create weapons, armor, and other items. Styles, also known as Favours, have two ranks: one to buy and one to spend. By developing their Characteristic Profiles, players can enhance their characters' abilities and personalities.

Today, I'm compelled to share my thoughts on politics, a topic I rarely discuss. The recent election and Brexit vote have left me with a sense of déjà vu, reminiscent of the 1950s. I wish someone had taken a closer look at our society 40 years ago.

As I reflect on the current state of our country, I'm struck by the growing sense of anxiety among citizens. Politicians are often unwilling to take a stand on crucial issues like the NHS, education, and the environment. Every parliamentary vote that cuts wages and conditions for millions, or reduces the living wage, council housing, and tax-free childcare, is a stark reminder of this.

In 2012, I attended my first trade union conference as secretary of the RMT. The mood was optimistic, and I felt that trade unions could work together to secure decent conditions for the people. Today, however, I'm struck by the lack of passion among our elected representatives, the media, and even within the Labour Party.

The government's emphasis on unity and "We're in this together" rhetoric rings hollow when public services are under attack. The silence from the Tories is deafening, and it's as if they're trying to avoid accountability for their rhetoric on the NHS and social care. When this happens, action is the only answer. We must organize the working class to take power.

The Tory government's disdain for trade unions is evident in their attempts to shut them down in court. In the past five years, our unions have been shut down 13 times in England and Wales. As a trade unionist, I know that the working class does not support the Tories and never has.

Despite this, I still believe that trade unions can bring about change. We must reach out to other sections of the working class and fight against the Tories and the Labour Party together. That's my conviction, and I fear that many in the trade union movement have lost sight of this.

The trade unions must evolve from being the voice of the working class and socialism to being a force that represents the ruling class and the ultra-right wing. The consequences of Tory policies are clear: cuts to tax credits, housing benefit, and the NHS. The disconnect between these actions and the government's rhetoric is staggering.

The party of privatisation, corporate cronyism, and the 1% has been complicit in these policies, and the media has been complicit too. The BBC, in particular, has been a mouthpiece for Conservative spin. As a former BBC journalist, I understand the power of spin and how it can shape public opinion.

In conclusion, the Tories are not an alternative to Labour; they are the party that stands for austerity. As the Labour Party, we have always opposed austerity. Our position has remained consistent: we will not stand idly by while the working class suffers.

As I reflect on my over a decade-long career in technical recruiting for start-ups and companies in the technology landscape, I've come to realize that the most common mistake job seekers make is assuming that being a "good" candidate is innate. This assumption is far from the truth. What's crucial is being selective about the skills and characteristics that align with the job requirements.

In my experience, the key to success lies in the process. When I first started out, I believed that having strong back-office skills and the ability to deliver results quickly was enough to secure a job as a software engineer. However, this approach ignored the underlying process.

To be effective, we need to define the company culture, values, and goals. We must also consider the hiring manager's needs and the candidate's fit with the company and specific work requirements.

If we don't have a clear process, we can rely on observable traits, such as excellent interview skills, which include articulating answers, asking insightful questions, and proposing innovative solutions.

As a recruiter, I look for candidates who possess the following traits:

* Technical fit with the company culture, product, and business
* Ability to deliver results and provide value to the team
* Strong understanding of the product and its potential impact
* Leadership skills and marketability
* Passion and ability to sell their solution

When evaluating candidates, I consider two key aspects: being a good listener and being a skilled interviewer. As a listener, I aim to understand the candidate's perspective and determine whether their skills align with the company's values. As an interviewer, I ask questions that help the candidate showcase their problem-solving skills, such as:

* What do you see as the biggest problem you'll be solving?
* What would you do if you didn't have to build these solutions?
* How can we apply what you'll be building to achieve our business objectives?

By getting these questions out of the way early, we can focus on the candidate's strengths and what they can bring to the company.

Through my experience, I've learned that it's essential to show up, work hard, and deliver results. This approach has allowed me to build strong relationships with my colleagues and achieve success in my career.

Researchers at MIT have developed an innovative algorithm that leverages deep neural networks to predict the next card in a Shogi deck with remarkable accuracy. By analyzing the current card position and applying a unique weighting system, the algorithm achieves an average error rate of less than 10%.

The system's neural network learns to predict the next card by analyzing card positions and comparing them to a reference dataset. The algorithm assigns weights to each card based on the number of cards in the deck, focusing on packs with multiple cards. When a pack contains two cards with an in-set and an out-set, the algorithm prioritizes that pack. As more cards are available, the weight of individual cards increases. In a 32-card deck, a pack may contain 28 cards, with 16 unique cards. A weight of 1 indicates the player is likely to receive that card. Weights in some pack pairs are stronger than others, helping to predict whether a particular card will be played.

However, the algorithm's performance is not perfect. Players may hold cards that don't match the deck, and the algorithm is less accurate in high-dimensional situations or when faced with identical cards. The system also becomes sensitive to card positions already played.

The neural network operates by analyzing card probabilities, such as whether a card is currently out or not, or whether any cards in a pack will be out. It then decides whether to keep or discard the card.

To achieve this, the researchers divided their training data into thousands of small subsets, multiplying each by a matrix factor. They added the current cards to the matrix and multiplied by the size and position of the cards. The algorithm then predicts the next card based on the analysis of the training data, divided into subsets based on the number of cards in the deck.

The algorithm also determines weights within each subset, ensuring the weight factors sum to 1. It then multiplies the matrices to produce a single weight matrix for each subset. The system decides which subset to choose based on the current cards, and multiplies the weights matrix with the current cards to calculate the average result.

The algorithm takes the difference between the average weights and the sum of squared weights to determine the final weight for each subset. The result is a matrix and vector used to make the decision about whether to keep or discard a card.

The weight matrix's performance is sensitive to input connections. If inputs are not well connected, the weight matrix may be too small to distinguish between options. However, with enough computation power and data, the weight matrix can be made detailed enough to make an accurate decision.

A coalition of organizations supporting undocumented immigrants has filed a brief with the Supreme Court, urging the justices to revisit a 2014 decision that limited the scope of the "Dream Act," a 2013 immigration bill. The coalition argues that the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals' ruling was flawed and that the law unconstitutionally allows for "chain migration," which grants automatic citizenship to the parents of American citizens.

The brief, filed on behalf of the ACLU of Louisiana, the Center for American Progress Action Fund, the National Immigration Law Center, and ImmigrationWorks, asserts that the Supreme Court's own case law contradicts the 5th Circuit's decision. The coalition claims that the law does not permit foreign citizens to sponsor their parents for citizenship and does not grant automatic citizenship to their parents who have lived in the United States since childhood.

The brief will be sent to justices and Supreme Court clerks ahead of oral arguments in the case, where lawyers will argue that the decision was incorrect and that federal immigration law as it applies to families is unconstitutional.

"It's a new Supreme Court, and it's clear that the courts will play a significant role in shaping immigration policy," said Karen Tumlin, a staff attorney at the National Immigration Law Center. "The fact that this case is being considered is a significant development."

The "Dream Act" is part of a broader effort to provide legal status to undocumented immigrants who came to the United States as children. The law was passed in 2007 and signed by President Barack Obama in 2012.

The Supreme Court is currently reviewing a case from 2014, Amicus Curiae IV, which challenged parts of the law. In a split decision, the 5th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in favor of the federal government, claiming that the law violates the Constitution's ban on "emancipating" people.

In a separate ruling, the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals also found the Obama administration's program to be legally invalid. A three-judge panel of the 5th Circuit Court of Appeals later reversed its previous decision, stating that the "Dream Act" only permits immigrants who have been given temporary asylum or have been protected from deportation under two programs.

The "Dream Act" has been a focal point in the immigration debate, with proponents arguing that it provides a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants who came to the United States as children.
