The age-old question of dog poop has puzzled many a dog lover. As a dog owner, you've likely wondered about the composition of your furry friend's intestinal tract and how it compares to your own. To delve deeper into this topic, we spoke with two experts, Dr. Chris Calabrese and Dr. Sarah Muhs, to gain a better understanding of the intricacies of canine digestion.

The experts

Dr. Chris Calabrese: The concept of dog poop has been around for centuries, with ancient civilizations and modern-day research shedding light on the subject. So, what exactly are we asking about?

Dr. Sarah Muhs: We're not asking whether dogs poop, but rather what influences the ability of a dog's intestinal tract to absorb nutrients. What is the composition of the intestine? What does dog poop and human waste have in common?

Dr. Chris Calabrese: To better understand the digestive tract, let's ask: what is a dog's digestive system, and why would we want to know its composition? As a matter of fact, if you were a dog owner, you might ask me if your dog's intestine is more like a human intestine or a brain. What would you say?

Dr. Sarah Muhs: A more interesting question might be: is there a difference in the composition of the intestinal tract between breeds and species? This question is less controversial from a scientific viewpoint. What we do know is that when we compare intestinal composition with a human sample, there is no difference, it's in the same region. It is also not clear that the presence of feces in human faeces would affect the intestines of either species. I think you can appreciate why it's so important and why we'd like to investigate it.

The dog-poop theory

As a kid, I'd often play in the backyard while grandma took the dogs outside. I'd occasionally glance at the toilet while munching grass and watching a dog poop, thinking, "Ah, I better check that out!" And that's why I asked my dad about it. He looked at me like it was gross and a waste of time, but I knew that if I asked, I wouldn't get the answer I wanted. I wanted to know how it might affect the dogs and how it could be avoided.

We had a little research project where I'd throw fecal pellets. One day, I took out a plastic bag and placed the feces in it, then watched. This is actually one of the things the dog-poop theory was about.

This is a picture I took when I realized a dog's poop had been in the bag for too long: [Image credit: David P. Woodruff]

Is there anything different about dogs' poop that would affect it in a different way than our poop? Yes, the fact that poop is more concentrated means you get more out of it. But I don't think it's something you can avoid or avoid for good.

Can dogs eat their poop too?

Dr. Sarah Muhs: Yes, they can. The composition of poop is similar to urine. So, it's true that when a dog eats, it retains all the nutrients that are there. And if that poop is stored in its system for some time, the intestines can absorb a certain level of nutrients.

In 2017, President Trump unveiled a budget blueprint, a comprehensive plan to reshape the federal government. Among his campaign promises was the elimination of the $19,000 annual grant funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, the public media arm of the Federal Communications Commission. The proposed cuts aim to boost funding for local stations and grant the FCC the authority to restrict the Corporation for Public Broadcasting's funding to public broadcasting stations in over four-fifths of the country.

This is not the first time the Corporation for Public Broadcasting has been in Trump's crosshairs. The president has repeatedly criticized public broadcasting, dubbing it "public enemy No. 1." Last January, NPR's vice president of communications explained why this label is misguided.

"The idea of public TV and radio, as well as radio stations and a public media presence, are fundamental concepts," says Vivian Schiller. "The Corporation for Public Broadcasting, an entity, has been around for nearly thirty years, serving the same purposes as when it was established."

The proposed budget is likely to disappoint Trump, as it slashes federal funding for public broadcasting by over 20 percent and allows the Corporation for Public Broadcasting to cease operations. Additionally, the budget eliminates tax credits given to the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, forcing it to pay taxes on some of its revenue.

"The idea of a centralized entity providing grants to local communities to support public broadcasting is a crucial aspect of the American idea," says Schiller. "This concept is essential to American democracy."

The President's budget also proposes a 10 percent reduction in funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. "I believe this is misguided and counterproductive," says Schiller, who joined NPR in May.

Schiller attributes the Republican budget's cuts to the House's desire to shift away from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting's subsidy formula, which ensures the agency can reach low-income and lower-population areas. "They're essentially redirecting funds from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting to programs that can only support specific income ranges and population demographics, funded by tax credits," says Schiller.

In celebration of a significant milestone, the University of Michigan community is commemorating the 150th anniversary of the founding of Sigma Phi Epsilon (SxE), a pioneering women's sports club. This remarkable achievement dates back to February 9, 1888, when Samuel Gompers, then president of the University's College of Engineering, responded to a request from the women's athletics director to establish an athletic club rivaling the men's teams.

At the time, the University offered only a limited range of sports, and the establishment of a rival team was seen as a hindrance to women's basketball players. Gompers chose the name SxE in honor of the engineering schools and William M. Robinson, a former engineering student who made significant contributions to improving the physical safety of women.

Initially, the club faced skepticism from the community, but it continued to grow and evolve over the years. In the early years of the 20th century, SxE began to flourish, with membership numbers increasing to over 1,500 women in various clubs. The organization played a vital role in promoting women's athletics at the University, and its impact can still be felt today.

Throughout the 1970s and 1980s, the number of women participating in University athletic teams grew significantly, with the addition of new programs such as women's swim team in 1983. By the 1990s and 2000s, the number of members had grown to over 55,000.

Susan Brown-Simmons, a former SxE member and current Associate Director of Women's Athletics Operations, reflects on the significance of the organization: "SxE was more than just a sports club – it was a haven for women. It provided a space for us to come together, support each other, and pursue our passions."

In recognition of its contributions, SxE was officially recognized by the University in 2001. Members of the organization had the opportunity to choose how they wanted to be represented, and in 2002, they decided to revert to their original name, Sigma Phi Epsilon.

Today, SxE continues to play an important role in the University's culture, promoting women's athletics and providing a sense of community and camaraderie for its members.

Chapter XV: Battle of the Somme

On July 16, 1916, the German army launched a significant offensive on the Western front, commencing at approximately 10 a.m. Initially, they made progress, but their momentum was soon hampered by the subpar quality of the trenches and the numerous trenches constructed by the French and British forces over the years. As one British soldier quipped, "Trenches are the worst thing in the world. But they haven't been around that long."

Confronted with the daunting task of fighting on two fronts against a single enemy, the German army made a series of critical errors that ultimately undermined their chances of success:

The German army failed to establish solid defensive positions, instead opting for a makeshift defense, which forced them to retreat, leaving behind no trenches or strongpoints. This allowed the French and British to reoccupy their trenches and expand their defenses, securing more ground.

The German army failed to concentrate their troops, scattering their forces across the front without intention of regrouping, thereby allowing the French and British to organize their forces quickly and move swiftly against the German trenches.

The German army failed to adequately prepare their troops, with Commander Albert Kesselring being overly cautious and failing to take necessary steps to prepare his troops before the war. Kesselring attempted to utilize British artillery and inferior German equipment, resulting in dismal performance on both fronts.

The German army failed to capitalize on their significant numerical superiority. By 1916, the Germans outnumbered the British and French by several times on the Western front and almost four times on the Eastern front.

The German army struggled to contend with the limited strength of the French and British forces, which were roughly 6,000 men each, a tiny fraction of the German army's total strength.

The German army faced difficulties adapting to the ever-changing and unpredictable terrain on the Western front. When they attempted to capture a narrow ridge overlooking Ypres on July 16, 1916, they were forced to retreat. The Germans had assembled a significant force on one front facing the French and British on the opposite side of the ridge, but the French and British were able to reorganize their forces and repel the German forces, thanks to their advantage in time, terrain, and troop speed.

The German army was slow to recognize the need for proper trench organization and tactics. For over a month, the French and British constructed an effective trench network with British artillery support. By 1915, trench warfare in Europe had reached a stalemate, and the Germans were unable to effectively exploit their numerical superiority and mass formations to attack the trench systems.

The German army had a poor understanding of the nature of war. After losing both Meuse-Argonne and the Somme, the Germans found themselves fighting a war that was far more complex than they had anticipated:

The Western front of the Great War was the largest and most complex of any at the outbreak of the First World War, spanning over 2 million square miles, stretching from the North to the Baltic, and from the North Sea to the Baltic. Its theaters of combat crossed nine foreign nations and five continents, spanning an area extending from the Black Sea to the Himalayas. At its core, the Western front was a struggle to establish a "Greater Europe."

Bluefin Tuna Crisis: A Growing Concern

A disturbing trend has emerged in the Atlantic bluefin tuna fishery off Australia's coast. Researchers have detected a concerning level of parasites in over 10% of the caught fish, which can cause liver inflammation.

The parasites, known as hookworms, are linked to fishing methods that involve long lines or nets. Satellite tracking has shown the spread of the parasites across the Pacific, including the Atlantic, and along the southern coasts of Australia, New Guinea, and Fiji.

The study, conducted by the University of New South Wales and the National Sea University in France, highlights the need for improved fishing practices to mitigate the spread of the parasites. The European Union has already banned bluefin catches from the Mediterranean and other areas, citing concerns over a potential health crisis.

New Zealand, a frequent bluefin fishing port, is not at risk of catching the parasites. However, more than 60% of bluefin tuna caught off NSW, Western Australia, Queensland, and Victoria were infected. The researchers are monitoring the distribution of hookworms and planning to expand their study to Pacific bluefin tuna, which is commercially fished in Australia.

We're excited to share some updates on the upcoming 0.13 Alpha release. As usual, the new features have presented some unexpected challenges. The most notable change is the introduction of.fgd files, which have replaced traditional game files, and the addition of auto-save functionality for your game data. A brief aside, but worth mentioning.

For those unfamiliar with.fgd files, here's a concise overview. From the official release notes:

.fgd files are standalone game files that can be compiled for multiple games and platforms.

During the compilation process, they're compressed using gzip-compatible formats.

These compressed binaries boast a remarkable balance of small file size and rich data content, resulting in a significantly smaller game.

The name may have sparked confusion, as it bears some resemblance to encryption tools. However, the underlying process is distinct from traditional encryption methods.

To simplify the explanation,.fgd files employ two primary compression techniques:

1. Dictionary compression, where a set of possible strings is condensed into a numerical representation, reducing the file size.

2. File compression, which incorporates various techniques, such as Huffman coding and LZ77, aimed at compressing files for faster loading into RAM.

For those new to gaming,.fgd files typically resemble.exe files paired with.ogg or.mp3 audio files. Due to their rapid compression and decompression,.fgd files won't require copying when uploaded to game servers.

Giant Panda: Unraveling the Enigma of Online Censorship

Giant Panda, a groundbreaking app for iPhone and iPad, empowers users and publishers to scrutinize online content for breaches of free expression and social justice, including Facebook and Twitter censorship.

Developed by a University of California, San Diego professor of communication and information ethics, the app is now available on Apple's App Store. The App Store team's blog post highlights the significance of their research on censorship, revealing "intriguing findings" when analyzing 20.6 million Facebook messages. They discovered that the number of removed messages due to community standards mirrored the number of illegal pages monitored by Twitter and those banned from blogs.

"When examining online censorship, it's essential to consider the offline context as well," the team emphasizes. "Our analysis revealed that almost 100 million messages contained content removed for violating community standards, often due to complaints taken offline. This underscores the delicate balance between free speech and its limitations."

The social psychology of Internet censorship is further illuminated by comparing the most censored messages with those that garnered the most likes, favorites, and shares.

"The most censored Facebook messages attracted more complaints and likes, which is unsurprising, given the audience. However, the most censored messages rarely featured complaints about specific issues. Only 2 percent of posters claimed their article would violate the hate speech policy, while 25 percent claimed a quote violated the threatening speech policy. In contrast, within specific Facebook groups, complaints about specific articles were more common, with 24 percent complaining and 20 percent liking and sharing a news article quote."

The impact of censorship on those who write the most censored messages remains unclear. While it's not a direct ban, the message may still spread and serve as a warning to others who might follow a similar path.

A recent investigation by a global team of seismologists suggests that the California earthquake had a profound impact on Japan, resulting in a devastating tsunami that struck the country just hours later. The disaster claimed the lives of at least 17 people and led to the meltdown of the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant.

Researchers publishing their findings in the journal Nature Geoscience concluded that the magnitude 8.9 earthquake that hit Japan on March 11, 2011, and the subsequent tsunami were likely connected.

Dr. Eric Berger, a prominent expert from the University of Washington's School of Oceanography, noted that the tsunami that hit Japan was likely severe, but not as intense as previously reported. However, he declined to comment on the methodology behind the study's conclusions.

The tsunami, which measured over 10 meters high, struck Japan as the country was preparing to celebrate the successful opening of the nuclear plant on April 1, 2011. The resulting floodwaters damaged the plant, triggering a meltdown that left 11,200 people dead or missing and forced the evacuation of 40,000 others.

Some experts have speculated that the power plant was not fully repaired before the earthquake, making it vulnerable to the tsunami-induced meltdown. However, this theory remains unverified.

According to Berger's research, the earthquake and tsunami were likely triggered by the immense stress generated by the power plant's earthquake. This stress, in turn, triggered the nuclear meltdown.

Berger emphasized that the earthquake had a profound impact, not only causing the tsunami but also affecting Japanese society as a whole.

One of Berger's co-authors, David Sutterley, from the U.S. Geological Society's Pacific Northwest Earthquake Center in Seattle, noted that their research was the first to demonstrate a direct correlation between earthquakes and tsunamis using Japan's earthquake sensor data.

Although their study did not determine whether the tsunami triggered the quake or vice versa, Sutterley believes that the correlation between the two events must have been triggered by some underlying factor.

"We aimed to provide the most comprehensive analysis possible for this paper, leaving the question unanswered for further investigation," he said.

I'm using the hack to bypass a glitch and get my computer to render the game correctly. In the past, I used an Xbox 360 controller for this, but I no longer have one, so I've developed a workaround.

I've discovered that there are three methods of emulating a game: using the Windows API, the Direct Input method, and the DirectSound API.

The Direct Input method involves drawing the graphic data the game expects on the display using DirectInput. This method handles the X and Y axis and allows you to tell the game to render the graphics you desire. The Direct Input method using DSL/HDMI is the simplest, but it requires special drivers for the motherboard.

The DirectSound API is the most complex, as it runs as part of the DirectSound driver program. It handles calculations and input and uses sound drivers. You can use DirectX9 and DirectX10 libraries to handle audio, and there's an option in the DxDiag menu that allows you to specify what's being rendered on the display and audio data.

I created my DirectSound and DXGI drivers and was able to get the DirectSound API working. I was looking for the SDL driver, which handles most of the input from the game. Unfortunately, I didn't realize that SDL is a Windows application. I eventually found DirectSOUND, a cross-platform implementation of the DirectSound API that works on Windows, Linux, and OS X. I installed it and created a simple script to get it running in Windows. This allowed me to bypass the need for motherboard drivers and simply point it to the DirectSound API. Now, I still have some issues, but switching back to the DirectInput API allows me to control the game using only mouse input, which enables me to play the game and view the output.

Let me provide an exemplary illustration of how well that phrase is understood.

This is how you convey a message through a campaign. Now, you might expect the Democrats to excel at using the "kiss backside" line, but you would be mistaken. A novel research initiative exploring the potential health implications of a natural gas boom is underway at the University of California, San Diego's research facility. According to a statement released by the research team, the "Hydraulic Fracturing, Health Impacts, and Environmental Sustainability" project is currently in its inaugural phase and may lead to further research initiatives if funding is secured.

The study, led by the University of California, San Diego's Department of Earth Sciences, focuses on the potential health effects of fracturing fluids used to extract shale and petroleum reservoirs.

"Our initial study aims to elucidate the toxicological and reproductive health impacts of hydraulic fracturing from initiation to completion," the statement explains. "Our secondary level of analysis examines hydraulic fracturing and health outcomes, including research on social and environmental impacts."

Although not yet formally accepted for peer review, the project aims to determine the health effects of "fracking fluids" and investigate their environmental and human health impacts.

The research team is collaborating with a team of scientists at the University of Virginia, who also plan to continue their study on the health impacts of fracking. The two universities are part of the Ecolab Energy partnership in the U.S. Northeast, which combines the University of California, San Diego, with the University of Richmond to study the causes, effects, and solutions associated with the rapid growth of the gas industry.

The authors of the blog post, Michael DeGroote, a professor in the University of California, San Diego's Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, and Sarah Sorensen, associate professor in the Department of Earth Sciences at Virginia Tech, described their work as both basic and applied science, stating that it will begin by analyzing data from a 2009 peer-reviewed paper on hydraulic fracturing.

"Our work is merely the first step," DeGroote said in the statement. "For every paper, there are others that have not yet been published, offering new insights. It's exciting to lead this project, as it sets the stage for future collaborations with this community."

In the initial phase of the project, the researchers identified several health and environmental effects related to fracking, including increased risk of certain diseases, birth defects, birth injuries, neurological disorders, and respiratory illnesses. Although the study focused only on health impacts from fracking, the research also found higher levels of air pollutants near fracking sites compared to nearby non-fracking zones.

"It is essential to consider that these studies are preliminary and only examine health impacts related to fracking," said Ecolab executive director Michael McGovern, in the statement. "This project should raise awareness about the possible adverse health impacts of hydraulic fracturing. It clearly demonstrates that the shale gas industry, its operations, chemicals, and methods have the potential to negatively affect human health, emphasizing the importance of scientific facts."

"Our goal is to use this research to inform the public about fracking and its health impacts, as well as better understand how fracking might affect community water resources."

According to the statement, the researchers hope to continue their project for an extended period if funding is available, noting that the project is still in its early stages.

The "Hydraulic Fracturing, Health Impacts, and Environmental Sustainability" blog post is available online through the University of California, San Diego's website and the UC San Diego Research Watch project website.

The latest federal budget fails to address the glaring shortcomings in our country's management.

Conservatives might hastily point to other nations, such as the UK and Greece, where governments are grappling with rising deficits, but there's no concrete evidence to suggest Canada is in the same boat.

In fact, the Conservatives' lack of effort to rein in federal finances could ultimately cost Canada billions in future revenue.

It appears the government is unwilling to confront a fundamental issue – how can we reduce our deficits while maintaining reasonable financial health? Over the past decade and a half, the federal deficit has consistently grown, with an accumulated $100-billion debt.

Yet, the Conservatives seem reluctant to tackle this pressing issue, opting instead for minimal efforts to address it and save money. After eight years, they're even unwilling to acknowledge Canadians' growing concerns about excessive spending and demands for change.

The Harper government has invested over $120-billion in new infrastructure projects, many of which are questionable in quality or unnecessary. While Conservatives argue these projects are essential, Canadians need no reminder that they rarely create jobs or generate net economic benefits. Instead, they often result in significant cost overruns and exceed initial investment costs.

Concurrently, the government has spent billions maintaining a large fleet of aging warships, jets, trucks, and equipment. These outdated upgrades have become bloated, expensive, and inefficient over time. By keeping our aging equipment near obsolescence, the federal government is losing out on billions in annual revenue.

Given Canada's mismanaged federal finances, it doesn't make sense to continue increasing the government's debt burden.

Canada's debt has risen during this parliament, exceeding $320-billion, and is projected to reach $439-billion over the next three years, with no new funds allocated to pay down the debt. Instead, it continues to grow.

At $400-billion, Canada's federal debt-to-GDP ratio is a concerning figure. While it remains relatively within historical norms, other large countries' debt-to-GDP ratios are below 66 per cent, and Canada's is below the historical average of around 61 per cent (adjusted for population size).

Instead of cutting taxes and balancing the budget by raising taxes, as the Conservatives have planned, is there a viable plan to deliver on Canadians' demands for a smaller government, reduced federal debt, and smarter tax policy?

The reality is that our current federal finances are not under control, but rather reasonably well-managed. This is a departure from the past decade and a half, during which the government's financial problems have persisted.

While the Conservatives tout Ottawa as a model for financial management, the reality is that we have a growing deficit, and the Canadian economy is not generating sufficient prosperity for the average Canadian to enjoy a comfortable standard of living.

Rather than seeking solutions through increased government spending, there is a proven method for maintaining reasonable federal financial health: responsible fiscal management.

Fiscal management means balancing the budget not just annually, but also controlling spending for the long term – for today and for future generations.

The NDP and Canadians across the country want to live within their means and avoid taking on debt they cannot afford.

It's time for the Conservatives to wake up and stop their irresponsible spending habits.

Our hour-long conversation was the closest thing to a press event I've witnessed from a young artist in a long time.

As is often the case, a press release was issued shortly after our chat. It was a standard four-sentence statement, signed by Ilan Bluestone, which didn't reveal much new information.

Jack Ü is known for being self-aware, and our conversation reflected that. However, it took me a little while to realize that the press release was genuine.

The first two tracks from his previous album, The Love Club, have been released, but I'd like to share a sample of what they sound like.

Ilan Bluestone / Jack Ü: "Just Because"

From where I was sitting, I thought the title referred to a club anthem, but Jack Ü took a different approach. He started talking about what it means to be a friend.

Ilan Bluestone / Jack Ü: "Friends"

"When I found out who I'd be working with, it was an unusual reaction," he explained. "Coming into a situation without any prior connection, it was an interesting experience."

There's no hint about the album's sound or style, as Ilan Bluestone isn't sharing those details yet. Instead, he's focusing on creating a narrative-driven record.

"This idea popped into my head a month ago," he said. "I want to create a character who's the main character of the record." He wants to ensure his sound and story are fully developed before releasing the album.

Ilan Bluestone / Jack Ü: "I Want Your Love"

"People were asking me if I had a story," he continued. "I do, and I'm just starting. I'll take what I've learned about music and my life and make sure the music fits those ideas."

As for when we'll hear the finished product, Ilan Bluestone doesn't seem concerned. "What I've told you is enough," he said with a smile. "So I'm just going to live with it from here."

Later that night, my phone rang. I couldn't believe I had a direct line to Ilan Bluestone, but I figured it might be a great way to let him know about the upcoming feature on Noisey UK. He answered.

Ilan Bluestone: "Hello."

Noisey UK: How are you feeling?

Francesco Bernoulli, an Italian mathematician, devised an equation that has become widely recognized as the Bernoulli equation. This equation describes the tendency of a liquid to remain stationary at a fixed temperature.

In mathematical modeling, the Bernoulli equation is employed to describe the motion of particles in a gas or liquid within a laboratory setting. Additionally, it is used in fields such as medicine, physics, and thermodynamics.

The Bernoulli equation is typically expressed as:

B = C * p * A

where B represents Boltzmann's constant, C represents the universal constant of potential energy, p denotes the specific heat of the fluid, and A signifies the absolute temperature.

The term C * p * A is often referred to as the energy density of a fluid. The heat capacity or thermal mass of a substance is the amount of work required to elevate the temperature of the substance to a specific value. This work is measured in Joules.

In everyday language, the unit used to measure a chemical or physical value is the Joule, a unit of energy. By considering the universal constant of potential energy C as a unit of energy, we can conclude that a Joule represents the energy necessary to raise the potential temperature of a liquid or gas of a given substance from one temperature to another.

The energy required to elevate the temperature of a substance within a laboratory setting is measured in Joules per Celsius degree Fahrenheit of temperature increase. This is expressed in terms of energy per unit mass of substance.

Thus, the amount of energy required to elevate the temperature is equivalent to the energy density of the fluid.

Why is the Bernoulli equation significant?

The Bernoulli equation is often utilized to model the motion of a particle within a fluid or gas. The particle is assumed to possess a fixed momentum, and it is demonstrated that when p is altered such that p = 0.5, the particle will immediately return to its original state. Conversely, if p increases to 1.5, the particle will return to its original state.

When the Bernoulli equation is applied to such a particle, the particle becomes stationary.

Why is this relevant? Suppose we have a set of particles, and we set their initial positions x0, y0, z0, and w0 to be 0.2, 0.8, 2.4, and 6.8 degrees, respectively. We wish to determine how the particles will move away from the origin after applying the Bernoulli equation. In other words, what will be the maximum distance from the origin that a particle will move away from at a speed p?

The answer depends on the values of x, y, z, and w. For instance, if p = 0.5, the maximum distance is 1.9 cm. If p = 0.3, the maximum distance is 1.4 cm. If we multiply p by 1.6, the maximum distance is 2.8 cm.

We desire to utilize the equation in the laboratory setting for the same set of particles, and we know the maximum distance to be 2.8 cm, which is close to the value of 2.6 cm in the laboratory setting. Therefore, how can we conclude that the Bernoulli equation informs us of the minimum distance to go to and from a maximum value?

The challenge with calculating distance from zero is that, by definition, it is a continuous function of x, y, z, and w, for any values of x, y, z, and w. Thus, if we apply the Bernoulli equation to set a variable k such that p = 0.5, we conclude that the maximum distance is, in fact, 2.5 cm, where k is a variable. This is the problem with calculating distance from zero for any constant values of x, y, z, and w: We can arrive at any value of k through a significant amount of trial and error. But why? Why can't we simply utilize the constant c? And why do we need to know the value n of k, and what is n in general? We need to know this because if we were to know n, we can compute a formula for distance, and the formula for distance is:

d(n) = w(k)*t(n-p)*z/t(n)

where w represents the universal constant of potential energy, t denotes time, z signifies velocity along the path, p represents momentum or energy, t denotes time, k denotes the constant representing distance, and that constant is represented by the universal constant of potential energy. And that is how distance was computed when using the Bernoulli equation.

Of course, we would like to be able to compute the distance to a given location by a constant value of t. And we will have to be a little more cunning now and utilize the Bernoulli equation in a more sophisticated manner.

My partner and I embarked on a four-day escapade to Scotland, revisiting a country we've grown fond of. We've previously celebrated her birthday there, and I must say, the experience was quite enjoyable.

During our trip, we stumbled upon St. Asaph church in Dumfries, which is not your average church. Its striking architecture, with its tall, white, and red stone façade, bears a resemblance to the ancient Roman Catacombs and the Roman Colosseum. What's more, this church has been in existence since the 6th century, retaining its original structure.

What sets St. Asaph apart is its unique practice of reading the Divine Liturgy, or the Lord's Prayer. The church's patron saint, St. George, leads the prayer, which begins with:

O God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,

I believe in thee and I worship thee.

In thy name I hope to obtain eternal life.

I believe that there is no God but thee, the Lord.

I believe thou shalt grant unto me, by thine inspiration, wisdom and strength,

and by the prayers of thy saints, pardon for my sins,

and obtain mercy for my people, O Jesus Christ my Lord. Amen.

This tradition dates back to the church's founding by St. George and St. Edmund, two of the seven archbishops of Scotland. The prayers of these saints, along with those of Sts. Asaph and Dunstan, were used in the first Liturgy, the Liturgy of the Word.

What makes St. Asaph's Liturgy special is that it hasn't added anything to the Lord's Prayer. The church's congregation sings a different version, where St. George recites the Lord's Prayer. This is known as the "Great Praised One," a new form of prayer and language.

As we read the Bible aloud, St. Asaph's congregation sings a different version, in which St. George sings the Lord's Prayer. This is called the "Great Praised One," because it is a new form of prayer and new language that St. Asaph is using. It's a way of praying that is different and more intimate than what St. Asaph is used to doing.

When we read St. George's prayer, we can find the language in our life and in God that expresses love, forgiveness, and mercy. This is why we read aloud, because when we read scripture aloud, we are praying the Great Praised One. We don't have to say it aloud, because when we read it, it is recited again by God as he is speaking. When we pray the Lord's Prayer, we are praying the Great Praised One.

St. Asaph, although a Catholic saint, is not actually a Catholic. Although he may have said the Lord's Prayer in the chapel of St. Asaph, if you visit the Catholic catacombs, with its marble sarcophagi and thousands of skulls as memorials to the dead, it appears that St. Asaph would never have uttered the prayers we do today.

To be Catholic, one must be baptized into the Church. Baptism is a rite in which the laity is immersed in a stream and is then washed with wine. Baptism is not a symbolic offering of the Body of Jesus Christ.

Therefore, I'm not baptizing myself into the Church when I say the Lord's Prayer. Nor am I believing it. Baptism for Catholic children is something they would receive at an age where they would feel that they are ready for it and which, to me, seems more about belief because of my age.

We read "The Lord's Prayer" because we believe it, with all our hearts, with all our souls, believing that God wants us to come to believe it and to pray it. Our faith in the words of the Lord's Prayer is, to me, a spiritual act. Our faith in the words of the Lord's Prayer is our faith in something greater than ourselves.

Google's legal team may attempt to circumvent this issue by arguing to a judge or jury that the information is protected by confidential business and financial information. Carvin suggests that the company could argue that the information is not privileged by using its own privileged information.

In theory, a judge would need to consider whether an attorney-client relationship existed, Carvin said. However, there is no federal case law regarding whether legal discovery must include a determination from a client.

Carvin noted that the recent WikiLeaks case may have been particularly concerning because it did not violate WikiLeaks' First Amendment rights, despite the company providing some documents and being implicated in the release of confidential government files.

The company did, however, release a copy of its Transparency Report and published a brief statement explaining its involvement with WikiLeaks.

The court is likely to approach the issues raised by the Department of Justice differently, according to Carvin.

When you challenge your muscles with progressively tougher workouts, they adapt by growing stronger. This process starts when you use your muscles, causing micro-tears in the fibers. Your body responds by repairing these tears, which leads to thicker, stronger muscle fibers. This phenomenon is called muscle hypertrophy.

One way to push your muscles to the limit is by lifting weights or doing resistance exercises. When you lift, your muscles must work against the weight's resistance, forcing them to grow stronger. You can also use your own body weight as resistance by doing push-ups, squats, or other bodyweight exercises.

Another approach is high-intensity interval training (HIIT), which involves short, intense bursts of exercise followed by periods of rest. HIIT can stimulate muscle growth by increasing oxygen and nutrient demand in your muscles, making them stronger and more efficient.

It's crucial to remember that your muscles need time to recover and rebuild after a workout. After exercising, your muscles need a chance to repair and rebuild, so ensure you give them adequate rest between sessions.

I recently discovered the most scenic road cycling route in Alberta, starting from Nederland and stretching approximately 9.5 kilometers through picturesque fields on the North Shore of the Lake of the Woods. This route, known as the Rondo-Kapp, offers breathtaking views and a chance to refuel with a snack and coffee break. As you ride, you'll notice the terrain shifts from rolling hills to snow-covered landscapes, with the Rocky Mountains looming in the distance.

The North Shore is a hidden gem, with numerous cycling paths and trails waiting to be explored. In the winter, the area transforms into a winter wonderland, with temperatures dipping to around -20°C. If you're looking for a unique experience, take a stroll along the shores of Lake Nipigon, where the scenery becomes a miniature forest on sunny days.

For those seeking a more leisurely ride, I recommend starting in Nederland and turning right onto Wabamun, then heading north. The North Saskatchewan River offers a short, scenic detour, but be prepared for a moderate hike to the next location.

As you continue north, you'll cross the Alberta Rocky Mountains, where the scenery becomes even more dramatic. Take a moment to appreciate the wildlife, including deer, elk, and moose. Be sure to cross the River of Fowl, a historic bridge built in 1909, and admire the 'Big Rock' statue.

The ride culminates at the end of the first bridge, where you'll find a volunteer organization, A.R.R.K.S., offering directions and assistance. From here, follow the paths to the top of the climb, where you'll find more sculptures and a stunning view.

For a different perspective, try turning left onto the Alberta Canadian National Railway tracks and following them for about 3.5 kilometers. Take in the scenery and snap a few photos before continuing on. Alternatively, start in Nederland and follow Highway 5, turning right onto 7C and left onto 7D, which will take you through the city of Nederland and eventually to Jasper.

Whichever route you choose, be sure to stop and appreciate the beauty of the North Shore and the Lake of the Woods.

Our surveillance activities are guided by two fundamental principles. First, we must pursue communications that may violate the law. Second, we must do so only after an individual or entity has been shown to be outside the US, where privacy protections are stronger.

The concept of "mansplaining" and "dead white men" is often misunderstood by those who claim to be fighting for equality. In our society, it's common to assume someone's gender without explicitly being told, which can lead to confusion and miscommunication. Some individuals, regardless of their gender identity, may struggle with feeling pressure to conform to traditional gender roles.

The expectation that men should be the ones to "get things done" while women should focus on domestic duties is still prevalent. However, this outdated notion neglects the fact that many people, regardless of gender, can excel in various roles. For instance, I have a boss I don't particularly care for, and I often work from home. While some might accuse me of "mansplaining," I simply need to fulfill my professional obligations.

The criticism of "mansplaining" often stems from the misconception that someone who disagrees with another's opinion is somehow oppressive. This creates a false dichotomy, where individuals are forced to either explain their viewpoint or be accused of "mansplaining." I believe there are a few issues with this argument; first, it's unclear what the end goal of "mansplaining" is. Why must someone explain their opinion, and what if the other person refuses to listen? Should they simply be told to "shut up"?

Another issue is that the person accused of "mansplaining" doesn't feel oppressed; if they did, they wouldn't engage in the behavior. In many cases, men are accused of "mansplaining" because they simply don't understand the argument.

So, why do men often engage in "mansplaining"? Because they're expected to, which is one of the main reasons why many women think men don't like them and get annoyed with them: we're expected to make decisions on their behalf. Men don't like making decisions for others and tend to be less verbal about it than women. Feminism doesn't have a problem with men making decisions for others; they do it all the time, so why can't we tolerate their dislike of being told what to do?

There's another aspect of "mansplaining" that's often overlooked – it has nothing to do with the person being "splained" to. When I'm "splained" to, it's usually by someone I know and like. If I'm "splained" to by someone I don't know, it's much more difficult to explain without coming across as condescending. I believe when feminists make this claim, they're actually saying something like, "If you're really confused about why they said'mansplained,' then you need to learn why people say it when they don't like your arguments and stop being such a pain." But that's unfair.

So, what is a "mansplainer"? Is it someone who says women should pay more tax? Is it someone who thinks all feminists are stupid? No, it's someone who is told exactly what to do when they don't know how to explain themselves to a woman. Men still engage in this behavior in our society, and it's very common for us to talk about how we're being "mansplained."

The recent passage of the UK's anti-terrorism and security bill has left many in the journalism community bewildered. According to a study conducted by the BBC, nearly one in ten individuals arrested under this legislation remain at large two years after their initial arrest.

The report highlights the concerning implications of this law, which will enable the monitoring of nearly half the UK population in the future. Professor Peter Watt, Director of the University of East London's Intelligence and Security Centre, has voiced his disapproval, stating that this law is a clear violation of human rights and demonstrates a lack of respect for the rule of law and the police.

The bill was enacted in response to three terror attacks in the UK, which were traced back to the UK's intelligence services. The legislation allows security agencies to monitor internet, phone, email, and social media use, as well as hold internet usage records for up to 12 months. It also permits the bulk interception of communications and allows for the extension of "snooping" beyond the UK.

Of those arrested under the law, nearly half were released within two years, while another quarter remained at large after a year. A further 20% were arrested again and released. Professor Watt noted that over a third of those arrested are still under continuous official surveillance and will be liable to surveillance at the end of the period.

Many experts are puzzled as to why such legislation was passed, given its lack of justification. Dr. Kevin De Bruyn-Kerkhof of the University of Surrey stated, "If the purpose was to catch terrorists, it failed, and if the purpose was to monitor individuals, it has done so in the most intrusive way possible, without public support or democratic sanction."

Professors Robert Jay Lifton and Peter Watt both expressed concerns about the law's potential for abuse and its impact on free association and expression. Lifton questioned the use of power and suggested that the law will not be effective in stopping terrorism.

The report was released ahead of the British intelligence sharing arrangement with the US, which will allow information about internet activity by UK citizens to be shared with US authorities. The report concluded that British spying is in direct defiance of the UK's Human Rights Act.

According to the Department of Culture Media and Sport, over 40% of the UK population will be monitored under the new law. The department stated that the bill will allow GCHQ to request personal information from telecommunications companies and internet service providers as part of "pre-crime" and "preventative" operations.

In the wake of the bill's passage, UK Prime Minister David Cameron emphasized his government's commitment to fighting terrorism.

In this study, we aimed to investigate the brainstem's role in the behavioral effects of ethanol. To achieve this, we used a novel paradigm involving the medial forebrain bundle, which has been previously used to study ethanol's behavioral effects. Rats were administered an acute dose of ethanol and then tested for behavioral changes in two tasks: locomotor latency and choice reaction time. Our results showed that ethanol decreased locomotor latency and increased choice reaction time, with a greater effect on the ventrolateral preoptic nucleus compared to the medial forebrain bundle or striatum.

The study's findings highlight the importance of considering the brainstem's role in ethanol's behavioral effects. To overcome the limitations of previous behavioral studies, we used an animal model without a ventral striatum. This allowed us to isolate the brainstem's effects and gain a better understanding of ethanol's mechanisms of action.

Our study contributes to the growing body of research on ethanol's effects on brain function. Recent studies have shown that ethanol can have direct and indirect effects on the brain, including changes to the mesolimbic dopamine system and prefrontal cortex. Chronic ethanol exposure has also been shown to decrease striatal dopamine D2 receptors, which can be reversed by acute or prolonged ethanol administration.

Ethanol is a widely consumed substance that can have significant negative effects on the central nervous system. These effects can include memory loss, attentional control impairment, and motor coordination impairment. Additionally, ethanol can impair motivation and inhibit dopaminergic neurotransmission, leading to changes in behavior such as increased locomotor activity and risk-taking behavior.

We used male Sprague–Dawley rats for our study, which were obtained from Charles River Laboratories and acclimated for one week. The rats were then trained using an initial 3-day period of continuous water drinking followed by 5 days of intermittent water restriction. They were then allowed to drink water ad libitum and received an acute injection of ethanol. The next day, they were tested for behavioral changes.

In the late 1970s, a small group of researchers at the National Institutes of Health conducted a study on the long-term health effects of atrazine on laboratory rats. The results showed a significant increase in birth defects, particularly congenital malformations. The researchers concluded that atrazine is a suspected human carcinogen. A subsequent study found an increase in birth defects and abnormalities in the reproductive tract, thyroid, and sperm parameters. However, the most severe effects were observed in rats receiving the highest doses of atrazine.

A study published in Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry in 2011 found a strong correlation between atrazine exposure and amphibian deformities. The study showed that high-dose exposure caused deformities and atrazine resulted in an average of one deformity per 10,000 amphibians. The most widely cited estimate was 100 deformities per 10,000 amphibians.

The EPA took several years to respond to concerns about atrazine's toxicity. The agency's investigation found consistent effects of atrazine in fish and the environment, including deformities in frogs, salamanders, and toads. Atrazine has been detected in well water and human drinking water in concentrations over 1 part per billion.

In the early 1980s, atrazine was found in drinking water in a small number of Wisconsin communities. In 1991, the EPA announced a moratorium on the use of atrazine in drinking water due to concerns for public health. The agency conducted research comparing atrazine exposure to that of other common herbicides and concluded that atrazine was not more toxic than 2,4-D or dicamba. The EPA did not impose restrictions on atrazine use and instead implemented a voluntary reduction in its use, which was completed by 2003.

Despite atrazine being registered in 13 states and used in 17, it is not registered in California, Texas, or Washington. The EPA has not taken action on California's registration renewal application since 2016. California became the first state to require registration of atrazine with the EPA after passing a law in 2007 that requires registration for new herbicides sold to distributors. Other states have passed similar legislation.

Atrazine use in farm settings has increased significantly in recent years, with some states experiencing high concentrations. The EPA estimates that atrazine concentrations range from 0.9 to 6.4 parts per billion in water supplies and soils in the United States. However, university studies have shown lower concentrations, ranging from 0.09 to 0.18 parts per billion.

The EPA estimates that atrazine is a probable human carcinogen. In 1992, the agency declared atrazine a probable human carcinogen, indicating that public concern is warranted if they drink water. The EPA is not currently conducting new studies on atrazine. If the agency decides to take action, it could potentially ban atrazine use by all farmers and users, but would need more evidence of its carcinogenic effects.

In 1997, the EPA conducted a comprehensive review of atrazine's safety, concluding that there is evidence of human health effects. The review also found atrazine not to be at higher risk than dicamba. The EPA did not find a statistically significant increase in birth defects in the study, but noted that the study lacked adequate statistics and should be interpreted carefully.

In 2011, the EPA concluded that no additional scientific evidence on atrazine's safety was needed. The agency concluded that atrazine is not a probable human carcinogen, but is aware of human epidemiological studies suggesting the herbicide may have carcinogenic effects.

Retirement planning is a crucial aspect of securing your financial future. Two popular options for saving are Roth IRAs and 401(k)s. Both offer unique benefits, and the best choice for you will depend on your individual circumstances. A Roth IRA is a personal savings account that allows you to contribute after-tax dollars, which means you've already paid taxes on the money. This account grows tax-free, and withdrawals are tax-free in retirement. In contrast, a 401(k) is an employer-sponsored plan that allows you to contribute pre-tax dollars, reducing your taxable income. The money grows tax-free, but you'll pay taxes when you withdraw it in retirement. When deciding between the two, consider your expected tax bracket in retirement. If you think you'll be in a higher bracket, a Roth IRA might be the better choice. If you expect a lower bracket, a 401(k) could be the way to go. Additionally, consider whether your employer offers a 401(k) match, which can be a significant perk. By contributing enough to take advantage of the match, you're essentially receiving free money to help you save for retirement.

A recent study published by the University of Virginia reveals that the US economy experienced a decline in manufacturing jobs between 1999 and 2014. Despite this, manufacturing still played a significant role in job creation, accounting for half of all new entrants in the labor market during this period.

Researchers Mark Perry from the American Enterprise Institute and David Autor from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology analyzed quarterly employment changes and aggregate employment statistics between the third quarter of 1999 and the fourth quarter of 2014. They utilized a model to investigate whether changes in industry employment numbers were driven by productivity increases or market forces.

A prevailing assumption about the relationship between manufacturing and economic growth is that manufacturing is a robust job creator. Indeed, between 1995 and 2013, manufacturing generated 6.4 million net new jobs, resulting in an additional $3.6 trillion in spending. It was the largest contributor to job growth during this period, providing 5.2 million jobs and generating another $3.9 trillion in economic activity.

However, if these gains had not been offset by losses in manufacturing spending in the final three years of the period, estimates suggest that manufacturing would have generated around 2.5 and 1.9 million jobs. By the end of 2013, when jobs were severely impacted by the Great Recession, manufacturing accounted for 3.1 million more jobs than it did in 1994, but also created 1.9 million fewer jobs. These net losses equaled the loss of 2.2 million jobs from the entire period and marked the largest decline in manufacturing jobs since 1945.

The authors conclude that the manufacturing slowdown and its effects on various industries can be attributed to changes in factors like productivity and globalization, but also note that the manufacturing industry's role as a job creator decreased during the period, largely due to the shift towards service creation and globalization.

The authors acknowledge that their findings do not prove that U.S. manufacturing companies are not job creators, but suggest that the manufacturing sector is the primary cause of job losses during the period.

"It is also noteworthy that the manufacturing sector lost significantly more jobs than all other domestic industries combined over the past quarter century," they write. "For example, the decline in manufacturing employment and spending between 1997 and 2013 was roughly comparable in magnitude to the entire decline in the nation's capital stock between 1967 and 2011."

In this period, capital stock decreased from $15 trillion to $13 trillion in just 15 years, while manufacturing employment increased by over 7 million. The authors conclude that while the manufacturing industry may be declining as a major job creator, it still provides substantial employment to Americans.

"The loss of manufacturing employment over the past few decades has been significant, and it has contributed substantially to the national decline in employment," they write. "For example, between 1997 and 2013, the US lost an additional 11.4 million industry jobs, or almost 4.5 percent of net total US employment. Between 1997 and 2013, this number was roughly twice as large as the national decline in capital stock or the loss of manufacturing employment between 1997-2000 and 2001 – almost a two-thirds drop. As the nation's capital stock declined and manufacturing employment declined, the number of workers employed by manufacturers, in general, declined as well."

Objective:

To investigate the impact of physical activity and macronutrient composition on long-term weight management in a high-carbohydrate, moderate-fat diet.

Methodology:

A 21-month dietary and exercise intervention was conducted with 15 obese adolescents, aged 12-15, recruited from a university-affiliated obesity treatment program. Participants were randomly assigned to either a high-carbohydrate, moderate-fat diet (35% protein, 18% carbohydrate, 50% fat, and 12% fiber) or a control diet (30% carbohydrate, 20% fat, and 15% fiber).

Data Collection:

Energy, macronutrient, and fat intake, as well as physical activity levels, were assessed at eight time points: baseline, 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, and 21 months.

Findings:

Weight loss varied significantly throughout the study, with an average loss of 12% (range 2-13%). No significant differences were observed between the two trial arms in terms of percentage of body fat, percent change from baseline, or changes between baseline and each 1-month-point.

Conclusion:

Dietary manipulation may not be an effective strategy for weight loss, although it may help reduce postprandial overeating and increase satiety, which is crucial for weight maintenance. Exercise is an essential component of a weight-loss regimen for children and adolescents, but it does not appear to improve short-term outcomes when compared to a low-fat diet.

Murder is a complex issue that can't be reduced to a single cause. While it's true that some individuals who lack empathy may engage in violent behavior, it's crucial to recognize that not all murders are committed by people without empathy. Similarly, not everyone who lacks empathy is a murderer.

Empathy refers to the capacity to comprehend and resonate with the emotions of others. When individuals struggle to understand the feelings and perspectives of others, they may act in ways that harm or disregard others' well-being. In extreme cases, this lack of empathy can manifest as violent or aggressive behavior.

There are numerous reasons why someone may struggle with empathy, including genetic predispositions, neurological or developmental issues, and traumatic experiences. It's also essential to acknowledge that some individuals may exhibit a lack of empathy in specific situations or with certain people, but not in others.

Other factors, such as mental health issues, substance abuse, and personal or societal problems, can also contribute to instances of murder. It's vital to consider the intricate web of factors that may lead to such tragic events.

Linux and UNIX share a common heritage as operating systems, but each has evolved distinct characteristics. The defining feature of an operating system is its ability to oversee the allocation of computer resources and manage hardware and software interactions.

Both Linux and UNIX operate on the principle of open-source software, where the underlying code is accessible and modifiable by the community. This shared foundation has resulted in similarities in command syntax and file organization, allowing both platforms to support a broad range of applications and server deployments.

Despite these commonalities, Linux and UNIX exhibit notable differences. Linux has emerged as a contemporary operating system, commonly found on personal computers and servers. In contrast, UNIX originated as a mainframe-focused system and, although still in use, is largely confined to high-performance computing environments and server applications.

The core distinction between Linux and UNIX lies in their respective positions within the technological landscape: Linux represents a modern, widely adopted platform, whereas UNIX embodies an older, specialized system with a more niche appeal.

According to Wai-tau, the driver had attempted to pull her into his vehicle, but instead of taking her to her destination, he asked to use another taxi and then stopped near a shop to steal money from the till. When she protested, he pushed her and threatened to have his wife find her a taxi.

Wai-tau alleged the groping took place in Mong Kok, a central area of the city, but the prosecution claimed it occurred in the evening, just before midnight.

The prosecution stated that Wai-tau had a motive to harass and sexually assault the victim due to jealousy, and that the victim was stressed due to recent employment termination and family difficulties. The prosecution also mentioned that the stolen money could have been used to buy food to calm the victim down.

The trial judge found that Wai-tau's actions were deliberate and intended to harass the victim. As a result, Wai-tau was ordered to pay the victim HK$5,600 in compensation, HK$100,000 in prosecution costs, and HK$150,000 in medical costs. Additionally, she was banned from driving for three months.

Not all helmets are created equal. Some block 90% of collisions, while others may be less effective. Shared-faced helmets, for instance, are highly effective, with 90% success rate in most situations. However, most helmets fall short, with only 30-50% effectiveness. There's a significant variation within helmets, making some a game-changer and others barely effective.

So, how much do helmets cost? You can find a basic helmet for under $60, but these often lack advanced features. Top-of-the-line helmets, on the other hand, can be quite pricey. What else can you do to stay safe?

Before hitting the road, take a moment to check your surroundings. Every cyclist is responsible for being aware of their environment. Additionally, wear a helmet when riding in areas with heavy traffic. Visibility is key, and being seen by other road users can help avoid accidents.

Investors can utilize statistical analysis to gauge market trends by examining the dynamics of price and volume patterns. This approach is based on the notion that market fluctuations can be predicted by analyzing charts and other statistical tools. For instance, some popular statistical indicators for evaluating mutual fund net asset values (NAVs) include:

* Trend smoothing: By averaging a security's price over a specific timeframe, investors can identify trends and patterns. This method can help filter out short-term fluctuations and reveal longer-term market movements.
* Volatility detection: Bollinger bands are a type of statistical indicator that combines a moving average with upper and lower bands. These bands can be used to identify potential breakouts and changes in market volatility.
* Momentum analysis: The relative strength index (RSI) is a momentum indicator that compares the magnitude of a security's recent gains to its recent losses. This helps determine whether a security is overbought or oversold.
* Trend confirmation: The moving average convergence divergence (MACD) is a trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages of a security's price. A positive MACD can be a bullish sign, while a negative MACD indicates a bearish trend.

These are just a few examples of the statistical indicators that can be used to analyze mutual fund NAIVs. It's essential to recognize that statistical analysis is just one method of evaluating securities and should be used in conjunction with fundamental analysis and other investment strategies.

To configure virtual machine storage, you'll need to set up a storage volume. A storage volume provides a virtual machine with the necessary storage and power resources. By default, a storage volume is created for each virtual machine when it's created with the Hyper-V feature.

Virtual machines can use one storage volume, which is automatically created when the virtual machine is started from an image or installation disc. Storage volumes can be configured to provide various features, including failover, volume isolation, compression, and recovery.

Storage Clusters

Storage clusters can be added to a storage pool or storage pool. Storage clusters can be configured to automatically take over a storage pool if it becomes disconnected. Additionally, storage clusters can be added manually at any time using PowerShell in Server Manager.

When running a storage pool with multiple physical disk drives, you can add only one storage cluster. Windows Server 2016 supports up to 10 storage clusters per storage pool.

Running Storage Spaces

To run Storage Spaces, enable the Virtual Machine with Storage Spaces feature on the VM and then connect the virtual disk to the virtual machine. When Virtual Machine Manager runs for the first time, it assigns the storage pool the same storage as the virtual machine configuration. The default storage pool is used for storage.

Configuring Storage Spaces

Storage Spaces works like a volume but provides high-availability, failover, and other performance-enhancing features. To create a storage volume or cluster, you must create a storage pool containing at least one disk drive. You can add more physical disks to the storage pool and add other virtual disks to the pool.

Using Multiple Storage Volumes

You can use more than one storage volume, and each volume can use different physical disk drives. For example, you can create three different storage volumes using two logical network adapters.

Creating a Storage Volume

To create a storage volume, create a storage pool and add a disk drive to each pool for virtual machines. Add a second disk drive to the remaining storage in the pool. After virtual machines are added to the storage pool and storage is configured, the storage volumes are made available as shared resources that other virtual machines can attach to.

Storage Volumes as I/O Devices

A storage volume is an I/O device on a hypervisor or guest operating system. It's separate from the virtual machine storage volume and is used by the virtual machine to perform tasks such as mounting the disk drive, reading data, and writing data. With a storage volume, you can define what virtual machine can do with an I/O device.

In the early 19th century, the American colonies operated as a semi-autonomous entity within the British Empire. This unique arrangement allowed the colonies to maintain a degree of independence while still being subject to British imperial policies. As a result, the colonies' citizens enjoyed limited rights, laws, and government regulations that were often influenced by British norms. A pressing issue in American politics was taxation, as the British government imposed various taxes to fund its operations and institutions, whereas the colonies lacked representation in these matters.

The colonists had limited say in the taxation system, except in some cases where local authorities imposed taxes. This led to a situation where the colonists received fewer benefits than the British, despite being subject to similar taxes.

Land Ownership

Prior to the American Revolution, British law prohibited the sale or rental of land between British citizens. In 1777, Parliament passed the Colonial Tenement Act, establishing a monopoly that allowed local residents to own exclusive rights to the land they worked. To work their land, colonists required a license from the government and British authorities, which could only be issued by the Crown. This was designed to prevent colonists from selling their land and becoming economically independent of London. As a result, colonists often sold or rented their land at inflated prices, making little profit from their income. This lack of incentive led to a decline in business competitiveness, causing many businesses to fail.

Personal Property Taxes

The colonists' main source of income was tax revenue from their employers, landlords, and those providing goods and services to the colony. The British government collected income tax and duties on property sales, as well as taxes on various factors like money and credit. These taxes and duties were combined with customs duties, creating "interim duties" that were collected on imported goods. As a result, most goods in the colonies, particularly land, were subject to taxation. For example, land owned by the British Crown and under cultivation was subject to customs duties, while colonists raised their own crops. Customs duties could be paid by consumers and were collected by the government as a levy on the colonists' income.

Real Estate Taxes

The tax on real estate in the colonies was similar to that on personal property. For instance, the British Crown owned the lands in the colonies through the "public domain." Colonels and other colonial officials had no legal right to these lands and could not sell them. They were considered "private property," although the Crown owned them. Property owners in the colonies were obligated to submit to the control of the Crown, which meant that a merchant or manufacturer could not operate without British approval.

In this system, British policy aimed to reduce the number of colonists living on their land, as the country was controlled by the colonists, not the British Crown. This led to an erosion of the colony's independence. A landowner might not realize that the land belonged to the colony, and instead, it was merely a matter of the Crown using force to collect taxes from the colonists until the revolution. When the revolution occurred, the colonists had limited recourse other than to take up arms against their colonial overlords, and when the British were defeated, the colonists lost a crucial advantage over the British. Taxes and duties were also used to fund the government's own expenditures, and some tax revenue was collected by law.

The colonies, like the British government, imposed taxes and levied tariffs or duties to fund their own expenditures. Taxation was a fundamental aspect of British economic policy, and many historians have called it "the oldest and most enduring feature of [the British] financial system."

Because the colonists controlled their own wealth and property, taxes were a primary means for the Crown to maintain control over the colonies. Given the significance of taxation in all economic activity, it is logical that the colonists created their own local systems of taxation to protect their interests and privileges. For example, merchants in a colony might insist that goods carried by settlers were subject to tariffs. In return, merchants could pay for imported goods more effectively and cheaply. Taxes helped merchants compete with foreign traders and maintain their control of the British market.

The American College of Cardiology (ACC) recently shared findings from a global study examining the effects of exercise on heart health, particularly in individuals at risk of heart failure (HF). HF occurs when the heart's pumping function is impaired due to atherosclerotic plaques narrowing the aorta.

The ACC, a prominent heart-health organization, published preliminary results indicating that exercise could reduce the incidence of HF by 8% in at-risk populations.

The study analyzed data from over 300,000 individuals across 28 countries, with approximately 12,500 participants followed up on for around 5.3 years.

Dr. Michael T. Moritz, Chair of the ACC's Cardiology Section and lead author of the study, highlighted the significance of the International Exercise Training Prospective Cohort Study (ITPS) report. He noted that the study's findings are comparable to those for other conditions, such as cancer, stroke, diabetes, obesity, asthma, and congestive heart failure.

The study suggests that regular exercise, including at least 200 minutes of aerobic activity per week, may benefit individuals at high risk of cardiovascular disease and heart failure. However, Dr. Moritz emphasized that a one-size-fits-all approach is not recommended, as individual responses to exercise may vary.

The study did not investigate the impact of increased exercise duration on cardiovascular disease and HF risk. Dr. Moritz expressed confidence that future research will build upon these findings.

A previous study in the Netherlands reported modest benefits of high-intensity exercise (HIIT) on cardiovascular disease, but was suspended due to serious complications.

Dr. Moritz noted that numerous large randomized controlled trials have demonstrated some improvement in heart failure with regular aerobic exercise. The American College of Cardiology will continue to investigate the benefits of exercise for specific subgroups of people with heart failure.

What's the Catch?

The studies' diverse age groups and diseases make it challenging to determine individual effects of exercise on heart conditions. However, they suggest a strong link between regular exercise and heart failure. While exercise may not be a panacea, it can still be beneficial for those with cardiovascular disease or heart failure.

The New York Times published an article by John Markoff, which left me underwhelmed. Markoff suggests that since Donald Trump's election, Democrats have finally found a path to political power. Steven Greenhouse, a New York Times politics reporter, believes a "new political era" is dawning, with Republicans in control of both Congress and the White House.

Greenhouse warns that the path to legislative success is now "extremely slim." Democrats hold the House, Senate, and White House, but a filibuster-proof majority is unlikely. They must also contend with President Trump, who has shown little interest in governing and could be unpredictable in Washington come January.

For a month, Greenhouse and Markoff have been warning that Democratic prospects are bleaker than they've been in decades. Their predictions of a Trump presidency were dire enough that Hillary Clinton wrote an op-ed in The New York Times last year, predicting it might be "too late for a turnaround."

Markoff believes the political system Democrats have dominated for nearly four decades may be ending. After the election, Democrats who thought they could use Trump's election to gain a more radical direction felt vindicated. Then Trump won, and his first 100 days have delivered shocks to a president who seemed poised to restore stability.

I've covered politics long enough to know it's premature to worry about the next four years. It'll take time to determine if Trump is capable of being more than a non-entity. Markoff is correct: "it may be too late for a turnaround." But that won't stop Democrats from thinking they had the election to lose.

This article highlights the need for Democrats to change their identity to survive. They must abandon identity politics, stop alienating working-class voters, and stop acting like a party that's "too late for a turnaround." Democrats can't continue to play the "we don't believe you" card and expect to win.

One reason Trump is so damaging to Democrats is that they've spent too long playing identity politics. Identity politics is about winning a particular group of voters. What makes it hard to win working-class voters? It's simple: by playing identity politics, you make the working class seem like a third-party group. Instead of talking to Democrats with their own history and issues, you're talking to people you don't fundamentally agree with.

But identity politics can't be avoided. It's a basic feature of the Democratic Party, like Trump's bigotry and homophobia. It has to be discussed.

The Democrats are the only party playing identity politics in a counterproductive way. They're trying to push Trump's hateful agenda through as an identity election while pretending it's about their own issues. This is a clear signal that they don't believe in their own party.

So how can Democrats win voters? The answer is something they won't admit: they can't win over Trump voters no matter what. They can't give them any reason to vote for Democrats. They can't claim to care about people who feel rejected by the party they've defined themselves with. They can't use policies that would put the party in line with their policies, because that would be a bad reason to vote for Democrats.

Republicans can easily run on their own identity politics and win again in two or three cycles. Democrats can't.
