A groundbreaking study has uncovered a striking disparity in drug use patterns across the UK. A comprehensive survey of 3,000 individuals revealed that England has the highest rates of illicit drug use, while Scotland has the lowest.

Researchers scrutinized data from the 2011 UK Drug Use and Misuse Survey, finding that both men and women in England are significantly more likely to have engaged in illicit drug use compared to their Scottish counterparts. Those of Welsh ethnicity, on the other hand, were found to be the least likely to have used drugs.

The researchers noted that, although Scotland does not officially track drug use, it is likely that the country's drug use rates are higher than England's.

"This finding may suggest that Scotland's relatively low levels of drug use are an important driver of higher levels of drug misuse among its ethnic minority communities," the researchers posited.

The data used in the study was collected as part of the National Survey of Drug Use and Health, which involves in-depth interviews with adults aged 15 and over, as well as a household-based questionnaire that assesses drug use habits. The survey was conducted in England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

"The sample is representative of the entire population, providing a comprehensive snapshot of drug use, drug-related harm, and social attitudes towards drug use," said lead researcher Sarah-Jane Pearce of the University of Liverpool's Institute of Social and Economic Research.

The study, published in the journal Lancet Psychiatry, revealed that people aged 15-64 in England are least likely to use illicit drugs, compared to those in Wales and Northern Ireland. However, among English individuals aged 16-24, the likelihood of drug use was also found to be lower compared to older age groups.

Notably, males in full-time education were most likely to have engaged in illicit drug use. The study's findings were consistent with those of the 2011 Scottish Mental Health Survey.

While the study provides valuable insights, the researchers acknowledged that the data may not be exhaustive, due to differences in response rates and survey methods. In England, participants were required to report drug use confidentially, which may have led to some individuals failing to disclose their drug use. The study was unable to determine the frequency of drug use.

The authors concluded that, despite the study's limitations, the findings may be useful in exploring the factors contributing to higher levels of illicit drug use among ethnic minority communities.

When the rain returns, the sun will shine again, but it won't bring the same warmth as the previous day. The second possibility is that the phrase is a modern variant of 'The sun will come out tomorrow', which is an expression of optimism or the idea that things will get better by the second day. The addition of 'thank you very much' might be a nod to this phrase.

Interestingly, the phrase 'thank you very much' as a formal sentence ending appears in a poem by Charles Simonyi, published in 1939 and 1941. This could be due to the author's background as a lawyer, as lawyers often use formal language.

A third possible source of the phrase is the US song 'The sun never set on the Pacific', recorded in 1935. The song's lyrics include the lines 'The sun never set today' and 'There's a new day of sunshine today'.

It's worth noting that the phrase 'The sun shone today' might have different connotations in different cultures. In the UK, for example, it's less common to use the phrase 'jeux' or'même' to express gratitude, as it's more commonly used in informal speech.

I've got a confession to make: I didn't exactly fall head over heels for the new Tomb Raider game. While it had its moments, it was lacking in a significant way. The world was rich and vibrant, and the voice acting was top-notch, particularly from the actress who brought Lara Croft to life. However, Tomb Raider: Legend, in my opinion, is a misstep. It's a far cry from the classic games that fans of the series hold dear.

I've never been a huge fan of the main character, and this game didn't change my mind. While it's not as bad as some of the earlier installments, it's still not great. The series has struggled to find its footing over the years, and this game is no exception.

One of the biggest changes in this game is the lack of tombs. It's a significant shift in tone, and it's hard not to feel a sense of disappointment when you realize that the game isn't what you expected. The story is also dramatically different, focusing more on Lara's personal struggles rather than her adventures.

The problem is that the game's nostalgia factor is overplayed. You're supposed to feel sorry for Lara, but instead, she comes across as selfish and lazy. The entire game is a reminder of her shortcomings, and it's hard to muster up any sympathy for her.

The graphics are still impressive, and the gameplay is mostly solid, but it's just not the same. The story is disjointed and lacks the excitement of earlier games. Instead of exploring the world and climbing structures, Lara is stuck on a few repetitive missions with limited choices.

Lara's character arc is all about her perceived inadequacies, which is disappointing given the series' attempts to flesh her out in previous games. For most of the game, she's just a victim of circumstance and a survivor of her brother's murder. There's not much depth to her character beyond that.

The gameplay is also affected by Lara's reduced mobility. She's no longer as agile or quick as she once was, which makes the game feel easier and less exciting. The controls are also harder to learn, which adds to the frustration.

There are a few moments where the game shines, particularly in the boss fights. The fight against the crocodile is a highlight, and the second boss fight is reminiscent of classic movies. However, these moments are few and far between.

The game has two major problems: a lack of originality and a story that's just not compelling. Both combine to make the game a disappointment. I was hoping for something more from the next Tomb Raider game – a more interesting character, more unique locations to explore, and a story that could take the adventure further.

So, you're curious about refrigerators, huh? Well, let me break it down for you. Inside the fridge, there's this clever liquid that circulates through a network of pipes. As it flows through these tubes, it picks up heat from the interior of the fridge. This heat absorption cools the air inside, which keeps your grub fresh and ready to devour.

But how does this liquid get cold in the first place? Enter the compressor, a nifty device that squeezes the liquid, making it hot. This hot liquid then travels to the condenser coils, located on the back of the fridge. These coils dump the heat into the surrounding air, cooling the liquid down in the process.

As the liquid cools, it transforms into a gas, which then passes through an expansion valve, allowing it to chill even further. Finally, the cooled liquid makes its way back into the fridge's tubes, where it starts the cycle anew, sopping up more heat and releasing it outside.

This continuous cycle of cooling and heating keeps the fridge at the temperature you've set. Got any questions about how refrigerators work? Fire away!

In the realm of historical enigmas, one mystery stands out: the tale of America's ascension to global leadership in defense and law enforcement. It's as if a subtle misstep in the natural chemical processes led early American engineers to employ an unconventional approach, substituting boronium for traditional catalysts.

The narrative begins in 1765, when Sir Humphry Davy, a renowned English scientist, presented his groundbreaking invention to the Royal Society of London's board for review. Davy's colleague had informed him that the society was considering patenting gunpowder. Following the board's approval, Davy received a cryptic message and telegram from an anonymous individual, claiming the society was no longer worthy of recognition. The note did not disclose the sender's identity or motives.

According to Davy's autobiography, "The Principles of Chemistry and Optics," the mysterious figure declared that the society had reached the end of its usefulness, required no funding, and had lost all its members. The individual claimed responsibility for ensuring the United States would never be granted a patent for gunpowder. Davy recalled the unknown person as an elderly acquaintance who had been friends with him for twenty years, with two sons and a modest means.

This anecdote has led to speculation about the potential for a single individual to spark the first explosion in human history. The "one person" theory is plausible, considering the case of J.E.D. McDonald, an engineer who died in 1837 while attempting to develop a high-powered gas-powered rocket for military aircraft testing.

Another theory suggests that the enigmatic figure could be Davy himself. It is possible that Davy's colleague had informed him about the imminent development of new metallurgy, prompting him to delay his invention until old age.

This theory, along with others proposing that Davy discovered the society's intentions and decided to sabotage it, has been debated for nearly 150 years. In 1955, British historian and chemist Sir Robert Watson-Watt conducted a three-year study, visiting the National Archives in London. He found that the society's first gunpowder patent, issued on December 17, 1762, included the statement: "This article may be manufactured by the said John Humphry Davy, who has a patent granted by the Royal Society of London." This revelation discredited Davy's claim to be the inventor of gunpowder.

A more convincing explanation, initially unassuming, emerged: In a July 17, 1761 meeting of the Committee of Correspondence, Davy discussed U.S. patent applications with fellow scientist Robert Bunsen. Bunsen referred to Davy as the "most extraordinary person we have ever met," advising him to patent new metallurgy, as someone else might do so if he did not. Bunsen's subsequent meeting, on September 17, 1766, just after Davy received the mysterious telegram, showed that he agreed to proceed with Davy's metallurgy patent, with the caveat that Davy could try again if his plan failed.

The evidence supporting and refuting Davy's involvement in gunpowder's invention is overwhelming. In July 1782, Thomas Harriot presented a paper to the Royal Society, claiming that a group of French scientists had invented gunpowder, while a group of English scientists, including Davy, had developed the same chemical.

Harriot's "proof" consisted of the ingredients required to make gunpowder, as outlined in a 1764 patent for an invention known as Deutz-Fahrzeug (Dupont).

The notion that China is a counterpoint to the United States is a compelling one, given its relentless pursuit of global influence. Over the past several decades, China has made significant inroads in South Asia and Africa, and its efforts to dominate the Asia Pacific region continue unabated. The driving force behind this expansion is, of course, China's ability to offer a cheaper, more competitive alternative to traditional global powers.

In this piece, I aim to argue that China's influence is not worth the cost, and that the United States cannot afford to perpetuate its relationship with China. China's aggressive pursuit of resources and markets has significant implications for the global economy and international relations.

China's efforts to tap into Africa's natural resources are often touted as a panacea for the continent's development challenges. However, history has shown that China's approach is often exploitative, with little regard for the well-being of local populations. For example, China's failed attempt to extract diamonds in Sierra Leone serves as a cautionary tale.

The real question is whether China's actions are driven by a genuine desire to benefit Africa or whether they are simply a means to an end – a way to extract resources and further its own interests. In my opinion, China's strategy is designed to use cheap resources to gain a competitive advantage over other world powers.

China's rise to global prominence is undoubtedly impressive, but its long-term sustainability is far from guaranteed. History has shown that every nation that rises to the top eventually faces a decline in its competitive advantage. I conducted an informal study of three periods in world power competition and found that there have been three instances in which the United States did not compete with China, opting instead to focus on other priorities.

In the pre-industrial era, the United States was too wealthy to worry about competing with China. During the industrial revolution after WWII, the United States had a surplus of resources and could afford to ignore the competition. It was only during the modern era that the United States felt compelled to compete with China.

In conclusion, China's influence is not worth the cost, and the United States must reevaluate its relationship with China. China's actions are driven by a desire to extract resources and further its own interests, rather than a genuine desire to benefit Africa or the global community.

Thrun's presentation at the 2017 Association for Computing Machinery International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction and Simulation was titled "The Human Platform." He posited that our technological obsessions with platforms are already integral to our culture and infrastructure, and will continue to play a crucial role in the future.

Thrun predicts that in the near future, mobile platforms will serve as a full-fledged replacement for devices like PCs or smartphones.

Think of mobile as the platform itself. A mobile platform will enable the creation of devices like computers, telephones, and smart appliances, and they will be capable of performing tasks beyond their current capabilities.

However, as mobile platforms interact with one another, they can become an essential component of the system, surpassing even the main device. Thrun notes that smartphones are the mobile platforms of today, but this will quickly change as people begin to live without smartphones, and their lives become increasingly complex.

So, just as the PC was an essential part of our computer system when it emerged in the 80s, and its capabilities are now equivalent to the personal computer, mobile platforms will become an essential part of our software system as our computing systems become increasingly digital.

But how can we create an interface for a mobile platform?

According to Thrun, we can look to the first human-made interface: the keyboard.

Thrun demonstrated how the keyboard, the first human-made interface, has been essential to the development of the digital information superhighway. When it comes to mobile platforms, the key idea is that when you think of a digital interface, you should think of it as an artificial keyboard. "In the twilight of his life, Walt Whitman uttered his final words: 'I am the one with the courage to stand now.' As he prepared to embark on a historic journey to Richmond, Virginia, he was driven by a sense of purpose and conviction. On May 23, 1862, he led a band of Union marchers in a bold protest against the scourge of slavery, an event that would be remembered as the 'Battle of New Orleans.'

The city of New Orleans, once a prized territory, had been reclaimed by the United States after being annexed by Mexico. The conflict that had ravaged the nation was a complex web of issues, with the South seceding over concerns about land and economic security, while the North fought to preserve the Union and end the institution of slavery.

The war had left a deep scar, with the Confederacy emerging as the sole remaining slave nation in America. Slaves enjoyed legal rights and privileges, but the reality was far from equal. The Confederate constitution, shaped by the interests of slave owners, enshrined the notion that slavery was a fundamental aspect of Southern society.

As the nation teetered on the brink of division, the secessionists argued that the Confederacy was founded on the principle that blacks should not be granted citizenship. The fear of racial integration and the desire to maintain a white-dominated society drove the Confederate leaders to enact laws that prohibited blacks from participating in the political life of the United States.

These Jim Crow laws, passed in the North and South, prohibited blacks from owning property, starting businesses, or serving in government positions. The laws were designed to maintain a system of racial segregation and prevent blacks from exercising their basic rights as citizens.

In the aftermath of the war, the nation was left to grapple with the legacy of slavery and the divisions it had created. The words of Walt Whitman, spoken in the midst of chaos and conflict, served as a poignant reminder of the power of courage and conviction in the face of adversity."

The classification system has three primary categories. The first two, designated as "standard" and "conventional," are the default settings and are present in all packages. The third category, labeled "enhanced," was introduced in the 1.0 release and will be primarily utilized in the 1.2.x version. The following packages feature this classification system:

For convenience, the "standard" categories are divided into three subcategories. The first subcategory is used directly by this package, the second is used by all other packages, and the third is used by this package.

Regarding the remaining categories:

The first category is not utilized. It serves as a convenience only and is also employed in the standard and enhanced categories.

The second category is not utilized. It serves as a convenience only and is also employed in the standard and enhanced categories. The terms "category-1" and "category-2" are synonymous.

The term "category-3" is synonymous with "enhanced."

For example, the standard category can be utilized as follows:

>>> from sympy import Standard
class Standard:
    pass
>>> standard = Standard()
>>> standard.a = 3
>>> standard.b = 7
>>> standard.c = 5
>>> standard.a = 6
>>> Standard()  # The standard category has no attributes.
>>> Standard()  # The standard category has no attributes.
>>> from sympy import Standard2
>>> standard2 = Standard2(10)  # Standard2.class_instance(standard)
>>> standard2  # The standard category has no attributes.
>>> standard2.b = 7
>>> standard2  # The standard category has no attributes.

Class definitions may possess attributes, such as (class) attributes for attributes on the class's instance.

For a class declaration, this is simply an index. For a class instance, this is the "class property."

Class instances are "global."

For example, the attributes of a class object are the "instance" objects:

>>> from sympy.abc import ABC
>>> ABC.object = 42
>>> ABC.object.a = 1
>>> ABC.object.b = 43
>>> A = ABC(object)
>>> A.object.a = 43
>>> class A:
    pass
>>> a = A()
>>> a  # The instance has no attributes.
>>> a.object.a = 43
>>> a.object.b = 5

Class instances do not inherit attributes from the class. This includes class attributes, attributes that are part of the class's class attributes when it is a standard or enhanced category, and attributes that are attributes on a class instance itself.

class A:
    pass
>>> r = A()
>>> r  # The instance has no attributes.
>>> r.object.a  # An attribute from instance class (A)
>>> r.object.b = None
>>> r.object.c = None
>>> r.c.class_instance([])
>>> r  # The instance has no attributes.
>>> r.object.a = 2
>>> r.object.b = 5

This functionality is applicable to standard and enhanced categories.

For "heavyweight" categories, objects do not inherit attributes from the class. This is because the weight of a class is determined by its instances (which are simply instances of the class).

class A:
    pass
>>> a = A()
>>> a  # The instance has no attributes.
>>> a2 = A()
>>> a2  # The instance has no attributes.
>>> a  # The instance has no attributes.

There is no "instance" attribute on a standard class, only attributes from classes.

class T:
    pass
>>> class D:
    pass
>>> d = D()
>>> d.object.class_instance(T)  # The standard class has no attributes.
>>> D()  # The standard class has no attributes.
>>> d.object.a = 1
>>> d.object.b = None

For "lightweight" categories, there is one attribute for class instances:

>>> class A(object):
    pass
>>> a = A()
>>> a[0] = 2
>>> a.object.a  # There is an instance attribute for A (which corresponds to a)
>>> A()  # There is an instance attribute for A (which corresponds to a)

The attribute is called object, and represents the class (instance) object.

class A:
    pass
>>> class C:
    pass
>>> class D:
    pass
>>> D.object.class_instance([C])  # Same as D.class_instance(C.object)
>>> D()  # Similar to D.class_instance(A.object)

For a standard class and a class instance, the object attribute has no value.

class A:
    pass

Rape: A pressing human rights issue. The United Nations Human Rights Watch emphasizes the need for the American people to acknowledge and address the cycle of violence against women in the US. This requires a commitment to understanding the complexities surrounding rape, says HRW. There are several key factors contributing to this issue. Firstly, according to the US Department of Justice, women aged 15-59 are three times more likely to be victims of rape than women of other ages. Women aged 18-24 are four times more likely to be victims of rape, as stated by the US Bureau of Justice Statistics. This disparity can be attributed to various societal and cultural factors.

Secondly, rape statistics are often underreported and undercounted. Misconceptions about rape, such as the notion that women often lie about their experiences or that there are "legitimate" and "illegitimate" victims, hinder efforts to prevent and address rape. Additionally, the lack of coordination among government agencies and NGOs hampers the dissemination of best practices for preventing rape.

Lastly, the public remains largely unaware of the prevalence and impact of rape. To combat this, government agencies, NGOs, and women's groups must work together to promote education and awareness about rape prevention and support services for victims.

The UN Population Fund emphasizes the importance of prioritizing women's sexual and reproductive rights, as well as access to family planning services. Women's groups in the US face challenges in promoting reproductive health issues due to a lack of political clout and resources.

US women's groups have made progress in forming support groups and providing resources for victims of sexual assault, but many of these groups lack formalized leadership structures and training. Additionally, many rape groups in the US lack official leadership structures and direct experience with rape victims, making it difficult to identify and support survivors.

The US government has responded to this issue by allocating a small percentage of its budget to gender equality programs. However, more needs to be done to address the systemic issues surrounding rape and promote a culture of respect and equality for women.

For users with Android 4.4, the process is similar, but the "Always wake up" mode must be enabled first. This feature can be useful, but it's essential to note that it may not provide enough battery life for extended periods.

By following these steps, you can keep your Android device awake during flights and stay productive or entertained.

The proposal includes the abolition of the post of Lord Advocate and the introduction of a new role with expanded powers.

The party also called for a duty on elected politicians to act with absolute impartiality when dealing with human rights cases, and for the new Lord Advocate to have the power to direct the prosecution of individuals in serious cases.

Dugdale emphasized the need for a new statute of rights, particularly for young people, and pledged to work towards its implementation as quickly as possible.

The New Hampshire Constitution outlines the power to tax, stating that it does not confer inherent authority to collect taxes or take and hold property. This principle has guided attempts to regulate property use or possession. The "exaction for public property" is a direct tax on the taxable class, similar to municipal taxes assessed based on property value.

Historically, New Hampshire has employed indirect levies on property, with no direct or indirect tax on interest. The legislature must levy a proportionate part of taxable property to fund public property use. The direct or indirect method of taxation is a tax on the property owner, but the key issue is whether the property is subject to the tax.

The general rule is that taxing bodies must levy taxes on property owners. The legislature aims to enforce the "natural right" of owners to their property, but this doctrine has limitations. The property itself must be liable to taxation, regardless of exemptions. The legislature's discretion determines exemptions.

In New Hampshire's history, exemptions have been granted in certain cases, allowing property owners to retain their assets. However, this is not a universal practice. The majority rule of taxation applies to all types of taxation, without distinguishing between specific types.

The policy of exempting certain property from taxation can have unintended consequences. It may lead to exempting all land or property with a mortgage, limiting the state's ability to direct taxation methods or amounts.

New research reveals no correlation between smoking and a decreased risk of breast cancer

Psychological distress is a significant risk factor for developing breast cancer, but there is limited evidence linking smoking to a reduced risk of cancer. A recent study confirms this finding.

The study also discovered no association between breast cancer and a history of mental health issues such as anxiety or depression. Women with a greater number of mental health concerns had a lower lifetime risk of breast cancer.

Researchers from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) School of Medicine and the American Cancer Society analyzed data from nearly 50,000 women diagnosed with breast cancer between 1998 and 2010. They also examined information related to emotional well-being and social connections.

The findings indicate that women with mental health issues had more than double the risk of developing breast cancer at a given age compared to those without. This association persisted even after controlling for other risk factors known to increase breast cancer risk. Additionally, the study found no evidence that social connections reduced the risk of developing breast cancer.

The research is published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Dr. Matthew D. Katz, lead author of the study and professor of epidemiology at UCSF, stated: "Although mental health issues are part of the breast cancer risk profile, we need to understand why a woman with a breast cancer diagnosis develops mental health problems, increasing her breast cancer risk, and how to intervene to prevent mental health issues."

The authors emphasize that they are not suggesting that individuals with mental illnesses who develop breast cancer should completely stop smoking - rather, they should be encouraged to explore alternative methods for quitting.

A diagnostic examination known as an oral glucose tolerance test, or OGTT, is employed to identify the presence of type 2 diabetes or prediabetic conditions by assessing the body's capacity to metabolize a predetermined quantity of glucose. This procedure involves measuring the concentration of glucose in the bloodstream prior to and two hours subsequent to the consumption of a distinct, sugar-rich solution. The OGTT serves as a verification tool for diagnosing diabetes when symptoms are present or blood sugar levels are elevated, as well as a means of detecting prediabetic conditions before they manifest as symptoms.

The pharaoh Khufu, who commissioned the project, likely intended it as his final resting place. However, the pyramid's significance extended beyond its original purpose, serving as a symbol of power and a gateway to the afterlife.

The pyramid's design is a marvel of engineering, with its five levels and four major chambers. The largest chamber, the Great Hall, contains four stone chambers that were said to be inhabited by the gods. The walls and chambers are made of limestone, with some blocks weighing as much as 100 tons.

The pyramid's exterior is characterized by its smooth limestone surface, which was polished to create a gleaming effect. The four faces of the pyramid are aligned almost perfectly with the four cardinal directions, a testament to the ancient Egyptians' mastery of astronomy and mathematics.

The pyramid's interior is a labyrinth of passageways and chambers, with the King's Chamber serving as the final resting place of the pharaoh. The Queen's Chamber, located in the East Pyramid, is believed to have housed the pharaoh's wife, while the King's Chamber in the West Pyramid is thought to be the burial chamber.

Despite its age, the Great Pyramid remains an awe-inspiring structure, with its sheer scale and precision engineering making it a wonder of the ancient world. Its construction is a testament to the ingenuity and skill of the ancient Egyptians, who were able to create a monument that has endured for millennia.

Research indicates that while suicide rates among men and women do differ, the gap is relatively small. Women are slightly less likely to die by suicide, with a disparity of roughly half.

Studies suggest that men are more prone to suicide, with a higher likelihood of self-inflicted harm. In fact, men are twice as likely to die by suicide as women.

A recent study published in JAMA Psychiatry analyzed data from five major surveys between 1997 and 2012. The findings revealed that the link between suicide and gender is most pronounced among young adults, with older individuals showing no significant difference in risk.

The study's lead author, Mark Bellis, a professor of epidemiology at Harvard Medical School, notes that while men are more likely to commit suicide, this disparity is less pronounced compared to women.

Interestingly, suicide rates have been rising among both men and women in recent years. However, the study's findings do not suggest a clear cause-and-effect relationship between the uptick in male suicides and the overall increase in suicide rates.

Bellis notes that the study's results make sense, given the significant difference in suicide risk between men and women. He also suggests that older individuals may experience a greater increase in suicide rates due to unique factors.

While suicide rates are highest among young people, the study found no difference in risk between males and females across different age groups. There is no age group where men have a lower suicide rate compared to women.

The study's author encourages those considering suicide to reach out to the national suicide prevention hotline and 24-hour crisis center, Samaritans.

In conclusion, while there are differences in suicide rates between men and women, the gap is relatively small, and the issue affects both genders.

A high-speed train project linking Beijing, China, with Tokyo's eastern edge has begun construction, amidst ongoing high-speed rail initiatives in the US and Canada. (Source: Reuters)

By Mieke Van Houtte and Paul Eckert

Tokyo - On a clear summer afternoon, the train whizzed across a vast expanse of green fields surrounding a hill in Tokyo's Shinagawa ward, a trendy area with a rich history of immigration.

The train's interior was a soothing dark blue, with tinted black windows offering a glimpse of the green landscape bathed in the soft, warm glow of sunset.

A Chinese tourist, capturing the moment with his smartphone, shared his experience with a Japanese friend, recalling the driver's warm welcome at Tamao Station. "It's wonderful to meet someone who speaks Japanese," he said.

This typical Saturday afternoon commute in a city with a growing foreign workforce, expected to expand further, is driven by Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's administration, promoting maglev high-speed train links as a vital component for revitalizing the economy.

With nearly 300 professionals working on maglev development and testing at Tamao, officials aim to operationalize the trains before the end of the decade.

However, the train encountered by the Chinese tourist differs significantly from Japan's iconic, futuristic concept, and the current experimental phase.

Japan's first maglev, launched in the late 1970s, was a prototype, and its sleek design is gradually being phased out.

Prime Minister Abe has announced plans to establish a maglev service connecting Tokyo and Osaka every three minutes by 2020, but the project has been put on hold due to its high cost.

Germany is also exploring maglev technology, aiming to build a tunnel under the Alps. In an interview, Abe praised Japan's maglev achievements, while critics view them as a means to move cars.

Japan is investing in various transportation technologies, including maglev.

In the US, Japan, and France, politicians are pushing rail projects plagued by costs and delays. Maglev technology, allowing trains to travel faster and higher, may offer a promising alternative.

The technology is being tested in the US, Canada, and China, where it is already in use.

High-speed rail is the fastest and most convenient form of transportation, reducing travel time by up to 70 percent. In a nation where travel time is often lengthy, fast trains can accelerate travel and cut pollution.

Despite Japan's success, experts argue it cannot afford to wait for other countries to catch up.

"We are now at a stage where we can build maglev technology that people can see and are excited about," said John F. Donohue, a senior fellow and Japan program director for The Century Foundation. "If Japan were to lead the way in high-speed rail, it would put pressure on other countries."

Some maglev projects are still in the planning stages. In the past decade, Japan has opened 15 lines and plans to build over 100 new ones, involving a combination of high-speed trains, low-cost commuter rail, and high-speed passenger rail.

"Building maglevs sounds easy, but it's not," said Kazuhiro Shima, head of Tokai Railway Co., operating the Tokyo Maglev. "Maglevs have not been used in Japan's subway system before due to smoothness issues and long standing times."

The Iran-Contra affair was a tumultuous episode in US political history that unfolded during the 1980s. Dubbed after two concurrent illicit activities, the scandal revolved around the clandestine sale of weapons to Iran, a nation with which the US had a contentious relationship, and the diversion of the proceeds to support the Contras, a rebel group fighting against the Nicaraguan government. The Boland Amendment, a US law, explicitly prohibited the use of government funds to aid the Contras, yet certain individuals within the US government, including Oliver North, defied this restriction. Upon discovery, the affair precipitated a massive political scandal, resulting in the punishment of numerous government officials, including imprisonment and job loss. The repercussions of the Iran-Contra affair were far-reaching, eroding public trust in government and its leaders, as well as prompting widespread scrutiny of the US's foreign policies during that period.

It's been a while since I first heard about "Avatar 2" being touted as "Hollywood's first fully 3D picture ever." I wasn't surprised, given the film's impressive box office numbers. Now that the movie is out and expected to dominate the domestic box office, I thought I'd take a closer look.

Initially, I was struck by the significant changes in the story. In the original "Avatar," the focus was on a human mission to explore a planet for seven years. In "Avatar 2," the setting shifted to a more stylized environment, with a film being made about the creatures that inhabit the planet. We then visited a desert planet and space, where humans interacted with an alien race with a unique perspective on humanity.

The core idea remained the same: humans experiencing a new planet, while the native species interacted with humans in a different way. This concept is crucial to understanding "Avatar 2."

The new world introduced in "Avatar 2" is more exciting and less earth-bound than the original. When we reached space, an interesting development occurred: humans became bored and preoccupied with having sex in space, leading to an accident. This is a common theme in science fiction.

I won't delve into the plot details, as there's already plenty of information available online. The story is fascinating and unexpected, coming from a franchise with less fanfare than "Avatar."

Regarding the story, "Avatar 2" is no longer just about humans trying to have sex with animals. It's more mature, grounded, and less frightening. The film has become more "adult" and "Hollywood" in many ways, with more emphasis on human characters.

The summer leading up to the release of "Avatar 2" saw a lot of discussion about the similarities and differences between the "Avatar" and "Star Wars" franchises. I wondered how "Avatar 2" could avoid being influenced by these comparisons. It's clear that "Avatar" had some success, and many people were relieved to see the franchise end. However, there's a large fan base for "Avatar 2," which appealed to a broader range of people.

The story in "Avatar 2" wasn't drastically different from what came before. The first "Avatar" was set between "Avatar" and "The Last Airbender," where scientists studied animal minds and researched a new technology. The ending featured a short cut, where the Avatar was shown in space, with humans obsessed with having sex with the species to help them survive.

However, "Avatar" was more grounded and less Hollywood. It focused on a group of humans, mainly Na'vi, who had to find their way in a new world and learn to survive. The movie was about being a good person while having fun. And that's what "Avatar 2" is about. I was very impressed.

In late winter, as the news of the US Army's highly debated policy shift on welcoming gay, lesbian, bisexual, and transgender service members spread, the National Association for College Admission Counseling issued a statement urging the Department of Education to revisit its guidelines for accepting transgender students. The current guidance has been met with controversy, with some arguing it unfairly discriminates based on gender identity and others saying it falls short.

The military's ban on LGBT troops, however, does not impact how colleges and students receive federal student aid - nor is it likely to, according to the US Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights.

For those unfamiliar with the federal government's approach to student debt, the government provides funding to colleges through the federal financial aid program. Most federal student loans are private, with repayment terms typically involving monthly payments. In cases where borrowers do not complete their education, the government may forgive the debt. The federal government also covers various education-related expenses, including books, fees, and living costs.

In addition to student loans, the government offers grants for education, including college tuition.

"The federal government's role is not to borrow or grant funds," said Betsy Cappelli, director of the Office for Civil Rights at the Department of Education. "Student loan repayment is the sole responsibility of the borrower. The federal government assists borrowers by covering the cost of higher education."

When the Office for Civil Rights received a complaint from the American Civil Liberties Union of Illinois, the department requested clarification from the Department of Defense on its ban on transgender service members, as well as a list of services transgender troops can access, such as hormone treatments.

In February, the Army revised its policy, which previously banned transgender service members. Military officials cited outdated and discriminatory practices, and argued that their own experiences in accepting gay, lesbian, bisexual, and transgender soldiers had shown the need for a more inclusive approach.

Under the revised policy, all service members identifying as transgender will be treated as the gender with which they identify, which may include medical treatments and surgeries covered by the federal government.

Some colleges leverage the federal government to circumvent their own financial aid policies, as the federal government is prohibited from considering factors like race, ethnicity, or religion when distributing aid or determining eligible colleges. In this instance, colleges have received funding through the federal financial aid program administered by the Department of Education.

Pablo Sandoval's future in San Francisco remains somewhat unclear, but his enthusiasm for being part of the team has not wavered. In a surprising turn of events, the Giants extended an offer to the 30-year-old third baseman, which he accepted. 

The Giants' three-year, $50 million deal was sent to Sandoval via text message, just one day after he agreed to a one-year deal with the Boston Red Sox. The deal is the largest in franchise history, surpassing the previous record.

Sandoval, who has consistently hit.275 throughout his career with a.789 OPS and 26 homers in 154 big-league games, will be entering the final year of his current three-year, $35 million contract. He will be eligible for free agency after the 2018 season.

In a brief statement, GM Bobby Evans confirmed that Sandoval had expressed his desire to remain with the team. "He's a great character guy," Evans said.

Sandoval's impressive career statistics include a lifetime.275 batting average, 26 homers, and 154 games played. He was acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in December 2010 and has since made five postseason starts, but has missed the World Series in four of the past five seasons.

The Giants' contract talks with Sandoval began in early December, with the goal of securing a new deal with the left-handed hitting third baseman who earned $10 million in 2015. The two sides eventually agreed to an extension that extended Sandoval's deal through the 2021 season, including a new injury protection clause, but no guarantee of a long-term deal.

The Giants made a late push for Sandoval, seeking a long-term deal that would have likely extended into his prime years. His name became public as a target when the Dodgers expressed optimism that they were close to an agreement with free-agent third baseman Mark Ellis, who had not yet agreed to terms with the team.

Sandoval eventually signed a four-year, $36 million contract with the Red Sox, ending a three-year, $36 million experiment that raised questions in the clubhouse about whether he still had the ability to produce at age 30. He has been healthy in 2015, hitting.292 in the first half and.297 in the second half.

"I know they wanted him here, I know that [coach Bruce Bochy] wanted him here," Evans said. "And what happened is he just chose to say 'No,' and that's great. So, he's still not coming here. I know I've got a decision to make here and [bust on] it if I want to. But I'm happy for the way he's playing."

Sandoval's agent, Casey Close of CAA Sports, has said his client prefers to remain in San Francisco.

Options with flexible expiration dates, commonly referred to as American call options, are generally more valuable than those with fixed expiration dates, known as European call options. This is because American call options grant the holder the freedom to exercise the option at any time prior to its expiration date. In contrast, European call options can only be exercised at the exact moment of expiration. The ability to exercise an option at any time can be particularly beneficial when the underlying asset generates cash flows, such as dividends or interest payments. For instance, if an investor holds a call option on a stock that distributes dividends, they may choose to exercise the option before the dividend payment is made, allowing them to capture the value of the dividend and potentially sell the stock for a profit. The value of an option is influenced by various factors, including the underlying asset's price, strike price, expiration date, volatility, and time remaining until expiration. Each of these factors can impact the value of an option, and the specific effect of each will depend on the unique circumstances surrounding the option.

I recently had the privilege of testing a pre-production Ubuntu Touch device under controlled conditions, where I was able to provide feedback and assess the device's performance under various scenarios. I also took the opportunity to put Ubuntu Touch through its paces in real-world use cases, and I'm thrilled with the results. In fact, I'd love to expand on these use cases and further refine and develop Ubuntu Touch. So, here's my assessment of Ubuntu's hardware and software performance on a phone, tablet, and desktop from day two and day three of testing.

Device and Software Testing

To evaluate the accuracy and stability of Ubuntu for Ubuntu Touch, I used a device purchased from Newegg, a tablet purchased from Amazon, and a desktop computer from HP. These devices were provided by HP and were used as part of a pre-production evaluation of Ubuntu Touch.

On each device, I used stock Ubuntu 16.04.2 x86 software with no special modifications. The hardware specs of each device were identical, except for the tablet, which had 4GB of RAM, while the other two devices had 8GB of RAM. All devices ran Android 4.4.2 KitKat at the time of testing, and Ubuntu Touch was built on the same OS.

I used unlocked devices to allow me to change bands, carriers, SIMs, and settings as needed to test the performance of each device.

Hardware and Software Testing Configuration

To get an accurate picture of how hardware performs on a phone versus an Android phone, it's essential to have complete control over the hardware, software, hardware settings, and software settings of the devices. I also aimed to know what to expect and make an educated prediction about how those expectations would be met.

This testing configuration had two elements: a stock Ubuntu phone (running 16.04.2) and an Android device (running KitKat at the time of testing).

Stock Ubuntu Phone

On my Android tablet and PC, both systems ran stock Ubuntu 16.04.2. All Android app settings were configured as usual, and no customizations or software add-ons were made.

To ensure a fair comparison, I used both devices with a full set of updates installed (i.e., installed the latest LTS version of Ubuntu before testing on the stock Ubuntu device). As I mentioned earlier, there is no difference between KitKat and LTS or between LTS and Nougat when it comes to Ubuntu Touch performance.

Software Configuration / Configuration Tweaks

The stock Ubuntu phone was configured with Android 4.4.2 (ICS) running on the device. Android 3.1 was also available, but no app selection was done to either of those pre-installed, so nothing was selected by default in the "settings" of the stock Ubuntu phone device.

Stock Ubuntu Tablet

Android 3.1 was installed on the tablet and configured as the default system software. Android 4.4.2 was selected by default as the default operating system, and app selection was done as usual.

One of the things I find interesting when using a stock Ubuntu device is the noticeable difference when moving from Android to Ubuntu. For example, the "Settings" app on Ubuntu Touch runs as usual, but it's "Settings" app on the Android phone runs in a rather unusual and awkward way.

Rather than having a single screen, the "Settings" app has multiple screens separated by "sections," and I usually have to scroll through a lot of information and "purchase" various app items. To this end, the "Settings" app is rather cumbersome when using Ubuntu Touch, with a lot of scrolling necessary to navigate between screens, and most frequently accessed sections are on pages that look pretty ugly and not really that intuitive to use without taking your hands off the device. I believe this is a significant aspect of the Ubuntu Touch experience.

A recent study explored the potential for an "emotional safety net" – comprising emotional support and social support – to mitigate the likelihood of impulsive suicide or self-harm in men. Participants were asked to report their thoughts and feelings about suicide over the preceding 30 days using a 7-point questionnaire. Data analysis employed two mixed-methods approaches: (1) a structural equation model examining suicide content and intent for the entire sample, and (2) a structural equation model examining suicide content, emotional support, and social support for a subgroup of men without prior suicide attempts. Follow-up telephone surveys were conducted for an additional 4 years to assess the relationship between suicide content, emotional support, and social support, and subsequent suicide attempts. Results showed that men reporting an emotional safety net at each time point were less likely to experience suicidal thoughts in both survey periods. Conversely, men who had experienced suicidal thoughts and feelings or suicide planning, but lacked emotional support and social support, were more likely to attempt suicide. The study suggests that emotional support may play a crucial role in protecting men from suicide ideation and planning.

The interplay between emotional support, social support, and suicide planning among individuals with mental health disorders remains poorly understood. While previous research has focused on factors influencing suicidal behavior, few studies have examined the relationships between these variables among individuals with and without mental disorders. Furthermore, the social environment has been shown to influence the expression of mental states, including suicidal ideation. For instance, depressed individuals with limited social support tend to display more depressive symptoms.

Numerous studies have established a link between depressive symptoms and suicidal behavior. A nationally representative sample found that individuals who had ever felt depressed were more likely to have attempted suicide within the prior month. Another study reported that depressive symptoms predicted suicide attempts in individuals with and without depression, with a stronger relationship observed in those with less severe depression.

Researchers have identified several factors contributing to increased suicidal behavior among individuals with mental disorders. Social support is one such factor, as individuals with serious psychiatric disorders reported higher levels of perceived support from others. These findings underscore the importance of understanding the nature of individuals' social supports and their interactions with mood states to improve community-based suicide prevention efforts.

This study aimed to investigate whether an emotional safety net – comprising emotional support and social support – can prevent men's decision to kill or commit suicide from being the result of impulsive behavior. We propose that emotional support and social support may prevent men's decision to kill or commit suicide by reducing suicidal ideation, which may lead men to refrain from taking their own lives.

STUDY DESIGN

This study is a secondary analysis of data from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) for 1999-2000, which included 18,579 participants, including 9,966 men, who reported a history of a mental disorder diagnosed more than 1 year before the survey. Participants were recruited through direct postal outreach, direct mailings, and visits to health departments throughout the United States. A total of 18,289 participants were invited to participate, with 60.5% agreeing to participate.

"I'm quite pleased to see the positive economic impact of marijuana legalization," said John O'Hara, a professor in the department of public health at New York University. "It's clear that this development has significant benefits for the health of individuals who use it."

The benefits of marijuana are well-established, but it's uncertain what the long-term economic impact will be if legalization continues to expand, which seems likely given the trend.

One of the most common questions now is why some people would choose to use marijuana despite knowing it may lead to health issues. The simple answer is that it's now legal.

Researchers at NYU's Langone Medical Center published a study in JAMA Internal Medicine on Tuesday, comparing trends in mortality rates, health program usage, and other public health metrics for people aged 25-35 in eight states that legalized medical marijuana since 1999.

The researchers analyzed data on the age, sex, race, and education of 2.1 million non-smokers and 2.4 million marijuana users in the study. Participants were excluded if they had a history of marijuana-related prescription drug or alcohol use, were incarcerated, had diabetes, heart disease, or cancer.

The study found that the age-adjusted percentage of non-smokers who were not regular marijuana users decreased from around 13% in 2003 to around 10% in 2012. The percentage of non-smokers with diabetes also decreased, from around 12% in 2003 to around 6% in 2012.

In terms of education, the study found that the percentage of non-smokers with high school diplomas or fewer degrees decreased from around 5% in 2003 to around 4% in 2012.

The study showed that there was no statistically significant increase in smoking rates through 2013. However, among marijuana users, there was a significant increase in prescription drug use, tobacco use, and risk of obesity and diabetes. The researchers noted that the increase in cardiovascular disease risk may be due to patients using marijuana medicinally.

"This could help explain why some people may choose to use marijuana before they've been diagnosed with serious conditions," said O'Hara.

The study also found evidence linking marijuana use to an increased risk of mental health issues, including depression, anxiety, and panic. The risk may be due to users smoking more heavily or longer, as many studies have shown that people use marijuana more frequently as their brain develops.

However, the increase in the number of non-smokers with diabetes is a different story. The researchers found that this might be associated with a change in how state Medicaid programs spend healthcare costs on people with diabetes who are non-smokers.

"More than 1 in every 10 people with diabetes who use medical marijuana have diabetes under their care," said Jeffrey Gordon, deputy director of New York University Langone Medical Center's Department of Public Health and the paper's senior author. "For those who do use marijuana, their use of it could reduce their need for diabetes treatment."

The researchers estimate that marijuana users may have contributed around $200 million to the American Diabetes Association in 2012.

The study's lead author, O'Hara, noted that the study is consistent with a large body of work showing that marijuana use has medical risks. He acknowledged that there is ongoing debate about whether legalization is the best approach.

"We support legalization because it's a relatively affordable way to manage pain and other medical conditions without the high costs of prescription drugs and alcohol," he said.

As I reflect on my life, I'm struck by the notion that 'the next big thing' is often an overhyped concept. In reality, the most significant accomplishment is often one's own personal growth. For me, that growth has been fueled by my passion for adventure and exploration.

Recently, I celebrated the 20-minute mark since I stood atop Mont Ventoux in the Alps, gazing out at the breathtaking view of Barcelona, Spain. This experience was a poignant reminder of the power of perseverance and dedication. In 2015, I became the first person to climb Mont Ventoux in 22 hours, 2 minutes, and 42 seconds since the mountain was first scaled in 1912. Since then, I've been driven to push my limits and explore new horizons.

As a child, I dreamed of being Spider-Man, soaring through the skies and leaping from building to building. As I grew older, I discovered that my passion for climbing was not just a fantasy, but a tangible reality. By the time I was 20, I had completed nine major challenges, and by my late twenties, I had tackled eight more. My personal best time was 14 hours and 45 minutes on the Eiger, and that achievement gave me the confidence to take on the Ventoux.

In the summer of 2013, I began training for the Ventoux, pouring over maps and research to find the perfect route. I was drawn to the Col de Sélévissement, a classic route that offered a unique challenge. I spent hours reading about the climb, pouring over descriptions and details, and I was hooked. I knew I had to tackle it.

As I prepared for the climb, I started writing a script to help me follow the route. Weeks turned into months, and I found myself training tirelessly. I knew I could do it.

On September 9, 2013, I began climbing Mont Ventoux for the first time, just as my junior year was coming to a close. I was 19, and that marked the beginning of a new chapter in my life. I decided to put my climbing career on hold and focus on my college studies. After completing my degree in Sociology and English Literature, I returned to climbing, and the time away from school had made me physically stronger.

The following year, I competed in a 10-day mountain climbing competition, and I was ecstatic. I had discovered a new level of physical strength and endurance, and I was determined to continue pushing myself. When I finished university, I started climbing again in early 2015.

As a professional cyclist, my training schedule is intense, with three workouts per day. This allows me to build up my energy levels and maintain my physical condition. I also have the flexibility to stay home in Scotland for almost four months of the year, which gives me the opportunity to continue climbing and exploring.

The experience of climbing is unique and transformative, and I feel grateful to have a supportive team behind me every step of the way. They're like my family, always there to encourage and support me, no matter where I am or what the weather brings.

A Surprising Look at What People Really Eat on Thanksgiving

As the holiday season approaches, many of us find ourselves scrambling to prepare a delicious meal for our loved ones. But what do people really eat on Thanksgiving? The answer might surprise you.

Thanksgiving: A Time-Honored Tradition

For many families, Thanksgiving is a time to come together and share a meal. Traditionally, this meal features a roasted turkey, accompanied by a variety of side dishes and desserts. But what about the food choices people make?

A Delicious and Fresh Feast

When it comes to preparing a successful Thanksgiving meal, freshness, local ingredients, and ease of preparation are key. People often choose their own foods with some variation, but there's always a sense of harmony and togetherness with family.

The Traditional Thanksgiving Table

Whether you're hosting a big or small gathering, the traditional Thanksgiving table typically features a roasted turkey, accompanied by side dishes and desserts. Some families may also include special traditions, such as a holiday song or a family meal called a "wedding."

A Delicious and Varied Menu

The most common Thanksgiving meal features a roasted turkey, often served with a salad, biscuits and gravy, and a variety of side dishes. But people also enjoy a range of vegetables, fruits, and classic sides like mashed potatoes, stuffing, and sweet potatoes.

A Sweet and Savory Finish

Pumpkin Pie Revamp

My little ones are absolutely crazy about pumpkin pie, especially the crust! I had some leftover recipes, so I decided to whip up a batch with a few tweaks. I started by using most of the ingredients from this crust, but with a few twists. First, I swapped out the fat in the filling for skim milk and whole wheat flour. That meant no cream cheese, and I opted for a mix of butter and coconut oil in the crust. This resulted in a more tender crust without the overpowering pumpkin flavor. You get the full pumpkin flavor in the filling, so you don't need the coconut oil to balance it out – which was a nice bonus. Next, I added a cinnamon stick to the filling instead of just the crust. It adds a hint of real pumpkin spice flavor.

Pumpkin Pie

3 tablespoons coconut oil

1/2 cup whole wheat flour

1/2 cup granulated sugar

1/2 teaspoon salt

4 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces

1/2 cup granulated sugar

3 large eggs

3/4 cup buttermilk

1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon

3 tablespoons melted unsalted butter, for topping

1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract

1 tablespoon whole milk, for whisking

1 8-ounce can pumpkin puree, drained and cut into 1/4 inch pieces

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Line an 8-inch pie pan with parchment paper. Combine coconut oil and flour in a bowl, mixing until smooth. Add sugar, then salt. Mix until combined. Combine butter and sugar in a large bowl. Add eggs, and mix until combined. Add buttermilk, cinnamon, and melted butter. Mix until just combined. Set aside. In a separate shallow bowl, whisk together milk and butter. Set aside. In the same bowl, mix together buttermilk, flour, and cinnamon. Add mixture to the bowl with eggs and buttermilk. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10 minutes or until dough is smooth. Shape into a large, oval shape that's 3/4 inch thick – it'll be slightly thicker than a quarter. Place dough in the prepared pie pan and cover with parchment paper for up to an hour. After the first hour, remove the pie from the oven and let it cool completely. Once it's cool enough to handle, press the dough firmly down using a fork to prevent it from sliding around.

When you're ready to bake it, remove the parchment paper and place the pie over a baking sheet so it's almost level with the bottom edge of the sheet. Grease the back of the pie plate with coconut oil and then place the pie on top of it. Bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until golden. Let it cool on a wire rack before cutting.

I've had the chance to explore the mobile networks of several major European countries. What I found was intriguing. Each network has its unique features, but they also share some commonalities. For instance, they all offer international roaming options, with varying limits on international minutes, data, and calling plans. They also have similar credit structures for making international calls, although the actual costs can differ significantly.

The outcome: during my first three weeks in the EU, I noticed that France's big three networks didn't charge for domestic roaming at all, with rates as low as €0.19 per minute. In contrast, the UK and Germany's networks had similar pricing, ranging from €0.17 to €0.30 per minute for international calls. Italy's situation was more varied, with two of its four major networks offering no roaming charges, while T-Mobile charged as little as €0.15 per minute.

It's true that French consumers tend to use their mobile services extensively, which might explain the lack of charges for international calls. However, this discovery highlights the availability of decent mobile roaming deals across Europe. In the UK, Germany, and Italy, two major operators offer prepaid plans that can provide a good value, while France's big three networks are excellent options for international roaming. When faced with multiple operators and similar pricing, I usually opt for the cheapest option from the top three operators.

Honda has announced a recall that could allow roughly 33% of its Civic lineup to receive repairs for a defect causing the steering wheel to lose its usual firmness, resulting in a noticeable wobble and vibration when turning the wheel.

The recall encompasses over 1.5 million vehicles produced by Japan's top three automakers. These cars are equipped with a key that automatically disengages when the vehicle is left idling or when the brakes are applied, Honda notes. This issue arises when the internal tension within the steering wheel becomes too lax.

When the tension is too low, the steering wheel can rotate, producing a distinct rattling noise in the steering column and dashboard. In extreme cases, the vehicle may become stuck in a low gear, leading to unintended movements or even brake lockup, according to Honda.

The issue was identified during Honda's research in March 2014. Although not a safety concern, the company is taking proactive measures to address the problem by recalling 1.47 million vehicles.

Honda is urging owners to schedule their vehicles for repairs between December 6, 2014, and January 18, 2015. Owners can arrange a complimentary inspection by contacting 1-866-234-1213.

Job interviews can be a daunting experience, leaving many of us feeling anxious and on edge. A recent study by the University of California, Hastings College of the Law, suggests that this anxiety can have a significant impact on our job search success.

Researchers surveyed over 400 students before and after job interviews, and found that those who experienced higher levels of anxiety were less likely to take on new jobs, less likely to get interviews, and less likely to get promotions. In fact, anxiety levels were a strong predictor of job search performance, with high levels of anxiety often leading to unsuccessful job searches.

The study also found that anxiety levels remained stable throughout the job search process, and were a strong predictor of job success after the interview. This suggests that anxiety can have a lasting impact on our job search outcomes.

The researchers attribute this to the physiological responses that occur when we're feeling stressed, including increased levels of cortisol, a hormone released by the adrenal glands. This can trigger anxiety and affect our decision-making abilities, leading to less optimal job choices.

The findings suggest that it's important to manage stress and anxiety levels during the job search process, as high levels of stress can lead to poor job search behaviors and decreased job success. The study's authors recommend that job seekers take steps to reduce their anxiety levels, such as practicing relaxation techniques and preparing thoroughly for interviews.

The study's findings are published in the May issue of the Journal of Applied Psychology.

Water storage structures, like dams, are designed to contain a specific volume of water. However, circumstances may arise where the water volume exceeds the dam's capacity. In such cases, the excess water requires a safe release path to prevent overflow and subsequent issues downstream. To address this, engineers design spillways – specialized channels or pipes that enable the water to flow away from the dam in a controlled manner. Unchecked overflow could lead to erosion and potentially catastrophic consequences, including dam failure or collapse.

Bonds are a type of investment where an individual lends money to a business or government, essentially functioning as a loan. The borrower commits to paying a fixed interest rate, known as the coupon, and returning the original loan amount, referred to as the face value, once the bond expires. A debenture, on the other hand, is a debt instrument that relies on the borrower's overall creditworthiness rather than specific assets. Typically issued by reputable corporations or governments, debentures are viewed as less volatile than other forms of debt.

While bonds are generally considered a more secure investment due to the backing of tangible assets, debentures may offer higher returns due to their perceived higher risk.

It's a common misconception that one can achieve happiness and fulfillment without resorting to any substance. Despite this, many individuals continue to use drugs, often leading to a vicious cycle of self-deception. Drug addiction is a complex condition that affects not only the brain but also the body, with far-reaching consequences. The misuse of drugs can lead to devastating, long-lasting effects, including damage to various areas of the brain and the hijacking of neurotransmitters essential for bodily functions.

In this article, we'll delve into the intricacies of addiction, exploring how it works, why people become addicted, and the various treatment options available. We'll also examine the effects of addiction on the brain and the importance of understanding these mechanisms in order to develop effective treatment strategies.

Addiction is often driven by the pursuit of immediate pleasure, which can lead to the repeated use of drugs and the development of addiction. The brain's reward system is designed to respond to pleasurable experiences, and drugs can activate this system, leading to a cycle of craving and use.

Quitting a drug can be a challenging and daunting task, especially for those who have developed a strong physical dependence. Withdrawal symptoms can range from mild to severe, including headaches, nausea, and difficulty sleeping. In some cases, withdrawal can lead to catastrophic physical reactions, making it essential to seek medical attention.

A more effective approach to quitting a drug is to do so gradually, allowing the individual to adjust to the absence of the substance. This can help minimize the risk of severe withdrawal symptoms and reduce the likelihood of relapse.

In order to develop effective treatment strategies, it's essential to understand how addiction affects the brain and the various mechanisms that drive this condition. By studying the brain's response to drugs and the changes that occur during addiction, researchers can develop targeted treatments that address the underlying mechanisms of addiction.

The brain plays a critical role in addiction, as it is responsible for processing the pleasurable effects of drugs and the subsequent craving and use. The brain's reward system is designed to respond to pleasurable experiences, and drugs can activate this system, leading to a cycle of craving and use.

Neurotransmitters are chemical messengers that play a crucial role in addiction. They enable the transmission of signals between neurons, influencing our behavior, mood, and emotions. In the context of addiction, neurotransmitters can be hijacked, leading to changes in brain function and behavior.

Memory plays a critical role in addiction, as it can be influenced by the experiences we have while using drugs. This can lead to the formation of negative memories and the development of avoidance behaviors. Understanding the mechanisms of memory and how they are affected by addiction is essential for developing effective treatment strategies.

In conclusion, addiction is a complex condition that affects not only the brain but also the body. By understanding the mechanisms of addiction and the various treatment options available, we can develop more effective strategies for overcoming addiction and improving the lives of those affected.

Social scientists and statisticians agree that the wealthy tend to be wealthier than the poor. This disparity arises from the fact that most people have access to the same resources, allowing them to acquire goods and services that others cannot. As a result, if the wealthy are indeed wealthier, it is likely that inequality will continue to increase.

However, what if resource overlap did not exist? What if rich countries could maintain their wealth even without sharing resources with others? This is the premise of a recent analysis by Robert Gordon of Northwestern University and Emmanuel Saez of the University of California, Berkeley, which examines the intergenerational transmission of economic opportunity in advanced economies.

The analysis reveals that inequality in the United States declined significantly in the decades preceding the financial crisis but has since stabilized, despite global income growth. Moreover, the share of earnings going to the top 1% has remained constant or even increased. This trend is concerning, as it suggests that the distribution of opportunities within the United States is widening as the rest of the world becomes wealthier. To address this disparity, the rich must be taxed at the same rate as others.

Gordon and Saez found that, from 1950 to 2014, the share of national income going to the bottom 90% of earners increased more rapidly in the United States compared to other developed countries. This trend does not hold true for the top 10% or top 1% of earners, suggesting that this disparity is primarily statistical.

The increase in inequality occurred during the "great moderation," a period marked by rapid welfare state reforms. However, this was likely due to weak economic growth, which allowed countries to implement reforms gradually. In contrast, the United States and other developed countries made significant adjustments on their own in the 1980s.

When the United States raised its top tax rate from 50% to 70% in the 1980s, the richest 1% of earners accounted for a greater share of the overall income than at any time since 1929. This shift significantly increased the share of income going to the top earners, consistent across both the top 10% and top 1% income brackets.

The United States has the highest relative inequality in the OECD, and may even be more unequal than the richest countries in the organization. The authors' measure of inequality, which considers labor market participation and income and wealth shares of the top 1%, shows that the share of income going to the bottom 90% fell more rapidly in the United States in the 1990s than in any other developed country.

The authors emphasize the importance of controlling for other determinants of income distribution, such as technological change and tax policies. However, the strong drop in inequality for the top 1% is not consistent with these factors. It is likely that other factors, such as the rise in the bargaining power of poor workers and the decline in wage discrimination between similarly situated individuals, would have been important regardless.

The authors also note that their measure of inequality assumes that every individual earns at their level of productivity. However, the US economy has experienced significant growth in the past two decades, with much of this growth attributed to higher average output per hour worked. In this context, it is not reasonable to assume that every person earns the same.

The discovery of a long-lost tomb has shed new light on the life and times of Tutankhamun, the Egyptian pharaoh who ruled over 3,000 years ago. According to experts, the tomb is believed to be the final resting place of the boy king, who was killed in the 1220s BC.

The tomb, which is located near the site of Tutankhamun's great tomb, is a fascinating archaeological find. It contains thousands of mummies and artifacts, which are arranged in rows, giving archaeologists a unique glimpse into the past.

Tutankhamun's burial chamber is particularly significant, as it was constructed by his father, uncle, and grandfather around 1350 BC. The chamber dates back to the end of the New Kingdom period, a time when Egypt was ruled by powerful pharaohs.

Tutankhamun's life was marked by tragedy, as he was killed at a young age. His son, Akhenaten, rose to power, but was later toppled by ancient kings who saw his cult worship as idolatrous.

The discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb has sparked intense interest, with archaeologists working tirelessly to uncover the secrets of the boy king's life and death. According to Abdul-Aziz Ismail, an archaeologist in charge of the site, the team has made significant progress, uncovering the royal coffin and a pharaoh's sarcophagus.

The tomb's construction is believed to have been a joint effort between Tutankhamun's father and grandfather, who built the tomb to hide the burial. There is speculation that an attempt was made to relocate Tutankhamun to an adjoining temple, but this remains unclear.

Some experts argue that the boy king was buried elsewhere and later moved to Akhenaten's tomb, while others believe that he was buried in the tomb discovered by archaeologists.

The discovery of the tomb has also shed light on the life of Tutankhamun's cousin, Kiya, who ruled for 1340 years and was believed to be the son of Tutankhamun himself. The tomb has provided a unique glimpse into the past, giving archaeologists a chance to learn more about royal funerary rites and customs.

The tombs built by kings were usually filled with mummified and partially mummified bodies of rulers, and the discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb has provided a fascinating insight into the life and times of the boy king.

In 2154, the Enterprise-E embarked on an intergalactic mission and encountered two unidentified creatures. Upon returning to Earth, it was determined that the creatures were not from our planet. Admiral Kirk took this information to Starfleet, leading to the ship's deployment to a distant galaxy.

The Enterprise-E's command division included Chief of Security Travis Mayweather and First Officer T'Pol.

Following several incidents of the USS Enterprise-E being destroyed in intergalactic space, Starfleet created a special division to track down and rebuild the vessel.
