The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) has made a decision regarding the collection of phone records, despite a recent order from the Justice Department to cease the practice.

The NTIA's decision was made after the National Security Agency's (NSA) bulk collection of metadata was challenged by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) in the US Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court.

The ACLU requested that the court order the government to stop collecting phone records, and the NTIA responded by stating it would continue to collect them. This comes as the Supreme Court is set to decide whether to reinstate the mass collection of US phone records under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.

US President Barack Obama has urged Congress to reform the FISA court to ensure that "only a select few" are using the program. He also emphasized the importance of the collection and storage of phone records in maintaining national security.

The president stated that intelligence agencies should always seek court approval before engaging in surveillance that gathers communications about people known to live in the United States. The White House added that the surveillance of phone calls is critical to American security and privacy and is carried out under authorities enacted by Congress to counteract terrorism.

The ACLU's executive director, Anthony Romero, stated that it is time to end the dragnet collecting of phone call metadata and that the government must stop doing it once and for all. Senator Ron Wyden, a member of the Senate's intelligence committee, echoed this sentiment, stating that the government's continued collection of vast amounts of Americans' phone call information is an affront to the American people and the Constitution.

The NTIA had argued that collecting phone records is a powerful investigative tool in finding terrorists who use encryption. However, critics argue that the program is engaged in widespread collection of data that could be used against Americans without an individual warrant.

The US government has claimed that the program does not collect the metadata of American citizens, but a government analysis published in December 2013 concluded that the phone records included records on "nearly all" of the United States population.

When you notice an unusual reading on your urine test, it's crucial to schedule a follow-up appointment with your healthcare provider. To address the issue, consider the following steps:

Collaborate with your healthcare provider to develop a personalized treatment plan. This may involve taking prescribed medications and adhering to a recommended regimen.

Work with your healthcare team to manage any underlying conditions that may be contributing to your high albumin levels. This might involve making lifestyle adjustments, such as adopting a balanced diet and incorporating regular exercise, as well as taking medications as directed.

Regularly monitor your kidney function to track any changes. Your healthcare provider may recommend blood and urine tests to assess your creatinine and glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

Consider seeking guidance from a healthcare professional or joining a support group to help you navigate your condition and make informed decisions about your treatment.

It's essential to note that the appropriate course of treatment will depend on the underlying cause of your high albumin levels. Be sure to follow up with your healthcare provider and adhere to their recommended treatment plan.

The US National Archives is poised to revolutionize the way we access historical documents. The National Archives has been working to digitize the Madison Papers since 1995, with the goal of creating a comprehensive online collection of public records. Ferriero believes that making everything available online under a searchable index would take the project to the next level.

"We're building a digital library of documents that will provide a repository of the most important information collected in the United States over time," he explains. "This will be a valuable resource for historians, public health experts, and scholars, and will also attract foreign scholars from around the world."

A fresh development in the ongoing struggle over the Affordable Care Act's insurance marketplaces has unfolded in Kansas, a state that handed Mitt Romney a decisive victory in 2012. Republican lawmakers have introduced a proposal that would significantly reduce the number of individuals covered and eliminate subsidies for many recipients.

The Republican bill would also substantially limit access to the marketplace. Approximately 1 million people would lose their subsidies, according to the Kaiser Family Foundation. The insurance marketplaces currently cover around 10 million Americans, with approximately 9 million of those individuals residing in Kansas. The exchanges are a crucial component of President Obama's signature legislation. The Obama administration estimates that the Affordable Care Act would have imposed a significant financial burden on the state, roughly $1.2 billion in 2015, without the exchanges.

Kansas Governor Sam Brownback, a Republican, has consistently expressed opposition to the Affordable Care Act. In 2013, he announced plans to discontinue the state's Medicaid program. Instead of expanding the program through the Affordable Care Act, Brownback opted for a conservative alternative, the Medicaid block grant program, which he initially proposed in 2011.

The block grant model has proved successful for many Republican governors, as it allows them to maintain control over their Medicaid programs. However, it has been a disappointing outcome for Kansas, with the healthcare insurance exchange and Medicaid expansion resulting in a net increase of only 4,900 individuals in the state when the original bill was signed. In 2014, the state was required to cover $125 million in federal Medicaid funds out of pocket.

In a recent column, I touched on the flaws in the US healthcare system. One major issue is that the current model doesn't account for the true costs of healthcare. When considering direct medical costs and administrative expenses, the system still leaves consumers with a hefty bill. The price of a medical procedure or pharmaceutical drug varies depending on several factors, including the time of service, patient's condition, and payment method.

Several other issues affect consumers and taxpayers, but these three have the most significant impact. Estimating the true costs of healthcare is challenging, but Medicare and Medicaid provide some insight. Medicare adjusts the value of services based on the total cost, while Medicaid multiplies the cost by the patient's income. The difference between the two is zero, resulting in a conservative approach to reimbursement.

This means that Medicaid and Medicare only cover the most expensive and effective treatments, leaving some individuals with no payment or coverage. Even if there's a benefit to receiving hospitalization at a lower cost, it's minimal. Healthcare is a vital part of the US economy, but it's expensive to deliver.

The current model also contributes to the large number of uninsured and underinsured Americans. While the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act ensures health coverage for everyone, the federal government's role in providing coverage may not be the only or primary mechanism. Federal programs, such as the Community Living Assistance Services and Supports program, provide assistance to low-income individuals and families but only cover a portion of their expenses.

To better understand the cost of providing insurance to the poor, consider the process for a young adult in Philadelphia seeking a job and insurance. Getting a job is less expensive than obtaining insurance, which often requires a medical exam. If an individual goes to the doctor without employer-provided coverage, they may pay for an exam they would otherwise have to pay for.

It's essential to recognize that healthcare is a vital function of the US economy, but it's expensive to deliver. If the government can negotiate with insurers to lower healthcare prices, there will be less cost in delivering healthcare to patients. This would be beneficial for low-income Americans and taxpayers alike.

— Robert Tracinski, founder of the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities.

Exploring the Hemispheres: A Journey Through the Northern and Southern Hemispheres

As we delve into the fascinating world of hemispheres, it's essential to understand the unique characteristics of each region. The Northern and Southern Hemispheres, in particular, exhibit distinct features that set them apart from one another. By examining the relative positions of these hemispheres, we can gain a deeper understanding of the Earth's geography.

The diagram above provides a simplified representation of the Earth's hemispheres, showcasing the North and South Triangles. This visual representation demonstrates the significant differences between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The Northern Hemisphere, which includes the northern polar region, is situated north of the Southern Hemisphere, whereas the Southern Hemisphere is positioned south of the Northern Hemisphere.

To further illustrate the relationship between these hemispheres, let's consider a more detailed diagram. This diagram highlights the Earth-Sun/Earth system, providing a more accurate representation of the hemispherical structure.

The second diagram showcases the South and North poles, represented by red triangles, along with the hemispheres of Africa, Australia, Antarctica, and the Southern Hemisphere, depicted on a blue rectangle. This visual representation allows us to better comprehend the size and positions of the Earth-Sun and Earth-Africa/Africa regions, as well as the South and North poles.

When examining the Earth-Africa/Africa region, we notice that the Southern Pole is situated in Africa, while the Northern Pole is located in Antarctica. This leads us to assume that the North Pole is situated in Australia, which is incorrect. In reality, the North Pole is situated in the southern part of Antarctica.

The difference between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres is particularly evident at the South Pole, where the Southern Pole is located in the Eastern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere is situated in the Northern Hemisphere.

The Earth's hemispherical nature is also highlighted by the presence of mountains in Antarctica, South Africa, parts of South America, and parts of Eastern Asia.

The Earth's formation is believed to have resulted from the fusion of two separate pieces, which eventually merged to form our planet.

The Northern Hemisphere and Southern Hemisphere are hemispheres in themselves, but due to the Earth's spherical shape, they are actually composed of four separate hemispheres. These four regions are located on the equator, near the center of the Earth.

As we look directly up at the sky with the Sun at the Southern horizon, we can clearly see that the Southern Hemisphere is located further north than the Northern Hemisphere. This is a direct consequence of the Earth's non-circular shape.

Our planet is composed of two primary layers of material: a molten outer layer called the Earth and a solid inner core, which keeps the two layers separate. The solid inner core is covered by a shell of water, which can move upwards or downwards due to friction from the planet's rotation.

The Sun plays a vital role in protecting the Earth's surface, but it is not the only factor. The gravitational pull of numerous large objects in the Solar System also contributes to the planet's stability.

The Moon, in particular, plays a crucial role in the Earth's rotation and gravitational balance.

A clever approach to eliminate lint from your code, inspired by the Python Lint. This tutorial has also been adapted for Ruby. The syntax employed for lint in this tutorial differs slightly from that used in Django Lint. However, it should function effectively in both projects. Getting Started To install the package, visit PyPI or use pip from source. From source: `sudo pip install --upgrade lint-lint` Usage To utilize the lint feature, simply invoke the lint method and provide the code you wish to analyze. Example: * From an existing module: `from lint_lint import lint; lint.Report()` * From a string: `from lint_lint import lint; lint("#some code")` * From a template: `lint('

#some code

')` Options The lint module accepts various keyword parameters to customize the report and modify settings. Please note their purpose. Report The report generated by Lint is the primary output. By default, it produces a simple list of reported violations. You can also provide additional strings to display violation details or modify report formatting. These are passed as the third argument when using a string argument. When omitting the report keyword argument, Lint will report all violations, even those it cannot detect due to lack of warnings. In a template, supply a string to output along with the report keyword argument. This may represent some of the warnings. Output defaults to an empty list if omitted. The --verbose option can be used to display the full source code of Lint while running, which may be helpful when debugging specific violations. Options -v and --vvv will display more verbose output, but only if --verbose is enabled. Warning Numbers Warning numbers can be assigned to reported violations. The default is 1. To enforce a specific number of warning numbers, add "warning_number=1" to the report argument. You can also provide a comma-separated list for the warning number. In addition, if a given line is used in a violation, it will be interpreted as the warning number of that line. To display example violations, run: `$ lint -vv --report lint_some_file.py # some code violated # --number=10 warning_number=24 # a number 1 violation #` The --report option is an alias for lint(). Report by Line If you're using something like rambler, you don't need to pass reports. Instead, use lint to generate a formatted report that you can open and print to a file. Example: `lint([[ " # some code ", " # another value ", " # a third value " ], 2])` The -p, --pretty option can be applied to the report, which can be very helpful for visually displaying data. You can also set your own formatting to print only matching lines. Contributing To distribute code against your module or theme, you'll likely need to build the Lint package using standard build-steps. Running lint using pip is probably the fastest way to go, but if you'd like help or documentation on the current steps for your distribution, ask below. Acknowledgments

A specific type of chemical reaction, saponification, occurs when a combination of an ester and an alkali is heated. The alkali, often a strong base like sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide, plays a crucial role in this reaction. The ester, typically a fat or oil like lard or olive oil, undergoes a transformation as a result of the heat. The ester bonds are broken down into smaller molecules consisting of an acid and an alcohol. The acid reacts with the base, yielding a salt, while the alcohol emerges as the primary product. This process is commonly referred to as "soap-making" due to the resulting soap-like substance.

Within the context of establishments that primarily serve alcohol, individuals employed as bartenders or in related roles play a crucial role in providing exceptional customer service. These employees, often referred to as "bar staff," typically work in establishments such as bars, lounges, or taprooms, where their primary duties involve serving and preparing a wide range of beverages for customers and their guests.

The term "bar staff" encompasses a broad scope of employees, including those who work in breweries, hotels, motels, restaurants, and retail establishments that sell or serve alcohol. According to the Department of Labor, "bar staff" includes anyone who is employed primarily as a bartender or prepares beverages on or for premises where such beverages are sold or served.

In certain situations, employees of retail establishments with an average nightly occupancy of 500 or more persons must be residents of that establishment and work within the premises. This definition is crucial in understanding the regulations that apply to "bar staff" employed by other employers.

The Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) defines "employees" for purposes of determining whether to grant or deny a "special immigrant visa." The Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics has conducted an analysis of the employment status of individuals granted a temporary work or residence permit under INA section 212(a)(12)(B), finding that the "bar staff" definition encompasses bar staff employed by restaurants, hotels, motels, or other retail establishments.

To demonstrate a substantial connection between the job held and the employer, employers must show that there is a substantial connection between the job held and the employer's business. This connection is deemed substantial if the employer could not find a replacement with similar skills and experience at a comparable wage and working conditions. If no substantial connection exists, the employer may not be entitled to favorable treatment.

The Department of Labor's regulations and interpretation of § 5101(a)(2) outline a three-part test to determine substantial connection, divided into subparts A, B, and C. Subpart B requires that the employee who actually fulfills the job duties has a substantial connection to the establishment that employed them.

When your partner or significant other leaves your home uninvited after asking you out, take note. It's not the end of the world if they don't return, says Dr. Susan L. Greenfield, author of The End: Understanding Dating Abuse and Surviving Stalking. In today's world, where social media and mobile devices have made it easier to track our movements, it's crucial to be aware of potential stalking situations.

If someone is following you or your partner, you have two options: handle the situation safely or take advantage of the stalker's emotions. "You can choose to either get yourself into a secure position or take action against the stalker," Greenfield advises.

How Can Someone Follow Me?

Stalkers often lack boundaries, and one example is when someone follows your partner after asking you out, says Greenfield.

Before taking action against a stalker, your partner may try to initiate a romantic connection and then inform friends or family members about your relationship. If the friend or family member doesn't believe you, they can report the incident to the authorities.

"You don't need a criminal record to report a stalking incident," Greenfield emphasizes. "The police are receptive to calls about stalking."

Why Does Someone Want to Follow Me?

The reasons behind stalking often relate to the victim's relationship status. If you're dating someone you're not interested in, the stalker might feel you're not giving them enough credit, leading them to follow you home.

However, it's essential to communicate to the stalker that their behavior is unacceptable. The best course of action is for the stalker to move on and make an honest decision about what's best for them.

"You need to make a decision that feels right for you," Greenfield advises. "It won't be easy, but it's crucial for your well-being."

Don't let a stalker manipulate you by saying they're following you home to get revenge on their partner. This behavior is likely to escalate.

Dealing with Stalking

It's a challenging situation, but Greenfield encourages victims to try the following strategies:

Ensure your partner's safety and support system are in place.

Never share financial information with anyone, including the stalker.

Avoid visiting places suggested by the stalker.

Put away your phone.

Don't engage with strangers.

Report the incident to the authorities. The FBI and local police are committed to solving stalking cases.

"It's essential for the victim to get involved," Greenfield emphasizes.

In the realm of electron physics, the polarization effect plays a crucial role in semiconductor functionality. The polarization of electrons, which refers to their direction of rotation, is not typically a major concern in semiconductor physics, but it becomes significant when attempting to control electron flow across a conductive surface. Since electrons naturally align with the surface of the semiconductor, the "normal" position of the electron on the surface is identical to its position within the semiconductor. However, a small offset in polarization creates a distinct polarization difference, allowing for the transfer of electrons between positions within the semiconductor.

The electric field within a semiconductor is directly proportional to its polarizability. In a semiconductor with zero polarizability, the electric field remains constant regardless of the electron's proximity to the surface. This does not preclude the deposition of electric charge on the semiconductor surface, but it does imply reduced resistance to electron transfer between distant points on the semiconductor compared to the same location within the semiconductor.

Polarizability is measured by examining the direction of the electric field across the semiconductor, which comprises the electric field at the core and perpendicular to the planes of the semiconductor. One common manifestation of semiconductor polarizability is the direction of current flow. The current is perpendicular to the semiconductor plane, which is normal to the axis of the semiconductor. The electric field across the semiconductor is referred to as AC voltage, with the positive portion corresponding to electron polarization and the negative portion corresponding to hole polarization. The direction of the electric field is directly proportional to the semiconductor's polarizability.

The polarizability is the electric polarization component, which is a vector multiplied by the electric field. Additionally, two other key aspects of ideal, pure semiconductors relate to polarization.

When the electric field at the core and outside the semiconductor combine, they add a component perpendicular to each other with the same direction. Such electrically conductive surfaces are referred to as superconductors. The electrical resistance in a current flowing through a superconductor is typically greater than one volt per amp. The addition of the electric polarization component perpendicular to the component in each direction of electric field always results in the same electrical resistance. For instance, if the field component perpendicular to the electric field is parallel from point to point on a surface, it always results in a resistance at that point of one volt per amp.

The electrical current is a linear function of electric polarizability and electric field. The polarity of the current depends on the polarity of the electric field. Therefore, the polarization of the electric field can significantly impact the potential for current flow through the semiconductor. At the very least, the polarization of the current can be a significant determining factor.

Electron Polarization (Polarizability) Effect

Electrons within a semiconductor are not uniformly aligned with the magnetic plane but are instead polarized by a small amount. Electrons on the surface of a semiconductor may be aligned in one of two ways. They may occupy the "normal" position of the semiconductor, which is the direction of rotation for the electron on the surface. This "normal" position can be identical to the normal position of the electron within the semiconductor. Alternatively, an electron may be aligned if the electric field is parallel to its surface. If the electric field is parallel to the surface of the semiconductor, all electrons may be aligned with their normal position. Since only a few electrons' electric fields are perpendicular to the surface of the crystal, it is not feasible for this electric field to transfer electrons from all points within a semiconductor to any point on a neighboring surface where the field is parallel.

Semiconductor Poles

If no electric field is present at the surface of the semiconductor, only one direction of electron rotation may exist, but there will be no electrically conductive material at the point where the electron is located. Such a semiconductor will have many surface electrons, resulting in very low conductivity, which is referred to as a "quartz surface".

If an electric field is present at the surface, only one direction of electron rotation perpendicular to the surface could exist, and there would be no electrically conductive material at the point where the electron is located.

The evolution of science is often attributed to the "Great Academies" of the British and French, with the United States following suit with the establishment of its own major science academy, the Royal Society. However, this narrative oversimplifies the complex history of scientific inquiry.

The question of "when" is not the same as the question of "who." It is essential to understand what sets science apart from other forms of human inquiry, rather than focusing solely on the number of individuals involved. The scientific method is characterized by its ability to build upon existing knowledge, whereas non-specialist inquiry is often limited by the availability of ideas and the capacity to pursue them.

The distinction between science and non-science is not solely due to the scientific revolution or the "newness" of modern science. Rather, it stems from the cumulative nature of scientific inquiry, which allows for the gradual accumulation of knowledge over time.

In astronomy and physics, the discovery of the solar system's structure and the distance of the Earth from the Sun were long-standing debates. The concept of the solar system as a small part of the cosmos was a central theme in these discussions. The first experiments in science were not groundbreaking, but rather built upon existing knowledge.

Galileo's telescope, for instance, was not a revolutionary invention, but rather a refinement of existing technology. His instruments allowed for greater detail and accuracy, leading to significant discoveries in astronomy and physics. The telescope's impact was not solely due to its novelty, but rather its ability to build upon existing knowledge.

The development of science is not a sudden, revolutionary event, but rather a gradual process of discovery and refinement. The story of science is not one of individual geniuses, but rather the cumulative efforts of many individuals over time.

My mother, a member of the Communist Party with a long history in China, received a surprise order from party officials to relocate to the United States when I was just four to five months old. At the time, her husband was imprisoned, and that was all she knew.

For several weeks, she was under house arrest in Jiangxia, Harbin, or one of its satellite cities. The government aimed to break the monopoly on power by sending citizens from Communist states to the West to join workers' co-operatives. During her trip, my mother had to sign an agreement with the government, agreeing not to visit Hong Kong and returning to Jiangxia. She was subsequently sent to a labor camp in Hanyi, Hebei province, where she contracted malaria. After being discharged, she continued to work as a cook and maid before eventually leaving the country and moving to the United States.

2. A shared hometown, perhaps?

As a child, we were allowed to share our names, occupations, and even have our picture taken with our parents. Growing up in a city, we naturally learned about the area through stories and pictures. It was almost a requirement to discuss the places we lived and the people we met.

We were also taught that we came from the same place, simply by looking at each other.

3. No formal surnames in our generation

In China, most of our generation (around 95%) do not have last names. In fact, most of us don't even know how to refer to our parents by their family surname. My mother would often address my brother and me as "we" or "me," even when we were together. It was considered impolite to call someone "you" without a family surname. However, our parents would call each other by names we were used to calling them, but never given. For example, my mother would call her parents "Ming" (mother), "Bian" (father), and "Lao" (brother). This usage is a typical Chinese way of expressing affection.

Every country faces challenges, and China is no exception. In recent years, I've heard people discuss their love for China and its vastness and population. Here's an example of another way people talk about China: "Our life is so big, and so many choices are available to us!"

As I grew up, I was captivated by the film "The Day the Earth Stood Still," which sparked my fascination with the world we inhabit. The movie's exploration of natural disasters and their impact on the planet has stayed with me. It's essential to acknowledge that earthquakes are an inherent part of life on Earth, resulting from geological causes, some predictable and others unpredictable.

The film's dialogue resonated with me, particularly the USGS earthquake monitoring network's detection of the first wave of earthquakes in the San Francisco Bay Area on January 26, 2010. This event was linked to fracking and the resulting wastewater disposal. However, the true story is more extensive.

Fracking, the process of injecting fluids into the ground, can trigger earthquakes. The pressurized fluid can increase the pressure to the point of a quake, potentially triggered at the pressurized part of the well. One earthquake can trigger a chain reaction, causing another quake, and so on, resulting in a cycle of quakes. Each new quake is followed by the energy of the previous quake spreading, causing even larger quakes and potentially a tsunami.

It's crucial to understand the natural cycle of earthquakes and their potential connection to fracking. The USGS classifies these "induced earthquakes" as a natural part of life on Earth. An earthquake and tsunami could have far-reaching consequences, affecting the entire country and potentially the world.

However, this natural cycle is not something we should ignore. There is growing evidence of fracking contaminating groundwater from hydraulic fracturing sites in the American West. These chemicals could increase the risk of earthquakes. If we comprehend how fracking impacts the groundwater supply chain, we can better understand why we are still living in a nuclear winter and how to prevent it.

Fracking is not limited to the US; the rest of the world is beginning to take notice. What could be a global disaster is something local communities are working hard to overcome. California, with its many oil and gas producers, is one of the most educated counties in the US.

As an example, the Sierra Blanca area in the Bay Area is a microcosm of the rest of California. It's home to oil industry companies and a growing population of people affected by fracking. In January 2013, a small group formed Friends of the Earth San Francisco to educate communities and the public about fracking and its potential impacts on our water supply.

We're hosting events to educate the public about the risks associated with fracking. We want everyone in San Francisco to be aware that fracking can happen in their backyard, so we need to become informed and educate ourselves. This will be essential if we want to protect our water supply from being drained.

As part of our ongoing research into the impact of fracking on the water supply of the West Coast, we've been trying to answer the question, "what's next?"

After a year of research, we've discovered that the next threat to American democracy is fracking.

The recent months have witnessed a significant surge in Chinese students departing for Britain, with figures from the Chinese Education and Research Board indicating that this trend is unprecedented in the modern era.

In the first half of 2013, approximately 16,000 Chinese undergraduates opted to pursue studies in science, technology, and engineering at UK universities. This represents a notable increase of 10 percentage points over the course of the academic year.

These students are primarily drawn to the UK due to Beijing's emphasis on equipping its young people with expertise in a wide range of technical fields, as well as access to world-class research institutions.

In a recent development, the Chinese Education and Research Board launched the "China Science and Technology Talent Charter", a document outlining the country's strategy for securing a position for its future leaders in cutting-edge research.

Under this charter, Chinese students are expected to achieve a minimum score of 80% in a specific subject, and China must attract at least 500% of the best undergraduate talent.

Students who return to China for the autumn term are expected to resume their studies the following year. The number of Chinese students departing for the UK and the US has consistently increased since 2005, as China's economy has grown, but this year has seen a notable surge.

The board stated that this influx is the largest since 1995, following the devaluation of the yuan.

China's education minister, Yuan Guiren, hailed the charter as a vital document for China, emphasizing the country's ambition to become a global hub for science and engineering expertise.

"We believe that a global education sector requires a strong academic foundation," Mr. Yuan said. "We are eager to learn from your experiences and promote science and technology education worldwide."

China will continue to collaborate with international scientific and academic institutions to share its expertise in science and technology education.

"We will continue to develop our education and training system to enhance the abilities of talented students pursuing careers in science, technology, and innovation," Mr. Yuan added.

One Chinese graduate, Liu Zhicheng, has already achieved success in the US, receiving the prestigious Rhodes scholarship, which aims to improve students' life chances.

A British Council spokesperson noted that there is currently no evidence to suggest that the UK's higher education record has been negatively impacted by the increased numbers of Chinese students.

It remains unclear whether the exodus is linked to the announcement that China has established a state-owned technology university in Shanghai and launched a joint venture with Shanghai Pudong University, both offering degrees in science, technology, and engineering.

The universities, China Academy of Sciences and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, are the first joint ventures between Chinese and foreign institutions, designed to provide students with a global education and cater to those aspiring to become business leaders, engineers, or doctors.

China Academy of Sciences has set a benchmark for future research with its five-year national research plan, aimed at making China a world leader in research into medical and technological breakthroughs.

The Shanghai Academy of Sciences is another Chinese university that has gained international recognition.

Chinese academics make up less than 2% of the academic staff at a handful of universities worldwide. It is hoped that their efforts will be recognized and promoted by British institutions. Britain has already established partnerships with both Shanghai Jiao Tong University and the CAS. The former will utilize its vast resources, while CAS will establish new research centers. A new £50 million China Engineering Research Centre will be opened in Manchester.

British universities are also becoming increasingly attractive to Chinese students seeking to pursue research. Over 130 Chinese universities, including the prestigious Tsinghua University in Beijing, applied to the British Council to offer places to foreign students. The chosen universities were selected by an academic panel comprising academics from 10 British universities.

In the era of digital media, the concept of personal relationships with consumed content has gained significant traction. However, the pressing issue of piracy has garnered relatively little attention. This is unsurprising, given the complexity of accurately quantifying the scale of piracy.

The piracy industry has faced significant setbacks in recent years. Initially, some legitimate business models, such as BitTorrent, gained popularity. However, these services have since become largely irrelevant. Meanwhile, discussions around creating a new business model for entertainment distribution have been ongoing.

The challenge lies in addressing the needs of various stakeholders. Piracy is pervasive, and the entertainment industry must maintain a substantial support infrastructure to remain afloat. Despite efforts to improve their business, the industry will always need to allocate resources to support operations and maintain revenue streams.

The entertainment industry cannot eradicate piracy solely out of spite; it is a reality that affects nearly every industry and business. There are individuals who pirate content to support their music collections, while others do so for profit. These hardcore pirates are most invested in piracy and will be disproportionately affected by restrictions on distribution.

The estimated number of pirates exceeds 2.5 billion people, who collectively spend over $500 billion annually. If a significant portion of these individuals were to participate in the digital entertainment industry, they would represent a market larger than the combined GDP of the United States and Japan.

To sustain the current digital entertainment industry, the entertainment industry would need to allocate every cent of its profit to customers. This would require nearly every penny in revenue and profit. The primary motivation for many pirates is profitability, as they invest in expensive equipment and software to facilitate piracy.

Calculating the direct savings for legal consumers is challenging, but estimates suggest a daily savings of $1 to $7. If this were the sole source of the entertainment industry's profit, many employees would struggle to survive.

Piracy is a critical component of the current business model, making it difficult for the entertainment industry to cut support staff due to financial constraints. Most pirates are not concerned with artists' profits; they prioritize earning a living and investing in their equipment. Similarly, the film and music industries focus on generating revenue rather than ensuring artists' profitability.

The majority of those who consume pirated content enjoy it, but do not wish to pay for it. They are aware of the piracy industry and support it through content purchases. Without allocating a significant portion of its profit, the entertainment industry would struggle to maintain its current workforce, leading to a snowball effect and financial crisis.

The entertainment industry has a choice in responding to the growth of digital distribution. It can opt for the traditional approach, paying customers and supporting a larger workforce, or adopt a new strategy that prioritizes efficiency and profitability.

A significant number of individuals in the United States and Mexico are estimated to be carriers of the hepatitis C virus, which remains present on their skin as a chronic condition.

The majority of these patients receive a single injection of sofosbuvir every six months, according to Dr. Robert D. Grant, head of the Hepatitis B program at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health in Baltimore, Md.

Ensuring the integrity of the drug's active ingredient is the primary challenge in ensuring the drug's efficacy.

Concurrently, researchers are developing antiviral drugs that could be utilized to address infections related to hepatitis C without sofosbuvir, as presented at a recent hepatitis B conference in California.

"Hepatitis-B-related infections are currently incurable, as current treatments often yield limited benefits," said Thomas J. Frieden, director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

In the past year, at least 10,000 Americans who came into contact with an infected person or one who had the virus transmitted to them have become infected, officials report.

In many cases, patients are unaware of their infection.

In 2010, two men from Iowa traveled to South Africa to collect wild rhesus monkeys for a circus exhibit. One of the men, an undocumented immigrant from Mexico, experienced an unusual relapse after taking a medication that would normally suppress his immune response, causing his body to reject other prescribed medications. The man ultimately spent two and a half years in prison on a felony charge of illegal entry into a country.

To prevent another outbreak, the National Institutes of Health plans to invest between $100 million and $150 million over five years in developing a new drug that can effectively target hepatitis C in humans.

The goal is to create a regimen that would provide patients with two or three months of treatment with a single injection of antiviral drugs, administered every six to 12 months. "We are developing antiviral medications that are safe and effective for treating all types of hepatitis C," said Dr. Michael R. Osterholm of the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis.

Osterholm emphasized that individuals with chronic hepatitis B should not be prescribed one-time doses of sofosbuvir, regardless of its impact on the patient. Instead, physicians should work with patients to develop a personalized treatment plan.

Scientists are still uncertain whether newer drugs like saquinavir and pegylated interferon have any significant advantages over preexposure prophylaxis, a regimen that involves taking antiviral drugs before exposure to prevent infection.

In 2011, the NIH announced a new drug called nelfinavir or pelfinavir, an inhibitor of a cellular liver enzyme called protease. That drug had never been tested in humans before.

Several researchers stated earlier this year that pelfinavir is safer than sofosbuvir. However, because the drug is based on a cellular enzyme, it can affect any liver cells, including normal cells and those that are damaged.

"It is likely to be more of a toxicity issue if you are a liver cell. That said, if I were going to tell someone who has hepatitis C to take a drug that causes toxicity or liver injury while being on treatment, I would recommend that they not take that drug," he said.

"I think it's still too early to say whether or not that drug is better than sofosbuvir," he added.

The National Institute on Drug Abuse in Bethesda, Md., and the NIH's National Center for Research Resources in Rockville, Maryland, are leading the work on developing drug-resistant strains of hepatitis C that threaten to cripple hepatitis treatment efforts worldwide.

The new drugs could also impact efforts to develop medications to combat other infectious diseases, such as tuberculosis.

Scientists need to find a safe and effective way to target the proteases involved in the virus' attack on the liver, said Dr. Robert A. Green of Harvard Medical School. He stated that this process has become a major area of research, but "there hasn't been much progress."

Some scientists are also concerned that infected patients with untreated hepatitis C may transmit the virus to others. So far, there are no reliable tests to determine if HIV infection is a risk for hepatitis C.

In the U.S., drug-related deaths due to hepatitis C, mostly in patients under age 50, are much rarer than deaths caused by hepatitis A, a strain that can be spread only through blood or body fluids.

Researchers estimate that 10 percent of people with chronic hepatitis C are infected with hepatitis A, while 25 percent are infected with both viruses.

The Art of Safeguarding Your Digital Assets

Backing up your digital treasures can be a tedious and time-consuming endeavor. Nevertheless, it's crucial to protect your data from unforeseen calamities. You can opt for a comprehensive backup and restoration process, storing your files in cloud storage, local hard drives, or network storage.

Some crucial considerations to keep in mind:

When conducting manual backups, ensure you have a complete backup containing all your digital assets. Plan to backup at least one drive, but be prepared to backup up to three copies of your data.

When creating snapshots, utilize automatic-flipping functionality or incremental backups from disk.

Cloud Storage vs. Local Storage

By default, your app assumes the latest version is the most current. This assumption has several benefits:

You won't need to manually update your app's versions; simply perform a manual backup and restore to the latest version.

You can be confident that your digital assets will always be backed up, and changes made since the last backup won't impact your update experience.

However, this approach may lead to issues. If you want your app to update automatically, you'll need to periodically create and check out new versions on your own hardware. It's essential to create and check out backups regularly.

Creating a Backup

To initiate a backup, navigate to Settings -> Backup & reset. Click on File -> Back up and then click Next.

On the subsequent screen, you can specify the interval for backing up your files. You can set a minimum interval of 30 minutes per backup, which is useful for automated backups. Alternatively, you can specify a longer interval.

Once you've set the minimum interval, click Continue. On the next screen, select the location where you'd like to store your backed-up files. You can choose local drives, network storage, or cloud services. You can also backup to multiple locations, which is helpful if you have multiple apps.

Click Next to specify a folder for your backup. This folder will contain all your backed-up files. You can also choose to create a backup folder that will store all your files in a single location.

When you're finished, click Finish.

Your app updates will be backed up to the specified location. The file backup process may take some time, depending on the number of files you have and how many times you've saved files to that location.

Restoring a Backup

To restore a backup, navigate to Settings -> Backup & reset -> Restoring a backup. Scroll down and select the backup you'd like to restore. You can choose to restore a backup made at a different time or select a different backup location.

On the next screen, select the backup location to restore. When you click Restore, you'll be taken to the previous screen where you can choose the app you'd like to use to restore your backup.

Language diversity is a fascinating topic, and it's often surprising to learn just how many languages are spoken around the world. While some people might assume that only a few languages are widely spoken, the reality is that there are many more. In fact, the world is home to a staggering number of languages, each with its own unique characteristics and cultural significance.

One of the most interesting aspects of language is the concept of language families. A language family refers to a group of languages that are related to one another through a common ancestor. For example, the Indo-European language family includes languages such as English, Spanish, and French, which are all descended from a common ancestral language. Similarly, the Dravidian language family includes languages such as Tamil and Telugu, which are also related to one another.

But what about the geographical distribution of languages? Are there certain regions where only one language is spoken, or are there areas where multiple languages coexist? The answer is that languages can be found in all parts of the world, and they often overlap with one another in complex ways. For instance, some languages may be spoken in a particular region, while others may be spoken in nearby areas. This can make it challenging to identify the exact boundaries between different language families.

So, how many languages are there in the world? Estimates vary widely, but some linguists believe that there may be as many as 100,000 languages. This number is likely an underestimate, as many languages are spoken by small groups of people and may not be well-documented.

In terms of the relationship between languages, linguists have identified several key patterns. For example, many languages share similar grammatical structures and vocabulary, which suggests that they may have evolved from a common ancestral language. Additionally, languages often change over time due to contact with other languages, which can result in the borrowing of words and grammatical structures.

Finally, what can linguists learn about a language by studying its grammar and vocabulary? The answer is that they can learn a great deal. By analyzing the grammar and vocabulary of a language, linguists can gain insights into its history, cultural context, and relationships with other languages. This can be a powerful tool for understanding the complexities of language and its role in shaping human culture.

Battery Backup Systems: A Comprehensive Overview

The concept of battery backup systems has gained significant attention in recent times. In essence, these devices serve as a backup power source for your electronic devices, ensuring uninterrupted operation in case of a power outage or failure. A battery backup system typically consists of a rechargeable battery and an electronic device, often referred to as an "e-couple," which connects to the device being powered.

The battery backup system works by recharging the batteries of your electronic devices, ensuring a seamless transition between the primary and backup power sources. This feature is particularly useful for devices that require frequent recharging, such as laptops and portable devices.

Types of Battery Backup Systems

There are two primary types of battery backup systems: power-on-standby and pump-backup devices. Power-on-standby devices automatically charge each battery in the system, even when the device is turned off. This feature is crucial for laptops and portable devices that require frequent recharging.

Pump-backup devices, on the other hand, are designed to recharge batteries in devices that do not have an internal battery backup system. These devices are typically installed in the battery compartment of the device and recharge the batteries as needed.

Benefits of Battery Backup Systems

Battery backup systems offer several benefits, including:

1. Uninterrupted Operation: Battery backup systems ensure that your devices continue to operate even in the event of a power outage or failure.
2. Reduced Downtime: By providing a backup power source, battery backup systems minimize downtime and ensure that your devices remain operational.
3. Increased Reliability: Battery backup systems increase the reliability of your devices by providing a backup power source in case of a primary power failure.

Conclusion

In conclusion, battery backup systems are an essential component of any electronic device. By providing a backup power source, these systems ensure uninterrupted operation and reduce downtime. Whether you're using a laptop, portable device, or other electronic device, a battery backup system can provide peace of mind and ensure that your devices remain operational.

Step One: Understand Your Characters

As a romance writer, I'd like to clarify that this post is about characters and plot. To put it simply, each of my stories revolves around the characters, not the plot itself. A character is essentially a perspective within a story. For example, if an author has two main characters, one in the same city and one in another, they become "the story." The city where the story takes place is the setting, and the scene is unfolding between these two characters in that city. Think of your character's name as a representation of the story, and you'll get the idea. My own books focus on the city where the story unfolds, but there's always a secondary city that's also part of the story.

A good starting question for writing a story is, "Who/what is the protagonist?" Your main character is the one who starts the story and leads the way. She tells the story, and other characters might be interesting, but they never become leading characters. They're simply viewpoint characters - the other people in the story. There's no such thing as a leading character; someone is only considered the main character by people within the story.

The first step in crafting a good story is to understand the characters and not let them control the narrative. As soon as you do that, you'll find it difficult to let go of the story, even if you love the character. But as soon as they control the story, the character becomes too close, just like a friend you can't leave, even though you want them to.

A good writer never lets anyone be the main character, so all that's left is the conflict and resolution.

The writer should say, "I'm writing the story of these people, not their story, and not some of them," and "Not as a leader does the character act or talk," and "I'm not making them into who they really are, but I'm making them into what they're like when they're just normal people in your story."

Don't just write everything you see in your mind. Don't write in your own head first. That's why sometimes people who start with a good idea are surprised when it doesn't work out; they think they've already done it.

In the early days of my fiction writing, I thought of stories as collections of scenes. The Concept of Web Sockets

Web Sockets operate on the principle of establishing a persistent, bi-directional connection between a client and a server. This connection allows for the exchange of data in real-time, enabling applications to send and receive updates as they occur. Web Sockets are often used in conjunction with other technologies, such as HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, to create immersive and interactive user experiences.

Benefits of Web Sockets

Web Sockets offer several benefits over traditional HTTP-based communication protocols. For instance, they enable real-time updates, allowing applications to respond quickly to user interactions. Additionally, Web Sockets can handle large amounts of data and support multiple connections simultaneously, making them an ideal choice for applications that require high-performance and scalability.

Implementing Web Sockets

To implement Web Sockets, you'll need to establish a connection between a client and a server using a Web Socket library or framework. Once connected, you can send and receive data using the Web Socket protocol. Web Sockets can be used with a variety of programming languages, including JavaScript, Python, and Ruby.

Conclusion

Web Sockets are a powerful tool for real-time data transfer, enabling applications to communicate with each other in a bi-directional and persistent manner. By leveraging the benefits of Web Sockets, developers can create innovative and engaging applications that provide a seamless user experience.

According to the report, OBG led to a notable enhancement in border security. Following OBG, the Customs and Border Protection (CBP) deployed additional resources to the Southwest border, increased staffing, established an intelligence unit, and set up a joint intelligence center in El Paso. In September 2012, the DHS announced the deployment of additional personnel to the Southwest border to augment efforts.

These developments have led to an uptick in border patrol activities at the Southwest border, resulting in a significant increase in apprehensions from May 2012 to April 2013. Although apprehensions decreased in 2012, they surged in 2013, with enhanced resources and manpower contributing to arrests in both sectors. Notably, apprehension rates remain high on Mexico's border with the United States.

Achieving the results of OBG in the near term appears unlikely, given the complex factors influencing long-term success. However, this analysis will examine the key factors contributing to the DHS's ability to secure the Southwest border.

The analysis is based on data from Fiscal Year 2011 and the U.S.-Mexico Border Data, published by the Department of Homeland Security.

Factors enhancing security on the Southwest border

Firstly, the CBP should maintain its overtime work and increase its security presence in the Rio Grande Valley Sector (RGV), particularly the Rio Grande Valley Sector South (RGV-S). The areas north of the Rio Grande River have consistently been the most active border sectors since OBG began in March 2011. Recent increases in activity have been observed in areas where CBP personnel would normally be deploying to secure the northern border.

Secondly, the CBP should enhance its manpower by deploying personnel capable of providing more than just security in the Rio Grande Valley Sector. CBP personnel should collaborate with Border Patrol, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and the Department of Public Safety (DPS) to improve areas where Border Patrol personnel are deployed. This involves training for Border Patrol personnel to increase border security presence and improving capacity in sectors other than the Sierra Madre Occidental sector.

Thirdly, CBP personnel should continue to enhance collaboration with ICE and DHS to increase interoperability and information sharing. Increased information sharing will create a greater potential for the U.S. government to respond to border security threats. As the number of CBP agents has risen, there has been an increase in information sharing with ICE and DHS. However, the U.S. government has been slow to share information about individuals in the country illegally.

Fourthly, CBP should develop and implement a more comprehensive biographic and biometric immigration system and a more centralized and consolidated border system. These systems should provide all information about a person's immigration status, including their criminal history, prior arrest, and work authorization. CBP could also take steps to enhance its response to the increasing use of "dynamic entry" techniques, such as the practice of bringing undocumented immigrants into the U.S. on aircraft, boats, and other vessels.

Lastly, CBP should strengthen its coordination with other agencies, including Customs and Border Protection (CBP), to ensure adequate information exchange and prevent unauthorized access.

A coalition of prominent legal experts has written to the Office of Inspector General to express their concerns regarding the recent report on the Justice Department's practices. The experts, who represent a broad spectrum of legal and public interest groups, argue that the report's findings demonstrate that the department's problems are rooted in policy and implementation rather than in a cultural issue.

The experts point out that the Justice Department has been using an "affirmative consent" strategy to ensure that police stop, search, and arrest people of color at higher rates than individuals of a different race, with troubling consequences for public safety. They also note that the department has been overly reliant on data from the Bureau of Justice Statistics, which they consider questionable.

The experts' letter was published ahead of a public hearing before the House Judiciary Committee, which is holding two hearings on the report. The witnesses testifying in both hearings include three members of the current IG team and three members of the investigative staff for the DOJ's Office of the Inspector General, who have been critical of the Justice Department's failure to adequately investigate and address systemic problems within the criminal justice system.

The report's findings include several concerning issues, such as the Department of Justice's Office of Community Oriented Policing Services' inability to obtain and report its own internal data, the Office of Justice Programs' inadequate data to ensure fair grants, and the Bureau of Justice Statistics' cessation of collecting data on police stops. The report also highlights the DOJ's Civil Rights Division's pattern or practice of targeting people based on their race, as well as the department's failure to provide legal representation to those charged with crimes.

The experts urge the Justice Department to take immediate steps to ensure that its COPS/CRIME personnel adhere to department policy and provide legal representation to individuals subject to arrest.

In daily life, our bodies have a natural defense system against viruses, bacteria, and other microorganisms. However, certain diseases, such as cancer, don't have a straightforward immune response. Instead, the body's own cells can malfunction and attack healthy tissues.

Cancer is a complex disease, and its causes are multifaceted. While some cancers are linked to viral or bacterial infections, others have unknown or disputed origins. For instance, colon cancer might be caused by certain viruses, whereas pancreatic cancer could be linked to bacterial infections. Other types of cancer, like melanoma and leukemia, were initially thought to be caused by viruses but are now believed to result from a combination of factors, including lifestyle choices or genetic predispositions.

The key differences between cancer caused by viruses, bacteria, or the immune system lie in their symptoms. Here are some common signs of cancer caused by a virus, bacteria, or the immune system:

Our immune system plays a crucial role in fighting cancer. It produces antibodies that target and destroy cancer cells, both during and after tumor growth. These antibodies can also be used to treat cancer in other parts of the body.

Cancer cells can develop resistance to chemotherapy treatments or exhibit unique mechanisms of resistance, making it challenging for the body to eliminate them. In some cases, cancer cells can become resistant to multiple chemotherapy regimens.

The immune system can inadvertently strengthen cancer cells, leading to the development of drug-resistant cancer. If you exhibit any of these characteristics, your cancer might be resistant to treatment or even the immune system itself.

Cancer is not a natural part of the aging process. It usually results from genetic mutations in normal cells. However, in some cases, the body's own cells can develop cancer due to these mutations. Certain types of cancer, such as breast cancer, are not caused by DNA mutations but by other factors, including hormonal changes.

Cancer of the colon can involve genetic mutations, but they can also be triggered by environmental toxins, poor lifestyle habits, or a combination of these factors. In some cases, cancer may develop as a result of a drug-resistant cancer effect.

There is a higher likelihood of developing metastasis, the spread of cancer cells, especially in cases of melanoma. Many genes associated with cancer have been identified, but others require advanced research to determine their significance. These genetic characteristics may be crucial in understanding the tumor but are not always used in cancer diagnosis.

I was born in a predominantly African American neighborhood during a period of economic downturn. My upbringing was deeply influenced by my Catholic community, and I was baptized and raised Catholic until I turned 18. As I entered my 20s, I began to question the existence of a higher power.

My parents, a World War II Army Captain and a Catholic school teacher, instilled in me a sense of skepticism towards organized religion. However, a chance encounter with someone from a strict evangelical background marked a significant turning point in my life during the late 1960s.

In the mid-1960s, I stumbled upon a book titled "The Mystery of Eternal Life: A Personal Faith Statement" published by the Association of Baptists in America. I read the book multiple times, which sparked a deeper understanding of the concept of God.

This realization led me to dedicate myself to helping others in my community comprehend the existence of God. Despite being deeply in debt, I took out loans to fund my first ministry. My first church was a Catholic parish in a struggling neighborhood in Minneapolis. During my brief tenure, a man approached me, expressing interest in joining the church, which prompted me to study Catholic theology. I was shocked by what I learned.

I pursued a PhD in theology and philosophy at Saint Mary's University, where I read extensively on the concept of God and the Bible. In 1976, I presented my thesis on the existence of God to a Catholic faculty, criticizing their theology as "absurd."

During the 1970-1983 period, I served as the lead pastor of my church, while the Catholic faculty at St. Mary's developed a distinct philosophy for serving and teaching their students. I became an active member of the Committee on Catholic Concerns of the Archdiocese of Chicago, speaking at nearly every Catholic parish in the city. My life was publicly scrutinized, and I became a prominent figure in the Catholic media.

When approached by the press for interviews, I initially hesitated but eventually wrote about God in the Catholic weekly magazine, Catholic Perspectives. I became increasingly concerned about the lack of teaching within the Catholic Church. This would ultimately lead to my departure from the Catholic community – I transitioned to a career in journalism.

In early 1981, the Catholic newspaper of the Archdiocese of Chicago published a statement advocating for a change in how they approach those who disagree with them. One aspect of the statement I couldn't endorse was the notion that Catholic teaching on the existence of God should not be subject to dialogue with those who are not convinced of its reality or value.

This sparked a warning from the Catholic hierarchy, and in 1982, we issued another statement declaring that Catholic teaching is not open to dialogue with the atheist and agnostic community. When the statement was published, I was asked to respond, but I declined. Unbeknownst to me, the Pope was not willing to tolerate this stance. The Bishop of Rome issued a declaration, calling upon me to issue an apology. I apologized for the statement but refused to issue a formal apology.

A week later, I received word that I was suspended from my position as editor of Catholic Perspectives due to this controversy. I was on a plane to Rome at the time, and I was subsequently fired. The Archbishop of Chicago, the highest administrative position I held, informed me that I was expected to attend daily Mass and read the Mass every day.

I spoke with the Pope three days before my firing, and he revealed a plan for me: to appear on television, stating "I stand by my statement," and receive praise from the news media. Three years later, he became the Pope, and I met him for the first time in Rome, marking my first encounter with a non-Catholic in a public setting.

Representative Jeb Hensarling from Texas and Representative Jared Polis from Colorado have introduced the CARERS Act, which would permit the distribution of marijuana for medical purposes and its recreational use by individuals aged 21 and above.

The proposed legislation would establish a commission to examine state policies that align with federal law. A state could also legalize marijuana for recreational use if it is deemed commercially viable and has received voter approval in the preceding federal election.

Both lawmakers emphasized that the bill does not necessarily imply that medical marijuana use would be legal in their respective states. However, they argued that federal authorities should not hinder states from exploring the possibility of legalizing marijuana.

Hensarling stated, "If states wish to consider this option, that's perfectly fine. If states, including my home state of Texas, believe this could be a success for their economy, they should explore it."

Polis added, "I'd rather focus on obtaining a comprehensive drug policy approved by Congress than worrying about what some random congressman from Alaska thinks. I think I speak for other members of Congress when I say it would be detrimental to Texas if this proposal were to come forward in Texas."

The bill aims to address the long-standing polarization on drug policy in Congress, where Republicans have traditionally opposed marijuana legalization and Democrats have generally supported it. However, in recent years, Democrats have shifted their stance on drug policy in response to the country's growing heroin epidemic.

This week, the chairman of the Senate Appropriations Committee is considering a $400 million bill that would fund law enforcement by reducing the Drug Enforcement Agency's budget. A majority of Americans express concerns about the impact of income inequality on their country, but many have yet to connect some of the causes to the actions of their elected leaders, according to a recent report from the Pew Research Center.


The study, released last week, found that 58% of adults believe income inequality is the most pressing issue facing the US today, while 48% identified it as one of eight major concerns. However, only 37% of Americans link these issues to the decisions made by their individual elected representatives.


The findings come as lawmakers consider a proposal to increase the minimum wage and a series of budget measures that would boost funding for programs benefiting low- and middle-income Americans. A separate Pew estimate revealed that the median US household has less than $10,000 in savings, leaving them vulnerable to financial instability.


The gap between the wealthy and the rest has grown significantly over recent decades, with the top 10% of US households holding nearly 85% of total wealth in 2013 (a figure that has since decreased to 80%). While income inequality was a key concern during the Occupy Wall Street protests, it remains a secondary issue in American life, according to Pew data.


In his State of the Union address, President Barack Obama described income inequality as a "serious problem" affecting not only the middle class but also poor and working families nationwide. The Congressional Budget Office concluded that raising the minimum wage to $10.10 would lift 400,000 workers out of poverty and reduce family income by about $4,000, although other research has found that lifting pay above the current $7.25 minimum wage would increase the number of people who would work but struggle to afford basic necessities.


Pew estimated that 55% of Americans overall view rising income inequality as a major problem facing the country. While the percentage of people identifying such a problem has increased by 13 percentage points since 2006, the share of Americans citing higher inequality as a major concern has actually declined slightly since 2007.


Some 70% of Americans identified reducing inequality as a top concern, according to the results of an online panel of over 50,000 Americans. This figure is significantly higher than the 49% of Americans who identified rising income inequality as the country's big economic problem in mid-October. A separate Pew survey conducted in January and February found that 49% of Americans were more concerned with income inequality than with unemployment.

We reported on Sunday morning that Facebook quietly discontinued the "sponsored stories" feature, its primary source of revenue, following allegations of overly aggressive advertising. Since then, the social network has been distributing an updated notification to its marketing partners:

We appreciate your efforts in making sense of your ad campaigns. The sponsored ads feature has been removed from the Facebook Ads Manager dashboard, and the sponsored stories feature has been removed from the Facebook Ads Management Tools. A dedicated team focused on advertising-related issues will continue to support Facebook advertisers, ensuring they maximize the value of their ads. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

However, this was not the complete story.

Understanding the Disappearance of Sponsored Stories

To comprehend why the "sponsored stories" feature is disappearing, it is essential to grasp the fundamentals of Facebook's Audience Network system.

Facebook's Audience Network is a platform that enables marketers to target their ads across a vast array of Facebook users, as well as push their ads directly to those users. However, Facebook also sells tools to target that very audience exclusively, where advertisers can only access them with specific accounts or advertisers. This decision was made in August, coinciding with the removal of the "sponsored stories" tool.

The removal of "sponsored stories" and the Audience Network is Facebook's response to this situation. The company aims to incentivize users to engage more actively with ads by doing a bit more work (such as making a purchase), rather than simply clicking on ads.

If that is the case, why isn't Facebook allowing everyone to add the Audience Network as part of the Ad Manager tools?

The Role of Sponsored Stories

Facebook's primary source of revenue from sponsored posts is ads displayed on sponsored stories, which makes sense given its business model. The company receives a share of the revenue from the ads it displays, so it is logical that Facebook would want to use the "sponsored stories" tool as part of this process.

However, it is also possible that Facebook is simply attempting to utilize its data about its users more effectively, targeting users with the most relevant ads.

"If Facebook has been generating less than half of its revenues from sponsored stories, it may be more prudent to reduce the share of revenues from that area," said Chris Chabris, director of product at Facebook. "However, we are seeing the same level of engagement with video content as ever, and a high ratio of users clicking on ads on Facebook. Therefore, on average, we are spending more money on advertising on Facebook than our rival, YouTube."

If this is the case, it may make sense for Facebook to integrate the Audience Network into the Ad Manager, allowing the company to learn more about its users and generate more revenue from advertising.

Of course, there is an obvious implication to this: If Facebook kills the Audience Network, it will also eliminate any ability advertisers have to target ads at specific audiences on the social network, just one more example of how Facebook is attempting to reduce what its users see.

We have reached out to Facebook for further information and will update this post as we receive more answers.

AUSTIN, Texas - The US Supreme Court has agreed to review a challenge to Texas' voter ID law, a contentious measure that has sparked debate over its impact on voter participation.

As the December election approached, over 7 million Texans were registered to vote, according to Texas Secretary of State Rolando Pablos. The number of voters without valid identification in Texas increased by around 20% between 2012 and 2016, from 6.3 million registered voters to 7.1 million.

The Justice Department has sued to block the law, and Texas has appealed to the nation's highest court to restore it.

The Justice Department has challenged other voting restrictions imposed at the state level, arguing they disproportionately affect minority voters, including Hispanics, who tend to support Democratic candidates.

The court will consider whether a photo identification law with strict requirements, such as a concealed carry permit or a Social Security card, is an effective means of preventing voter fraud or a form of voter suppression. Voting rights advocates argue that these restrictions unfairly target minority voters.

Texas was the first state to enact a requirement that voters show photo identification. The law also requires citizens to be assigned a voting district.

The American Civil Liberties Union challenged the law in federal court. A six-member panel of the US Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit rejected the government's case against the law last month.

In the appeal, US Solicitor General Donald Verrilli argued that the US Constitution guarantees the right to vote and requires equal protection.

"It is clear from the record that the challenged laws, particularly the photo ID law, are neutral or substantially related factors in reducing the opportunity for Texas eligible voters to participate in elections," Verrilli said.

The Justice Department has said the voting laws disproportionately affect Latino, African-American, and young voters who tend to support Democrats. A Justice Department report last year found that a photo ID law was enacted in 27 states that would have an impact of one to three percentage points.

Under the Texas law, voters must present a driver's license, state-issued ID card, passport, tribal ID card, or US military photo ID - including one bearing a date of birth that is not more than 10 years old - to cast a ballot.

It does not require an original signature on a registration or a photocopied signature. It does not permit use of a concealed handgun or a special photo identification card issued by a county sheriff.

Those who do not have such ID could apply for a free voter registration card or voter ID card from the state.

Texas has said the law would help combat fraud, particularly voter impersonation.

"Voter ID is crucial to ensuring the integrity of our elections," said a state Republican Party spokesman. The state has estimated 3 million illegal votes were cast in the last two presidential elections.
