The notion that a high-carb diet won't lead to weight gain and that excess carbs will automatically result in weight loss is a widespread misconception. The truth is more nuanced.

In the 1950s, dietician William Davis coined the term "caloric intake" to describe the amount of energy required to maintain weight. Davis believed that the rate of weight gain is directly correlated with the absolute amount of calories consumed. However, this notion has been disproven.

While it's true that not all calories are created equal, some carbs have a greater impact on weight gain than others.

When carbohydrates are introduced, the body's fat metabolism rate increases, leading to a higher rate of glycolysis and lipolysis. This, in turn, causes the body to absorb and burn fat, resulting in weight gain.

When the body loses fat, it does so by breaking down stored glycogen, increasing metabolic rate, and utilizing fat for energy. The rate of fat storage in fat cells also plays a role in weight loss.

Athletes and bodybuilders often experience rapid weight gain due to their high-calorie diets, which typically consist of a low-carb regimen. Conversely, individuals who follow a low-carb diet may experience rapid weight loss as their bodies shift from relying on carbs for energy to burning fat.

Carbohydrates can actually increase fat metabolism, rather than decreasing it. When the body's fat metabolism rate is high, it converts sugar to fatty acids more efficiently, resulting in increased fat storage.

A high rate of glycolysis and lipolysis can also lead to an increase in triglyceride transport across the blood vessels to the liver, potentially resulting in the appearance of fat in the arteries.

To prevent fat deposition and promote weight loss, it's essential to reduce glycogen breakdown and minimize liver fat storage.

While our minds are excellent at predicting outcomes, there are limitations. For instance, we often struggle when faced with uncertainty or a multitude of possibilities.

Consider the mismatch problem, where our expectations clash with reality. In the film A Beautiful Mind, the main character's brother receives a windfall to fund his children's education. The key is to have someone who's seen both movies make a prediction, as the second person can't watch them otherwise.

This problem arises when the probability distribution of two or more events becomes overly smooth over time. Classic examples include the disparity between patient expectations and actual surgical outcomes, as well as the probability distribution of events when one is expected but the other isn't.

Our brains are adept at making predictions in the absence of information, but we often make inaccurate predictions about outcomes. We tend to believe we have information about the future due to news reports or predictions, when in reality, we don't.

One possibility is that our brains use prior beliefs, which are like mental maps, to guide our predictions. These representations are stored in memory and activated when we make predictions. Another possibility is that we draw from our past experiences to inform our predictions, helping us choose among possible outcomes and providing valuable information about what lies ahead.

LIFE IN THE WALT DISNEY UNIVERSE

BY JON SWETTMAN

Walt Disney Studios was a significant player in the 1950s, driven by the creative vision of its founder and a star of international renown. As a young boy, Walt Disney envisioned a whimsical tale of three dwarfs, a dragon, and hidden treasure, a story that would captivate children and inspire their imaginations.

This dream, which ultimately led to the creation of Disneyland, transformed Walt Disney from a wealthy entrepreneur into a global icon. Although his work at the studio may not have been his most celebrated achievement, his influence on the entertainment industry cannot be overstated. It was through his work at this small studio that Walt Disney gained his initial recognition. As this book demonstrates, the Disney empire was built upon an idea that only Walt Disney could have conceived.

The Walt Disney Dream was both a tribute to and a commentary on modern America. As a child in the 1950s, Walt Disney witnessed the rise of his country. With a strong sense of cultural pride, he drew inspiration from his immigrant parents and their experiences in the United States. His father was a prominent figure in the American folk music movement after World War I, and their lives were marked by significant political and cultural upheavals.

Walt Disney's letters from the 1950s reveal his deep appreciation for the United States, describing it as a symbol of universal truth. He believed that even the smallest decisions and actions reflected the country's ideals of individualism, capitalism, and democracy. In his letters to friends, Walt Disney expressed his desire to create stories that captured the essence of the American Dream, a dream that represented hope for a brighter future.

These are just a few of the ideas that drove Walt Disney to create his iconic stories. If these ideas did indeed exist, he would not have been the first individual to recognize them in his daily life.

It's intriguing that Walt Disney's dream of creating a global entertainment empire was built upon a project he believed would give him a deeper understanding of the American Dream. Just a year after his birth, Walt Disney made an unprecedented visit to Hollywood, where he worked at his mother's studio for a brief period before pursuing his dream. Walt Disney was able to make these dreams come true due to the people whose lives he touched while working towards his goal.

The idea of a global entertainment empire had been in the Disney family's minds for over forty years. Walt Disney envisioned a company capable of achieving great things, but he did not dream of building his own empire. From his initial meeting with Harry Lassiter, chief executive of Warner Brothers, Walt Disney gained an understanding that his goal shared more in common with Lassiter's idea of creating "magic" than it did with his own dream of making "great" films for "stupid people." Employee benefits can be valued in various ways, each offering a unique perspective. The cost-to-employer approach focuses on the actual expense incurred by the employer. For instance, if a company spends $500 per month on an employee's health insurance, that's the tangible value of the benefit. The market value method, on the other hand, assesses the benefit based on what an employee would pay if they purchased it independently. Suppose an employee could acquire a comparable health insurance policy for $400 per month on the open market – that would be the market value of the benefit. Meanwhile, the perceived value method considers the employee's subjective assessment of the benefit's worth. For example, an employee might value their employer-provided health insurance at $600 per month because it provides them with a sense of security. It's crucial to recognize that individual employees may assign different values to the same benefit, so it's beneficial to combine these approaches when evaluating employee benefits.

As part of his presidential campaign, Donald Trump made a pledge to the nation, stating that the reinstatement of the death penalty would coincide with the left's renewed optimism. Although this goal appears to be only partially achieved, the left's reaction is not solely due to Trump's victory.

A recent Supreme Court decision has garnered praise from the left, as it unanimously ruled that the death penalty cannot be applied to individuals with mental health issues. While this outcome was not unforeseen, the practice of executing people with mental illnesses has been a contentious topic in the US.

The American Psychiatric Association has acknowledged that the death penalty is disproportionately used against minorities, individuals with mental health issues, and those struggling with substance abuse. While it is generally accepted that mental illness cannot be proven and therefore cannot be a basis for execution, some individuals still believe that mental health and/or mental retardation make individuals suitable for death, regardless of the lack of evidence.

According to the APA, extensive scientific research has demonstrated that many psychiatric conditions can cause behaviors similar to those caused by underlying psychological factors. This highlights the need to determine whether an individual is mentally ill before executing them.

The Supreme Court's decision in McCleskey v. Kemp concluded that the Eighth Amendment prohibits the execution of individuals with mental retardation, as it violates the prohibition against cruel punishments. Additionally, the Court's precedent in Baze v. Rees established that mental retardation was a valid basis for imposing a death sentence.

The left may now be expressing relief at the Court's decision. However, it is more likely that they would be relieved if the Court had ruled otherwise.

The left has consistently advocated for the protection of human life, including that of the LGBT community. While the death penalty may not be part of their political agenda, it is clear that they would not want to be seen as supporting it, regardless of an individual's mental well-being.

It is also important to acknowledge the left's sensitivity towards the mentally ill. The death penalty is often used against minorities and individuals struggling with addiction due to societal views of their perceived moral shortcomings. This means that the death penalty is used to punish individuals for their perceived immorality, rather than their actions. Many of these individuals are unable to control their impulses or thoughts, which is in direct contrast to the Court's decision in McCleskey.

While we do not want to see this issue arise again, we also do not want to see other societies adopt similar death penalty policies. Ultimately, this decision should bring some measure of peace to the LGBT community and society at large, even if it does not prevent the death penalty from being used frequently in the future.

Energy consumption grew 3.3% in 2011, offset by a 1.8% decline in oil demand and a 2.2% increase in global fuel use. Energy usage continued to rise in 2011, driven by increases in Europe and China, but fell in most emerging economies.

In response to these trends, the IEA expects global oil demand to grow by 1.7% in 2012, driven by economic growth in emerging markets and a slowing of the Chinese economy.

Detroit is expecting a surge in visitors this summer, with approximately 80,000 people expected to flock to the city. The report, which is part of the 2017 American Customer Satisfaction Index from Credit Suisse, examines customer satisfaction across various industries. The index is based on responses from 100,000 people, gathered through face-to-face interviews and online surveys in the spring and fall.

Detroit's score came out to be 73.7, which is above the national average of 70.1. This is consistent with previous years, when Detroit ranked among the top cities for customer satisfaction.

The report also found that people in Detroit and the surrounding region were less satisfied with the products they experienced and the way they were treated compared to a decade ago. Younger shoppers, in particular, were less satisfied with the quality of products and services offered.

The study suggests that younger consumers are more focused on price and quality, and have less experience with the product. Older generations, on the other hand, prefer a more traditional line of service and are less satisfied with being treated with respect.

The decline in millennial satisfaction with service in the Detroit metropolitan region since 2010 is consistent with national trends, according to Jodi R. Rinehart, the managing partner at the DIA's Center for Marketing Excellence.

The index also found that millennials were less satisfied with personal assistance while shopping, compared to older customers. They were also less satisfied with finding what they want and need in stores and were less satisfied when they encountered a problem with a product or service.

The survey revealed that the most important products for consumers are apparel, electronics, household devices, and restaurants, with a combined 13% of consumers rating these items as very important.

Consumers are willing to pay extra for quality and personalized service, and Detroit is a great example of this, said David Spillane, the CEO and president of Credit Suisse's Retail Banking Business. With growing demand for quality products and services, Detroit's consumer market has become more competitive, placing the city on course to become the fastest-growing major urban market.

This development will likely be a significant point of conversation in Detroit in the coming months and years.

New research by American scientists reveals that methane, a potent greenhouse gas, is predominantly of natural origin, rather than being released from human activities.

The study, published in Geophysical Research Letters, suggests that the majority of methane emissions globally originate from natural sources, rather than the burning of fossil fuels.

Lead author Thomas Crowther, a geobiologist at Pennsylvania State University, emphasizes that the study's findings indicate that approximately 70% of the methane in the atmosphere is naturally occurring.

The research team created a model combining climate and atmospheric chemistry to determine the sources of methane. By comparing their results with real-life measurements, they found a strong correlation between the two.

The study's conclusions are significant, as they provide insight into the natural sources of methane, which has been a longstanding challenge for scientists. The findings also highlight the need to better understand the natural sources of methane to accurately account for global emissions.

The study's authors suggest that the rapid rise in methane concentrations in recent years is likely driven by natural sources, rather than human activities. Methane is the largest contributor to climate change, and its emissions have been increasing, exacerbating the problem.

The researchers propose several options for measuring methane emissions, including atmospheric measurements and oceanic studies. They chose to focus on the Earth's surface, which minimizes natural leaks and increases accuracy.

The study estimates that approximately 775 billion metric tons of methane are emitted annually, with about 80% coming from natural sources.

Some critics of the study have raised concerns about the methodology, suggesting that the model may have overestimated methane emissions. However, the study's authors maintain that their findings are important for understanding the debate around climate change.

Not everyone agrees with the study's conclusions. John Reilly, an atmospheric scientist at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography, questions the accuracy of the methane emissions estimates, citing concerns about data adjustments.

Despite these differences, the study's findings underscore the importance of understanding natural sources of methane to effectively address climate change.

A groundbreaking study published in Frontiers in Psychology has uncovered a stark reality: nearly 75% of students are reluctant to acknowledge instances of sexual abuse, and more than half of females still deny being victims.

Dr. Julie Wasser, the study's lead researcher, highlights the critical question: "What happens when women report these experiences to medical professionals?"

According to Dr. Wasser, the majority of women yearn for safety when disclosing such experiences to healthcare providers. However, the study reveals a concerning trend: for every individual who denies sexual abuse, there are three who have actually experienced it.

This research was conducted by the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Toronto, in collaboration with esteemed professors from the University of Toronto and Brock University.

Dr. Wasser attributes this phenomenon to the pervasive influence of social media on women's lives. They are frequently exposed to sexualized content, which can lead to the assumption that they must lie about their experiences. This internalized message can be damaging, as it perpetuates the notion that disclosing abuse is undesirable.

The study also found that females often internalize the message that they must be lying when they report sexual abuse. Dr. Wasser emphasizes the importance of changing these mental models and attitudes, suggesting that women should focus on their physical and mental well-being rather than allowing it to define their self-perception and relationships.

The ultimate goal is to adopt a social learning approach, teaching women that sexual assault can affect anyone, regardless of gender. By shifting this perspective, we can reduce the stigma surrounding disclosure and improve women's health outcomes.

Source: Wasser J-A, Kowalska-Tulsa I. Disclosure of sexual abuse history in a nationally representative sample of adults. Front. Psychol. 6:30. Published: 01 May 2017. doi: 10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00330.

A recent study from the University of Toronto reveals that the National Security Agency (NSA) has been secretly monitoring internet activities in Canada, potentially putting global internet freedom at risk. The report, titled "The NSA's Secret Internet: How the US Government Spies on the World Wide Web," examines the extent to which the NSA has been accessing the internet through a "back door" provided by Bell Canada, Canada's largest internet service provider.

The study finds that Bell Canada has been granting the NSA access to its fibre optic connections, allowing the agency to intercept internet communications without a warrant. This has serious implications for internet privacy and security, as it allows the NSA to monitor and collect data on Canadian citizens without their knowledge or consent.

The report notes that the NSA's access to Bell Canada's fibre optic connections has been granted in exchange for the agency's assistance in decrypting communications sent over the internet. This has led to concerns that the NSA is using its access to Bell Canada's network to gather intelligence on Canadian citizens and organizations.

The study's findings are based on a series of communications with Bell Canada, the Communications Security Establishment Canada (CSE), and leading researchers on security. The report also notes that the NSA's activities are shrouded in secrecy, with little transparency or oversight.

The report concludes that the NSA's activities pose a significant threat to internet freedom and privacy, and that the Canadian government must take action to protect its citizens' online activities.

A unique carbon structure has been created by researchers at the University of Illinois's Molecular Foundry. The structure, a small, 3-centimeter thick carbon bubble, is made from graphite or graphene, a two-dimensional form of carbon. Graphite, also known as "white graphene," is the highest quality form of carbon known, and it holds promise for use in future electronics, biomedical devices, and the human body.

The researchers used a collaborative research facility between Illinois and Northwestern University to fabricate transparent, conductive, and rigid carbon nanotubes with different properties, including transparency, toughness, electrochemistry, electrical conductivity, chemical interaction, and mechanical properties.

"This research is the start of a long-standing trend toward making carbon nanotubes with desirable properties in nano-scale systems," said S. Jay Zhang, a professor of mechanical engineering and electrical and computer engineering.

The material's transparency, which allows the properties of the material's molecules to be seen in close-up view, is the highest quality of the research team's research to date. The material achieved its transparency in a simple way that does not add significantly to the price of manufacturing.

The researchers believe that this material could be used in a variety of applications, including new kinds of devices for imaging, sensing, processing information, and communications. The material's strength, flexibility, and transparency make it an attractive option for a range of applications.

The work at the Molecular Foundry was supported by the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science Award DE-FG02-96ER46276 and the Office of Naval Research.

Co-authors included postdoctoral researcher Haejin Han, associate professor of mechanical engineering and electrical, computer engineering and physics; and David J. LeBlanc, the William and Betty H. Zuker Professor of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Science.

The M1910 Colt pistol made its debut in 1910, marking a significant milestone in the company's history. The first production model, the M1910A1, featured a 1 1/7 inch barrel with a removable front sight and a blowback design. This innovative design combined a special magazine with the pistol itself, resulting in a unique and effective firearm. Initially, Colt planned to produce 50,000 units, but demand from the Allies and the need for a.45 carbine quickly surpassed expectations. Between 1911 and 1913, Colt manufactured around 100,000 M1910A1s, a significant increase from their typical annual production.

The M1910A2, a smaller version of the M1910A1, was also produced, offering a more compact and affordable option. As late as 1918, production of both models remained relatively equal, with the M1910A1 featuring a small gold star and arrowhead on the right side of the slide, and a red X in the center. The U.S. military purchased a large number of M1910s from Colt in 1912 and 1913, many of which saw action in World War I. Following the war, the M1910 and its parts remained in service with some U.S. military branches until 1915.

Early M1910 pistols featured a single action/single action lock action, similar to the original M1921. From 1915 onwards, they were equipped with a two-operation trigger, which could be reset by pressing the trigger slightly backward. The M1910's action combined the earlier Colt single action with the successful Colt double action locking mechanism, making it the first revolver to feature both mechanisms. The Colt double action locking feature was similar to that used in the M1875 and M1868 Repeating Rifles. The lever on the right side of the trigger could be set to either single action or double action, and in either position, it locked both the hammer and striker to the frame using tappets on the top of the cylinder. This locking mechanism was also used in the M1903 and 1911 pistols. The trigger pull was relatively long, about one-third the length of the 1903 lever.

The pistol's grip was not ambidextrous, with either a slightly domed or pointed design. The thumb notch on the grip frame was a small slot for the finger to rest on the slide, rather than the slide being fixed into the grip frame. The M1910 was shipped with a special magazine featuring a large lever on the right side and a smaller slot in the frame for the magazine latch. The original Colt ammunition magazines used a lever on the left to set a notch that could lock or unlock the magazine. During the war, military units with original magazines did not need to switch to new magazines, as their magazines held up well and were adequate for use.

The M1910A1 became an instant success, with the U.S. military purchasing an astonishing 3.4 million units between 1913 and 1920. The M1910A1 also gained popularity among collectors, often selling above prices for other 1911 pistols. The M1910A1 was adopted by the U.S. Navy as the Mk 7, with a 3" barrel, and was used with the Mark VII torpedo hunter and submarine until World War I. The M1910A2, with its 2 1/2" barrel, was also used with the Mk VII hunter, but was sometimes considered underpowered by collectors who preferred the M1910A1 for its accuracy and power.

Sid Lee, a renowned lawyer with over three decades of experience, raised pertinent questions regarding the handling of cases involving police chiefs by federal authorities. Lee, who previously served as police commissioner in Birmingham and Shelby County, noted that it is uncommon to see police chiefs facing criminal charges, let alone serving prison time. In his extensive legal career, Lee cannot recall a single instance where a police chief was convicted of criminal misconduct and sentenced to prison.

Alabama's legal framework, established in 1884, grants police chiefs significant authority. Both state and federal laws require federal prosecutors to demonstrate that a law was breached to bring a criminal case against a police chief. Furthermore, prosecutors must provide evidence of the chief's violation of a federal law, typically an obscure provision of the 1869 civil service law. Only after a conviction can the chief face criminal punishment.

Lee and other former prosecutors pointed out that the evidence, including emails, videos, reports, and internal investigations, suggested that some police chiefs abused their power. This issue was widespread in certain police departments, with its existence well-known. Lee recalled a case involving John McDaniel, the then-Atlanta president of the police patrolmen's association, who was charged with federal bribery. McDaniel had sent an email describing the importance of a meeting for a special unit that was to take over the narcotics unit at Atlanta's police department.

The next day, the commissioner stated he was unaware of the unit, Lee said.

As prosecutors, they sought evidence indicating police chief involvement. Often, the evidence was concealed within the chain of command.

"If it was a chief, if it was a senior leader who would have received a reprimand, we found it," Lee said. "There were a number, but we tried to find all there was."

However, even when they found the evidence, the prosecutors encountered resistance from the police chiefs.

"The department leaders said, 'This is a very difficult case,' " Lee said. "They said, 'Why are you wasting your time with this case?' " Lee recalled one chief saying, " 'I can prove this. I can show you the evidence.' "

A federal prosecutor, who wished to remain anonymous due to ongoing investigations, shared a similar perspective.

A federal grand jury recently indicted Birmingham's current mayor, William Bell, and four city police officers, accusing the mayor, his chief of police, the chief's predecessor, and six other city employees of failing to report an armed robbery to the FBI during the summer of 2014. The FBI typically does not investigate crime or police misconduct, but the U.S. attorney's office in Mobile, Alabama, received a complaint and launched its own investigation. The case remains ongoing, with no charges filed. Bell and the other officers' indictments are unrelated to the federal investigation.

Two city police officers are also awaiting trial in federal court on drug charges unrelated to the gun-whacker. Their case is part of the broader probe, and it is unclear whether the federal investigation could impact the federal indictment. In a typical case, prosecutors might seek a plea deal involving guilty pleas or a trial. A trial would be less likely with an open-ended indictment.

If all charges are resolved, Lee said, "they might make a decision to charge a single police chief. But all have to be willing to go to court and make those arguments."

This is particularly relevant for U.S. attorneys, who can be political. There are also strong feelings among rank-and-file prosecutors whose offices have jurisdiction over municipal police departments that prosecute local crimes. Those prosecutors might not be willing to proceed with criminal charges if a federal indictment were to surface, especially if they had an open-ended indictment.

In Birmingham, Bell is widely considered a potential Democratic candidate for mayor in 2018. He stated that the investigation into his actions is "the reason you don't want to be associated with me politically. The fact of the matter is everyone knows I took a hard line with the drug dealers, and I have no regrets doing it."

While there are no public records of the conversations between Bell and the FBI, at least one person close to the investigation, a former police chief of a nearby town in southern Alabama, testified at the federal corruption trial of one of Bell's top lieutenants.

The First Indochina War, a pivotal conflict in Southeast Asian history, unfolded from December 19, 1946 to August 1, 1954. The struggle pitted France and its allies against the Viet Minh, a coalition of Vietnamese nationalists and communists, who sought independence from French colonial rule. The war's outcome was cemented with the Geneva Accords, which partitioned French Indochina into roughly equal territories and temporarily established separate communist and non-communist zones. The agreement also instituted a 300-day ceasefire, allowing for elections and a peaceful reunification of the region. Unfortunately, this vision was never realized, and the French ultimately relinquished control, paving the way for Ho Chi Minh's government to reunify the country. This conflict served as a precursor to the Vietnam War, a protracted and complex struggle that continues to shape the region's politics and identity.

A recent investigation has uncovered a significant correlation between maternal cannabis use during pregnancy and the risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in offspring. The study revealed that children born to mothers with the highest rates of heavy cannabis consumption while pregnant (defined as at least one joint per week or more) exhibited a 32% increased risk of ASD.

The risk was even more pronounced for children whose mothers had used cannabis while pregnant before giving birth, resulting in a nearly twice the rate of ASD compared to the other groups.

"We are aware that exposure to cannabis has detrimental effects on the developing fetus," says lead author James T. Hunt, a renowned expert in pediatrics. "However, the extent to which prenatal exposure may lead to later developmental issues remains unclear."

"Pregnant women who use cannabis during the first trimester may experience an increased risk of miscarriage or adverse outcomes," Hunt adds. "Cannabis appears to affect the development of the fetus as early as the second week of pregnancy."

The research team analyzed data from nearly 15,500 participants aged 22 to 45 years old and compared them with 14,963 children born to mothers with no history of cannabis use. The study found that the risk of ASD increased by 50% and that the risk for children of mothers who used cannabis more than twice a week rose to nearly twice the risk of the rest of the group.

This investigation, published in Clinical Toxicology, contributes to the existing body of research indicating a link between prenatal exposure to illicit drugs and autism diagnosis. A previous study in 2007 discovered that children with the highest concentrations of dopamine, a brain chemical crucial for learning and behavior, had the lowest levels of autism diagnoses in a U.S. study population.

The latest findings suggest that children exposed to cannabis from conception may begin to experience negative reactions to the drug as they age. As the brain develops a tolerance for the drug, approximately 70% of children who use cannabis may stop using it as adults. These children may be more prone to developing ADHD and a range of other neurodevelopmental problems later in life, the researchers suggest.

The research was funded by the National Institute on Drug Abuse, the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism, and the National Cancer Institute.

In India, the tax implications of stock market earnings are multifaceted. The tax rate on capital gains from share sales hinges on the duration of shareholding. If shares are sold within a 12-month period, the gain is classified as short-term and is subject to the applicable income tax rate. Conversely, if shares are held for more than 12 months before sale, the gain is considered long-term, attracting a lower tax rate of 10% (inclusive of surcharge and cess). Alternatively, taxpayers can opt for a 20% tax rate (inclusive of surcharge and cess) with indexation benefits, which may help minimize tax liability on long-term capital gains. It is crucial to recognize that tax treatment may vary depending on individual circumstances, and consulting a tax expert or the Indian tax authorities is advisable for tailored guidance.

Over the past 12 months, the Obama administration has consistently stated its willingness to utilize military force to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

However, the administration has faced growing opposition from Republicans, who argue that the president should be taking more proactive measures to avoid war with Iran. They have accused him of being overly passive by failing to articulate a clear case for military action.

Representative Michael McCaul, the Republican chairman of the House Homeland Security Committee, warned on Wednesday that even if the administration does not launch a strike on Iran to prevent it from developing nuclear weapons, military action would still ultimately be necessary.

"If Iran refuses to accept a diplomatic solution, they will eventually be faced with the necessity of taking action," McCaul said during a question-and-answer session. "Whether that happens tomorrow or in the future is for the Obama administration to decide."

McCaul emphasized that the U.S. still supports a peaceful path, which he believes would be preferred by international negotiators in Geneva rather than a military strike. He also argued that such a path would not violate the UN charter.

As the Obama administration makes its own decision on whether to proceed with military action against Iran if negotiations fail, some of McCaul's comments may reflect the reality that many Republicans may not yet be on board with a strike against Iran's nuclear facilities.

On Wednesday, Senator John B. McCain, Arizona Republican and likely Republican vice presidential nominee in 2012, suggested that lawmakers should hold a vote but not be inflexible on this issue.

He pointed out that Iran is a significant market for U.S. firms, and that the U.S. has an economic interest in maintaining good business relations with Iran.

"My problem with this strategy is that we have a trade deficit with Iran, and we need to ensure that if we take military action, they won't retaliate by banning all exports of oil or all imports from America," McCain said. "At the time, it's the right thing to do; it's the prudent thing to do."

On Wednesday, some Democrats also expressed concern that the GOP's push for a military strike against Iran would derail the ongoing talks.

Senator Robert Menendez, New Jersey Democrat and chairman of the Foreign Relations Committee, told reporters that if Obama decided to strike Iran, Congress would be responsible for ensuring that the Iranian regime does not acquire nuclear weapons.

"I don't care if it's in the best interests of resolving our differences with Iran," Menendez said. "I care about the Iranians not having a nuclear weapon."

And Senator Dianne Feinstein, California Democrat and chairwoman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, said Congress would need to approve any strike.

"There needs to be a great deal of political support in Congress for it, and I won't vote against the president," Feinstein told CNN. "But ultimately, if it's a war, it must be authorized."

The prefix six is rapidly gaining traction as the most widely used and popular among internet users worldwide. The study reveals that the average IPv6 prefix length has increased to 16.7 bits, a slight rise from the previous quarter. This growth is attributed to the rapid expansion of IPv6 prefixes, which increased by 463 percent over the past 11 months.

As IPv4 begins to phase out, IPv6 is poised to become the primary method of communication over the internet, particularly for mobile devices. The availability of over 7.5 billion IPv4 addresses will also play a crucial role in the widespread adoption of IPv6.

The study also highlights the disparity in IPv6 adoption among countries. While countries like the United States, China, and India have already made significant strides in IPv6 adoption, others like those in Europe, North America, Asia, Australia, and Africa are still in the early stages of adoption.

The researchers attribute the higher growth rate in the first quarter of 2016 to the increasing adoption of IPv6 prefixes. If this trend continues, the world can expect to see roughly 8.8 billion IPv6 addresses by the end of 2016.

The study's findings will be presented at the 23rd ACM Conference on Internet Measurement in April, held in Amsterdam. The research was supported by various organizations, including the National Security Technology Activity, the Open Government Program of the National Science Foundation, and the University of Illinois.

The Way of the Warrior and Shamanism: Exploring the Path of the Shaman

In my previous post, I introduced the concept of the Way of the Warrior and Shamanism. This post delves into a different aspect of this journey, focusing on the importance of becoming a better warrior and shaman.

The Way of the Shaman is rooted in the ancient philosophies of South American tribes, known as Tobacarla or The Way of the Turtle. It's a comprehensive philosophy that encourages individuals to utilize their unique strengths and gifts to serve their communities.

In modern times, this philosophy and the art of shamanism can be found in the teachings of the Chingano shamans from the Amazon forest. Chingano shamanism is a complex and eclectic form of shamanism that has a deep connection with the ancient beliefs of the Aztecs.

There are distinct differences between these two forms of shamanism, but one significant difference is that both the Chingano shamans and the Aztecs believe that becoming a better shaman is achievable through one's own unique traditions.

As with all shamanism, there are various paths to explore, each with its unique flavor.

The first form of shamanism known to our ancestors was the Medicine Man and his assistants. These shamans used plants and animals to heal their fellow people and each other. Their primary role was to communicate with nature spirits to make deals with various beings from the rainforest to the stars.

The Shaman was a vital source of knowledge in the Amazon Rainforest and was regarded as the shaman's most trusted lieutenant. However, due to the physical limitations of their role, their abilities were somewhat restricted.

These shamans, like the ancient Chingano shamans, recognized the presence of spirits, which is why they believed they needed to connect with nature to interact with them.

The nature of the nature spirits formed the basis of their religion, which is why shamans were allowed to coexist with their allies on the forest floor, where they could negotiate with these supernatural entities.

This belief had a profound impact on the culture and nature of those living in the rainforest. The shaman believed they had a special connection with all of nature and could use their powers to help those in need, interpret dreams, and communicate with nature spirits.

To become an effective shaman, one must possess certain qualities: a deep affinity with nature, a strong belief in one's abilities, the capacity to communicate with nature spirits, and the humility to live in the present, guiding and helping those they care about while remaining connected to nature.

I have focused on the "first path" because the shaman plays a vital role beyond simply utilizing their gifts to benefit the people of the rainforest. They must also protect the spirits and their territory, understanding that every life is sacred and that they must help people living with the spirit world to protect themselves.

I hope these essays have helped you understand the significance of the shaman's role and the importance of becoming properly equipped to fulfill it.

The second path of Shamanism, known as Bicultural Shamanism, involves working with indigenous cultures in our home countries, rather than our ancestral cultures. These indigenous cultures have a deep connection with the spirits, the land, and the land itself, and they possess a strong sense of spirituality and reverence for these spiritual beings. When we work with indigenous cultures, we aim to integrate their traditions and ceremonies into our contemporary community, sharing this wisdom with their descendants in a safe and secure manner.

The key is to understand our roots and how they have shaped us. We must be able to work not only with the native spirits of our home country but also with their ancestors. Without this connection and understanding, we cannot fully comprehend our unique gifts and how to utilize them.

This leads me to the third path, known as Traditional Shamanian Shamanism, which is a broad term encompassing the same concept. In this path, we work not only with the spirit world but also with our ancestors and their spiritual traditions. It is not limited to the shamanic experience or the shaman as such but the shaman as I have described them in my previous posts.

Austin's Real Estate Landscape: A Shift in Priorities?

When it comes to finding the perfect home, most people agree that having control over your schedule is crucial. However, when it comes to choosing where to live, some local officials are taking a different approach.

A recent analysis from the Texas Tribune and American-Statesman revealed that home prices are increasing faster in areas with lower taxes. This might surprise many residents and potentially sway voters who are concerned about higher taxes and spending.

The data showed that cities with the highest tax rates experienced significant increases in home prices, with some areas seeing a 24% increase since 2007. These cities also saw substantial growth in tax collections per capita.

The average annual net gain in cities with average tax levies was $7,200, compared to $5,700 for tax-friendly cities like San Antonio and $4,350 for those with lower levies.

It's essential to note that the analysis only looked at a small portion of the market, focusing on around 40,000 properties in three cities. However, the data highlight the importance of considering the tax code when buying a home.

"That's the No. 1 decision you make," said Dan Rees, a former GOP state representative from Denton. "If you don't know if your taxes are going to be increased, and you make a real estate decision based on the number of homes on the market and the price of the homes, you're really not doing yourself much good."

The Tribune and Statesman analyzed the total property value, not just land, among over 400 local governments that generated more than $15 billion in tax revenue each year between 2007 and 2012. The analysis showed that property values were growing at almost the same rate in areas with lower taxes as in areas with higher tax rates.

The analysis did not include counties or school districts, which often offer different tax options.

Some cities with high property values have also experienced larger property tax growth.

The Tribune/Statesman found that Austin and Dallas are the only two places where home prices have increased more quickly since 2007.

However, the areas that have seen the most property tax hikes have had smaller levies of nearly $500 per acre.

In Dallas, the average per-acre levy was more than 2,100 times the average for similar jurisdictions, while Austin's average levy was more than 2,200 times the average for similar locales.

Among city governments, four cities had a levy that was more than five times larger than the average value of local governmental property assessed in the three-year period examined by the Tribune/Statesman: Fort Worth, San Antonio, Plano, and Allen.

In the past decade, the price of oil has experienced a significant decline, with many sectors, including autos, utilities, and natural gas, seeing prices drop to around $20 per barrel. While economic uncertainty has likely played a role in reducing costs, the overall trend of lower prices has significant implications for consumers.

This downward trend has led to more informed spending decisions, particularly in the areas of cars, appliances, and housing. As a result, median household income has risen. However, lower oil prices also come with a direct economic cost, which is borne by consumers. In 2012, the Consumer Price Index for all urban consumers dropped 0.2 percentage points, with the decline being most pronounced for food and energy.

On the other hand, consumers benefit from lower prices on various fronts. For instance, a 2014 study by the nonpartisan Congressional Research Service found that states with high dependence on natural gas saw a statistically significant price difference for home-heating oil, natural gas, diesel fuel, and propane. Fuel oils are now roughly 10 percent lower in energy-intensive states compared to energy-independent states.

Anecdotal evidence suggests that this difference is common. "The fall in consumer prices can be attributed to the increased use of natural gas and oil in heat," said Joe Schmelzer, chief financial officer of the U.S. Conference of Mayors. "We're also seeing a significant impact from higher oil prices, which have affected retail gasoline prices for several months."

Some economists argue that oil is an "asset class" that can be traded between oil producers, importers, and consumers, thus reducing the "price" of oil. However, Schmelzer argued that energy prices are set in the context of global markets, where the value of a barrel is determined by various factors. The impact of lower oil prices should have no significant impact on the price of natural gas for consumers.

Companies may experience varying impacts. For example, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its member countries have significant economic and political stakes in maintaining oil prices at current or higher levels. Companies will not likely suffer as much as consumers of goods and services, as they pay a premium for oil when there is a lower "markup" between supply and demand.

There are likely a fair number of oil producers that are losing money on oil. However, the loss of revenues is modest compared to the gains that consumers will have from lower prices.

In recent years, Israeli officials have also complained about severe food and fuel shortages in the blockaded city.

The rush of adrenaline when a car reaches its top speed is unparalleled. The engine's roar, the tires' screech, and the driver's sense of accomplishment all combine to create an exhilarating experience. However, maintaining that speed can be a challenge, especially when conditions aren't ideal. The "bottom drive" concept acknowledges that a higher top speed can have unintended consequences on the drivetrain. At extreme speeds, the steering can become unpredictable, the brakes overly sensitive, and the engine may struggle to cope with the demands placed upon it.

As speeds approach 200mph, the tires begin to degrade, losing their grip and increasing the risk of losing control. The brakes, too, can become compromised, and the engine's temperature can rise to the point where it's difficult to maintain control. In such situations, the driver may need to adjust their throttle input to ensure the car remains stable. This can result in an unusual sensation, where the car appears to be moving slowly despite the high speed.

The "Top Drive" concept is designed to mitigate these issues by allowing the engine to continue working at its peak output until the end of the acceleration phase. By doing so, the engine can maintain its optimal power delivery, reducing the risk of understeer and ensuring a smoother, more controlled ride. This approach also helps to minimize the likelihood of the car "slipping" or losing traction, which can occur when the engine is pushed too hard.

It's worth noting that drivers who push their cars to the limit may experience a temporary loss of power at high revs. This can be attributed to the engine working harder than usual to maintain the desired speed. While the car may feel slower in the short term, the overall experience can be more exhilarating and rewarding for the driver.

Over the past few years, a small yet significant group of individuals from the United States and Canada have made a notable contribution to the fight against a highly infectious disease that has been ravaging humans and animals across Africa and Asia. The virus in question is Ebola, also commonly referred to as Ebola virus. Since its discovery, there has been a pressing need for effective treatments for this disease.

Fortunately, a breakthrough treatment has been discovered. However, it's crucial to note that this treatment is quite challenging, and for many individuals, it may be the only viable option for survival. Unfortunately, many others will likely succumb to the disease.

So, what exactly is this Ebola treatment? Essentially, it's an antiviral chemotherapy approach, which is essentially cancer medicine. While it has a formal name, many medical professionals struggle to pronounce it, so it's often simply referred to as "chemo."

The primary issue with this treatment is that there is currently no straightforward cure for Ebola, which means that many infected individuals will unfortunately pass away. This leaves us with two primary options: an experimental drug that lacks widespread interest, and a vaccine that, unfortunately, is too costly to produce on a large scale.

In light of this, we've explored alternative solutions. There are a few promising experimental chemo treatments available, although they are expensive and have yet to demonstrate significant success in human trials.

To better comprehend the type of Ebola treatment that the world is desperately seeking, we spoke with Dr. Craig Duda, the director of the AIDS and HIV Research and Surveillance Program at Columbia University.

In an exclusive article for The Guardian, Dr. Duda provides insight into the latest treatment available and why it may be a viable option. Here's a brief Q&A with Dr. Duda about the latest treatment.

What is this latest treatment?

The treatment is called "TKM-Ebola." This stands for Temozolomide-Induced Cure with Metastatic-Like T-Cell Receptor (T-cell receptor) Antibody (T-cell antibody). We aim to have it available for injection or oral administration within 30 days.

I have concerns about the cost and the difficulty of bringing it to market quickly. Does this concern change over time as the treatment improves and becomes more affordable?

We're eager to make it available as soon as possible. We anticipate having it ready soon. The main challenge is distributing the drug, which is why we're working to expedite the process.

How much of the current treatment supply is experimental?

We have a full stock of experimental medication. The reason we're experimenting with treatments is that we don't always know enough about the patient, the biology of the virus, and other diseases or drugs we're testing.

Imagine we're on the cusp of something new...

What if this project becomes the next big thing? Only time will tell.

So, here's the lowdown: we're transitioning from rough sketches of a future codebase to the real deal. If you're thinking of joining the crew, now's the perfect time to get involved. You'll help me refine the design, which will involve plenty of trial and error. (You'll see how I plan to streamline the design as we go along.) Alternatively, you're welcome to jump in and contribute your own ideas.

(And if you're interested but not sure where to start, don't worry – we can work out a plan together. In fact, we've already had a few contributors step up: Paul Bäcker, Mike Sussman, Matthew Nieder, Paul Stoffregen, Kevin Suddendorf, and yours truly.)

The key difference between this version and others is that it's built entirely in C++. I chose C++ because shell scripts and Python wouldn't be the best fit for various reasons.

Pancreatic inflammation: Heavy drinking can cause pancreatitis, leading to stomach pain and bleeding.

Stomach lesions: Prolonged alcohol use may contribute to the development of stomach or intestinal ulcers, causing stomach pain and bleeding.

The resolution explicitly prohibits governments from funding any organization that promotes homosexuality, citing "respect" and "adherence to human rights principles," according to a summary provided by the office of Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop.

The United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, and most Western countries currently involved in charter negotiations have supported a resolution that would bar government organizations from funding activities related to homosexuality if they contradict "the fundamental tenets of the American Constitutional order." However, some Western countries have threatened to veto the resolution, citing concerns that it violates their own constitution.

The resolution's fate remains uncertain, as a draft calling for the same ban was leaked online, sparking controversy.

In a recent statement, Bishop emphasized the importance of this issue to the Australian delegation, stating, "I have engaged with numerous government diplomats over the past fortnight. It is crucial to have the Australian Parliament and people on this matter."

A surge in militarization of American cities has been observed, with Chicago's recent incident serving as a prime example.

The police claimed the firearm may have been stolen in California, although this possibility was deemed unlikely. Nevertheless, they proceeded with the operation, resulting in a "massive and coordinated raid," according to David McNaughton, president of the Chicago Police Union.

A separate search warrant was executed in May, but no illegal items were found.

A gun advocacy group, Americans for Responsible Solutions, characterized the action as an "outrageous overreach" and noted that Chicago has the worst record for civil asset forfeiture in the nation, second only to New Orleans.

The group called for a review of all seizures and civil forfeitures in the state and urged law enforcement to adhere to common sense and avoid targeting law-abiding citizens.

It's worth noting that no criminal charges were filed in connection with the raid, although the possibility of future charges exists.

Regarding the unlicensed firearm, Chicago police stated that it was discovered during the search to be non-compliant with Chicago Police Department policy.

The Department of Justice's civil asset forfeiture program provides local police departments with additional resources to support their budgets. While legal, this program raises concerns about the potential for government overreach.

The research, published in an upcoming edition of Asteroid and Comet Science, suggests that some asteroids may be more dangerous to human civilization than previously believed. The study, led by Harvard University professor emeritus Geoffrey Marcy, found that asteroids that were previously thought to be rotating in the same direction may actually be moving in diametrically opposite directions.

The team used data from NASA's Stardust spacecraft to make their findings. They discovered that one asteroid, 2015 TB145, was rotating at a much faster rate than previously thought. This could have significant implications for our understanding of asteroid behavior and potentially hazardous asteroids.

The study also found that the relative speeds of the two asteroids were about the same, but that 2015 TB145 was moving faster. This could be due to the asteroid's larger orbit, which gives it more orbital energy.

The research has significant implications for our understanding of asteroids and their potential impact on human civilization. It highlights the importance of continued research and monitoring of asteroids to better understand their behavior and potential hazards.

In our most recent development, we've successfully integrated the new and improved CephFS into CentOS 6.3, making it easier for our team to work on the project and gather valuable feedback from the community. Our primary focus was on developing the initial CephFS features, fixing minor bugs, and enhancing the overall user experience.

New Features

Let's take a closer look at the new features we've added to CephFS in CentOS 6.3. We're prioritizing the most important features and continuously expanding our offerings.

Scheduled backups: Our new SCHEDULED BACKUPS feature allows anyone in the community to provide CephFS support or run it independently. The default scheduler is now a low-latency system for CephFS backups, and we've optimized the scheduler to reduce file system initialization time.

We've also introduced LZ4 compression, which reduces the space occupied in the CephFS file system by approximately 30%. This means that even more files won't overwhelm the SSD.

Better authentication: We've enhanced the authentication method to ensure users can access the correct password by default and to support CLI-only users who require interaction with the CephFS module.

Automatic mount points creation and deletion: Our new automatic backup solution now handles mount point creation and removal, simplifying the backup process and increasing reliability.

Added support for S3: We've incorporated S3 support into OpenStack NTP-based CephFS, a significant step that will streamline our development process and make it easier for users and the community to contribute.

Improved scheduler/compression algorithm: We've optimized the scheduler, reducing the amount of space taken on the SSD by approximately 30%. This results in a roughly 2x reduction in the performance impact of a cephFS backup process.

Reduced performance impact of LZ4: We've simplified and improved the compression algorithm to better reduce space taken on the SSD in a CephFS backup. With LZ4 and our improved algorithm, cephfs can now recover up to twice as much data from a CephFS backup compared to before.

We've made significant strides in improving the CephFS experience, and we're excited to see the impact these new features will have on our users and the community.

Other donors on the list included "many of our GOP bundlers" and "more than just GOP bundlers." The "realign priorities" strategy would be to encourage those GOP bundlers to maintain their support for Romney in private, allowing the Romney campaign to secure a significant portion of the funding from "hundreds of major" donors on the California primary ballot. According to the email, those on the list were asked to sign an "unofficial Republican National Committee pledge" to "not contribute to the presumptive Presidential nominee of either major party," enabling the Romney campaign to present a united front of "party regulars" for the general election.

The RNC's internal email outlined the plan to implement the anti-Romney "realign priorities" campaign.

"I would like to inform all CA GOP CA GOP bundlers that they are now on our list of key Romney bundlers. As I mentioned to our California CA Republican bundlers (many of whom are still weighing their options), the RNC is going to be conducting a targeted campaign to dissuade all of our California CA GOP bundlers from making a public commitment to the Romney Victory Fund," the email stated.

In the email, RNC Chair Reince Priebus is clearly attempting to persuade the party's most senior leaders that his campaign, which is facing significant challenges following losses in the New Jersey and New Mexico primaries, must now be the most serious campaign to avoid the "tragedy of the commons." Researchers from an international team have uncovered a surprising link between a natural repair mechanism in bacteria and the production of proteins essential for learning and memory.

The team discovered that in a mouse model for type 1 diabetes, the self-healing capacity diminishes with age. As bacteria age, their metabolic efficiency declines, making it challenging for them to maintain their repair mode.

The researchers found that by continuing to produce a small molecule called PAMPT, aged bacteria can restore their glycogen repair capacity. PAMPT has additional health benefits, including promoting growth and cell-to-cell communication.

The study also revealed that the same mechanism of glycogen repair in older bacteria enhances their ability to produce taurine, a vital compound for cell-to-cell communication.

"If we can find ways to improve the efficiency of these cells' glycogen repair, it could have a significant impact on the decline in cellular signaling observed in conditions like diabetes and Alzheimer's," said Dr. Sarah A. Johnson-Laird, lead author.

"This research is fascinating, and we're still learning about the role of these molecules in the aging process. We hope to uncover more about their functions and how they can be used to promote health," said Dr. David Y. Li, another author.

The study was recently published in Cell Research.

This recipe serves four and can be easily doubled or tripled to feed a crowd. Here's what you'll need:

* 2 cups quinoa or brown rice
* 2 tablespoons olive oil
* 1 large onion, chopped
* 4 cups peeled and chopped sweet potatoes
* ½ cup chopped sweet onion
* 8 ounces frozen chopped carrots
* 1 cup frozen chopped celery
* ½ cup cooked white beans
* ½ cup diced corn
* 3 cloves garlic, minced
* ¼ cup fresh parsley leaves
* ¼ cup fresh thyme
* ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon

* 1 cup water
* ½ cup soaked brown rice or quinoa

The House Judiciary Committee recently cleared the Justice Against Sponsors of Terrorism Act, also known as JASTA, paving the way for its consideration by the full House. If enacted, this legislation could potentially hinder the ability of countries like Iran and other alleged terrorist states from exploiting American laws or foreign criminal codes to take action against their citizens in the United States. The inability to prosecute individuals for terrorism-related offenses, such as the 9/11 attacks, could force the US to reevaluate its counterterrorism efforts.

The Obama administration expressed significant concerns that JASTA would compromise ongoing counterterrorism initiatives. John Bellinger, acting assistant attorney general for national security, emphasized that law enforcement agencies are well-equipped to handle the evolving threat environment and that JASTA would undermine their effectiveness.

JASTA would grant foreign courts the authority to override a presidential determination regarding the application of American law in a specific country. Currently, Americans can be tried and punished in foreign courts for committing terrorist offenses outside the US. JASTA would reverse this, making foreign convictions binding in the US. This change would be based on speculation rather than concrete evidence, failing to reduce the actual threat of terrorism.

The bill also enables federal prosecutors and court officials to incorporate foreign anti-terrorism laws into US criminal cases, even if these laws extend to unrelated crimes. This would permit foreign law enforcement authorities to prosecute those complicit in terrorism charges committed against the US and crimes committed in the US with no connection to the crime.

It appears the Obama administration sought a way to avoid limitations on its ability to prosecute domestic crimes, but its actions in the Senate to block JASTA are concerning. The bill passed the Senate with a similar vote to the House version, but Senate leaders have since reconsidered their position in light of the president's request. This development is a positive sign for a bill that deserves congressional approval.

The Federalist Papers have been shrouded in mystery, with many assuming that A. Hamilton was the primary author. However, this notion is based on a misconception. A. Hamilton did not write any Federalist Papers, but rather wrote the introduction to A History of the Federal Convention of 1787. This book, along with the Federalist Papers, served as the foundation for James Madison's writings.

The origin of the name A. Hamilton can be traced back to a letter written by James Madison to Hamilton, in which Madison refers to a letter he sent to his brother Albert Hamilton, addressing himself as A. Hamilton. This letter ends with the statement: "If you and he have ever had an opportunity of comparing our respective merits on that point, I think you will be fully persuaded, that I do not then merit the appellation of Mr. Hamilton."

In the Federalist Papers, A. Hamilton is frequently mentioned, but his ideas cannot be traced back or his contributions identified. It is likely that the person who wrote the introduction to A History of the Federal Convention was not the same person who wrote the Federalist Papers.

The first printed edition of the Federalist Papers appeared in 1788, and in those days, people often referred to the author in the text. Alexander Hamilton's words were referred to as his writing, but it is not accurate to say that Madison wrote most of the Federalist Papers. He was likely involved in many aspects of the papers, but the majority of the ideas were written by others.

In the book A History of the Federal Convention of 1787, I list the names of the delegates who attended the Constitutional Convention of 1787, but I do not include the names of all the authors in the text. If you look in the Appendix II, you will find the name only of A. Hamilton and the other person who wrote the text of A History of the Federalist Papers, Thomas Jefferson. The actual authors of the Federalist Papers remain unknown, except for the handful of delegates from the Virginia Assembly who were identified as the authors.

Gas prices fluctuate, but the average cost of a gallon in 2009 was approximately $2.27. The EIA's story on US oil production is complex, with data available for most of 2010, but not consistently since January 21, 2013. The agency's reports are crucial for understanding production changes daily.

EIA data originates from the US Department of Energy's "Drill, Baby Drill" initiative, which began in 2005. The agency aggregates monthly reports from companies that produce petroleum products. Daily reports come from oil and gas companies in various sectors: extraction, energy, processing, conventional, biofuels, natural gas, and Nexen.

Crude oil and products differ. Crude oil represents what's left after processing, refining, and sale. EIA collects data for the Oil Consumption Survey (OCS), which calculates total petroleum consumption. Quarterly data is collected, but not weekly or monthly. Volatility is common due to seasonal fluctuations.

The US is the world's largest crude oil exporter and producer of natural gas. Most oil comes from the Western Hemisphere and is distributed through pipelines. The top five producing states are California, Texas, Iraq, Russia, and Canada.

EIA publishes information on approximately 400 oil and natural gas processing facilities in the US. Refineries average 17 million barrels per day, while terminal operators may process up to 50% off-site. Crude oil output can fluctuate seasonally due to weather and other factors.

EIA statistics come from the Petroleum Consumption Survey (PCS), conducted quarterly as part of the Annual Energy Outlook (AEO). The survey collects information from oil and gas producers and refiners in various sectors.

When EIA says the US produces more oil than anyone else, it means the country is among the world's top five oil producers, producing over 95% of the world's oil and natural gas. The US has been the world's largest producer since January 2003, followed by Saudi Arabia, Venezuela, and Nigeria.

EIA natural gas statistics come from weekly reports on production, processing, and consumption.

As I reflect on the gaming industry, I'm struck by the dichotomy between the suits and the creatives. On one hand, we have the suits, who dominate the industry with their fancy cars and high-stakes deals. On the other hand, we have the creatives – the game developers, the writers, the artists – who pour their hearts and souls into bringing games to life. And then there's the games press, which sits at the intersection of these two worlds.

The games press has undergone significant changes over the past decade, driven by the rise of social media and online gaming. While it's true that some of its original values have been lost, its core mission remains the same: to celebrate games as art and tell their stories to the world. I believe that most game journalists would agree that the gaming community does a poor job of recognizing and celebrating the work of games journalists.

However, despite this, there are pressing issues that need to be addressed. As a games journalist, I've noticed that industry personalities and websites often use social media to promote games they love, which can lead to a lack of objectivity in their reviews. In my own experience, I've faced the challenge of writing about local multiplayer games, only to have indie titles emerge that are often of a higher quality than their commercial counterparts. While these new games deserve attention, I worry that the games press is becoming too focused on promoting them, rather than providing a balanced view of the industry.

This has led to a problem: many of these indie games receive poor ratings on review aggregators like Metacritic, simply because readers don't know how to critically evaluate games. As a result, I've had to become more critical in my reviews, while also being mindful of the potential consequences of pissing off game developers and publishers. My editor has even cautioned me to be more critical, while also avoiding giving too much credit to the game's publisher or developer, lest it cost me money.

When I discuss this issue with my fellow writers, they often tell me that they don't have to worry about these reviews, as they always say the same thing about every game. While I understand their perspective, I believe that this is a problem that needs to be addressed. I'll continue to write about local multiplayer games, but I'll do so in a way that's more critical and nuanced. The games press needs to decide whether it will continue to focus on local multiplayer games, or if it will evolve to become something new. Until then, I'll keep writing about these games, and exploring new ways to tell their stories.

The latest statistics from Australia reveal a concerning trend: the number of new sexually transmitted diseases reported in the country has risen by 26% between 2014-15 and 2015-16. This increase comes on the heels of a 21.5% decline in new HIV infections during the same period.

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, which compiled the data, the rates of new infections have increased across the country. However, it's premature to draw conclusions about the causes or reasons behind this uptick.

Several factors may be contributing to the rise in STIs, including an increase in casual sexual activity and unprotected sex. Additionally, some infections may be more easily reported and prevented.

In June, the NSW government launched a program to distribute 10,000 condoms to gay and bi men between 14 and 43 in Sydney. While this is an "overseas" program, it will be rolled out locally in the future.

One key risk factor is unsafe sex, particularly among individuals with STIs such as chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and syphilis.

The statistics, released in a bulletin, show that the total population with HIV increased by 13.8% between 2014-15 and 2015-16. This increase is largely attributed to people being diagnosed with the virus.

The ABS report also found that the rate of new infections rose in all age groups in Australia, except for the 25-29 age group. This is largely due to people living longer and a larger pool of newly infected men who have sex with men.

For women, the age-standardized total number of new cases per 100,000 population decreased from 3.1 for women between 20-24 to 2.9 for women between 25-29.

The total number of new cases among men was 2.5 for men between 20-24, 2.3 for men between 25-29, and 2.3 for men between 30-34. The increase in infections seen among men between 30-34 is more likely related to HIV infection.

Although people with HIV are more prevalent in those aged 20-24, the gap between these groups in 2015-16 compared with 2014-15 was only 8% higher for men. This suggests that there are reasons behind the increase in HIV infections that were once seen in younger people.

The report notes that there is a "strong correlation" between HIV infection and other types of STIs. One reason for this is the increasing rates of gonorrhoea and HIV infection.

Gonorrhoea is an infection of the mucous membranes that causes inflammation, pain, and swelling of the genitals in men and pre-cancers in women. It can cause a change in the sex of the baby inside a woman and is linked to sexually transmitted diseases in men and women.

In 2015-16, gonorrhoea was diagnosed in 10,100 people in Australia aged 10 years and older, and almost 4 in 100 had HIV in this age group. HIV was detected in 3,400 men and women aged between 10 and 49 for the same purposes. It is particularly associated with sexual risk-taking and drug use.

Gonorrhoea has also been linked to sexually transmitted infections, and therefore, other STIs are also increasing.
