The most striking feature of our solar system is its array of celestial bodies. A recent publication in Nature Geoscience has unveiled a previously unknown giant planet, Sedna, which may be the second largest body in our solar system, rivaling Jupiter in size. This massive object is shrouded in mystery, having been discovered in the distant reaches of the Kuiper belt.

Unlike its more prominent siblings, Ganymede and Europa, Sedna is an ancient relic, orbiting the Sun at an astonishing distance beyond the edge of the Kuiper belt. "A significant portion of our solar system lies beyond the outer planets, which is why we have numerous new Kuiper belt objects," remarks Paul Chodas, an astronomer at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, California. "Ganymede and Europa reside within the solar system, while Sedna lies outside."

The Kuiper belt comprises several objects that were captured by the gravitational pull of Jupiter and Saturn when they were still at the outer edge of the solar system. The inner Kuiper belt, including Sedna, is approximately 30 times farther away, with no significant moon or planet, situated about 2.4 billion miles from the Sun.

Researchers initially detected Sedna as an anomaly during the first Kepler mission, launched in 2009. The two-year mission has scoured the sky for small, distant, and distant worlds beyond the solar system. If it discovers an object like Sedna, it will alert scientists to its unique orbital mechanics, allowing them to attempt to determine its composition: rock, ice, or water. The Kepler mission has not yet found Sedna, but by comparing the orbits of the Earth and Sedna, Chodas expects it will likely be discovered within the next decade.

One of the primary questions astronomers have about Sedna is what drove it to leave its home and travel far beyond the orbit of Neptune. One possibility is that Sedna's orbital path is unique, suggesting it must have been born in a disk of gas and dust, rather than a bubble. This notion is supported by hints that such a disk may be the origin for many objects in the outer solar system, making Sedna's unique orbit potentially indicative of its origin.

However, this remains speculative, and future observations by next-generation instruments like the James Webb Space Telescope, the largest and most powerful space telescope ever built, will be necessary to confirm these findings. In the meantime, the research team has begun studying the objects they discover, hoping to shed light not only on Sedna's origin but also on the planet formation process in general. "This presents a wonderful opportunity for astrobiology, as these are relatively young rocky bodies, and it's crucial to understand the origin of such entities," says Chodas.

Over the past year, I've been frequently asked to share my experience developing a web service for extracting data from satellite imagery, which can be adapted for other applications. The primary use case is extracting and mapping roads on top of map tiles by street names.

If you're interested in learning more about the techniques behind this work, you can explore my GitHub repository or free software I've developed (see below).

I'd like to share a bit about my background, the technique, and the first application.

As you can see, I started working on this project in 2010. In June 2012, we introduced the GIS-Open project to the wider world, along with a Python client library called GeoFarms. The latter is still a work in progress, but we've already deployed GIS-Open in several commercial applications and received valuable feedback from users.

Initially, the project focused on mapping and extracting data from satellite imagery. I began by using OpenStreetMap (OSM) as my data source, which is a great open-source mapping community. However, I soon realized that handling the large amount of files and data sets was slow and challenging. This slowed down the entire process, but I eventually set up a few servers (one in Germany and one in France, each with 1GB of storage) to process the data to a TIFF format.

As I worked on the project, I explored the possibilities of using Python to develop web services. I was surprised to discover that similar software already existed, and I wasn't even aware of it during my research.

Some key points to note:

The main idea behind this software is straightforward: we use standard Python libraries for data extraction and web frameworks like Flask for server development, along with Jinja and HTML templating for HTML rendering.

The web services are created using Flask, which provides a HTTP server class (app) for creating web applications.

When a user accesses a data set, the server handles all data extraction as needed.

The Python client library is used for communication between the Python application and the server.

This article is part of a series exploring the GIS-Open technology stack.

How does it work?

In essence, the project is about extracting data from satellite images and creating a web service to provide it. The real idea was to create a web service that people could use to extract data using Python, and then provide data sets to those who requested them. This concept is common in many GIS projects, where data extraction and distribution are essential.

This project is not just a GIS project; it's a real service that enables data extraction and use. It's useful for me, as I can take data and integrate it into an application. If data is unavailable on the website, I can use the OpenStreetMap API to retrieve it if needed. It could also be used for a mapping project I plan to start in the future.

This is a complex problem that took me over 8 years to complete, with over 3000 lines of code, many files, and hundreds of images in various formats. I'm pleased with the result, as it shows that it's possible to solve these problems, even if it takes time.

The main challenges we faced during this project were:

Developing a service that allows users to easily download data sets or map tiles at a later stage.

Using standard Python libraries, without custom software or special frameworks.

Deploying the service on any server based on Flask.

Flask was also used as a template engine.

I hope this provides a better understanding of the project and its significance.

The Agricultural Community of Eastern Canada – A recent study conducted by the University of Manitoba has revealed that nearly three-quarters of farmers who were initially selected for the Green Jobs Program have already ceased operations.

The research found that over half of the 16 priority farmers included in the BC Farmers' Compensation Scheme (BCFPCS) will cease operations within the next 24 months. This has led to widespread frustration among farmers, who feel that the program has failed to meet their economic needs.

"It's unacceptable that farmers are being forced to continue working under a system that cannot provide them with benefits in the near future," says Paul Brown, president of the Southerwing Farmers Association of British Columbia. "When farmers are forced to work and pay the price of the system's failure, it's only a matter of time before it's eliminated altogether."

For the first time, the BC Farmers Federation surveyed the farming community's economic needs and found that 80 per cent believe that the Green Jobs Program has failed. This is not just a matter of economic needs, but also basic human rights such as healthcare, retirement security, fair wages, and adequate housing.

Farmers have been told for decades that they are not receiving adequate benefits under the BCFPCS. In fact, farm equipment insurance costs have skyrocketed to record highs, while the Green Jobs Program has stagnated and often failed to deliver.

"All signs point to the end of the Green Jobs Program," says Mike Schreiner, vice president of communications for the BC Farmers' Federation.

"The failure of the BCFPCS is preventing good producers from receiving fair treatment. They are being forced to continue working under the same system that hasn't worked for them for decades. Many farmers are only picking their last day of work this season. When they quit, those who remain in the industry won't have anyone to replace them for the next season."

BC Farmers Federation President Paul Brown agrees, calling for the government to immediately halt BCFPCS payments to farmers and remove them from eligibility.

"Providing assistance to farmers is not just morally right, it's a necessity. It helps improve productivity and promotes sustainability, but our farmers are not receiving equal treatment. If the BC Farmers Federation worked to ensure farmers weren't being forced to continue working for a dysfunctional program, we wouldn't have to reach this point," says Brown.

According to BC Farmers Federation research, 70 per cent of farmers surveyed agree that the BCFPCS is ineffective at preventing economic hardships such as loss of income, poor health, and loss of farm equipment.

The Southerwing Farmers Association of British Columbia represents the interests and needs of farmers in southern and eastern British Columbia throughout the agriculture sector.

A recent report from the Institute for Research on Poverty (IRP) reveals a widening disparity between average salaries and federal poverty thresholds in the United States.

The report, which examines data from the Current Population Survey's Annual Social and Economic Supplement from 2010 to 2012, finds that the average hourly wage for a U.S. worker is $15.89. In 2010, the federal poverty threshold for a family of four was $24,856. Consequently, a full-time worker over 40 years old would have to dedicate half of their paycheck to rent or housing for their entire lifetime. Meanwhile, according to data from the Census Bureau's U.S. Income and Poverty report for 2015, the average hourly wage for a full-time, full-year employee is $29.07—approximately 30 percent higher than the minimum wage in 2015.

The report also highlights that while the overall wage gap between those with higher and lower salaries is decreasing, the most disadvantaged workers are not experiencing a significant reduction. On average, the IRP found that in 2013, a full-time employee over 40 years old earning the average wage would have needed to allocate 30.4 percent of their income to housing, food, transportation, and clothing—more than twice the 30.1 percent of their salary in 2009. Annually, a worker over 40 years old would require an additional $3,567 in income to maintain independence.

"Despite the overall pay gap expanding over time, one key takeaway from this report is that the gap between those with higher and lower incomes is increasing," noted Michael Strain, IPR's CEO and co-founder. "This marks a significant milestone in the long-term development of a more equitable economy in which everyone can advance; it's also a crucial point of reference when evaluating federal programs aimed at the lower rungs of the pay scale. It is the challenge we should strive to meet, and it would demonstrate if policymakers chose to take more action."

The report focuses on the U.S. workforce, but the data on average wages across the OECD is also consistent with other research. According to OECD data, the average hourly wage at which a worker in each of the 30 OECD member countries earns in 2015 is approximately $22 per hour. While this level was much lower in previous years, the ratio remains higher than the OECD wage gap of 1.7:1. The OECD wage gap is defined as the average hourly wage required to lift a worker to the OECD's lowest 50th percentile position.

The US average wage is the first of the 30 countries in the report to improve, rising from $14.92 an hour in 2000 to $15.90 per hour in 2015. However, other countries experienced a greater increase between 2013 and 2014, including Switzerland and South Korea, both of which saw their average wages jump by more than $1.00 per hour.

June's employment numbers revealed a striking trend: the proportion of workers with at least a college degree has returned to the 70% mark. This growth is expected to continue.

This year, a remarkable 1.053 million new jobs were created, with a significant majority (more than half) held by college-educated workers. In July alone, a record-breaking 6 million new jobs were created, marking the third consecutive month of this achievement.

Interestingly, since 2011, over half of all new jobs have been held by workers with at least an associate degree. Conversely, less than 2 million jobs have gone to workers with less than a high school diploma.

As we examine the data, we find that the rise in education in the labor market has been slow to spread to the broader economy. However, by the end of this year, it's anticipated that the long-term trend will reverse, as education becomes a less significant factor.

Looking back at data from earlier in the century, we notice that a substantial portion of the overall increase in jobs was due to an increase in education from high school through college and graduate school. Specifically, the share of employment comprised of workers with a college degree has been steadily rising since the mid-20th century.

In 2010, this share reached 68.6%, up slightly from the 67.9% recorded in 2009. In 2006, 67.5% of the workforce held a college degree or more.

Despite the steady rise in education levels, the gap between the education levels of men and women has grown. In 1980, the share of jobs held by men with at least a college degree was nearly twice that held by women with college degrees. The gender gap in college completion has been growing almost as fast as the education gap between men and women.

One factor contributing to this growing education gap appears to be the widening of wage gaps between men and women. A recent analysis found that since 1980, wages adjusted for inflation have increased at a faster rate among all workers, particularly college-educated workers, than among similar workers without a college degree.

This growing wage gap has a spillover effect on the overall employment growth rate. By focusing on the education share of total employment, this analysis examines the impact of job creation on overall labor supply, rather than solely focusing on jobs created directly by worker education.

The following charts illustrate the effect of increasing education on employment rates over time. Since 1999, the education share of total employment has increased as the wage gap between college-educated and non-college-educated workers widens.

This pattern has been particularly intense since 2000, when more than half of all non-wage jobs were held by workers with a high school education or less. The chart illustrates the growth of the education share of total employment since 1980 and the widening of the wage gap between college-educated and non-college-educated workers since 2000.

Between 1979 and 2007, nearly all employment growth was in the most highly educated portion of the labor force. In 2009, the gap was essentially fixed.

In 2009, about a third of total non-wage jobs were held by workers with either an associate degree, a bachelor's degree or higher, or no more than college.

Although the share of employment comprised of college-educated workers has grown at roughly the same rate since 2000 as the educational wage gap has grown, even after adjusting for inflation, the overall increase in the education wage gap relative to the overall wage gap has been much less than it has been in the wake of this long-term trend.

As the chart shows, the widening of the wage gap between workers with and without a college degree has been much steeper in earlier decades. In 1980, workers without a high school education earned 20.4% more than workers with an associate degree. By 2009, those same workers earned 41.3% more than workers with an associate degree. The college wage premium as a share of wages earned by workers with an associate degree or higher had more than tripled since 1980.

A widening wage gap between college-educated and non-college-educated workers has had a disproportionate effect on the low-wage portions of the labor force, where high school-educated workers earn wages that are still lower than those earned by high school-educated workers with some college. For example, in 2009, the average wage for workers with a high school diploma ($20.60) earned almost $7 less per hour than workers with some college.

I've discovered a fantastic Git feature called "reflog" that allows me to explore the history of my commits. To get started, I use the following command:

git log --since "24 months ago" --until "24 months ago"

This gives me a list of all the dates I've modified files since the last commit. It's surprisingly useful for keeping track of changes over time. 

When I want to dive deeper into the history of a specific branch, I use the following command:

git reflog --since "2 years ago"

This shows me the entire history of the branch, including all the commits and changes made over time. To get a specific view of the branch's history, I can use the --short-term option:

git reflog --since "2 years ago" --short-term

This allows me to see the commits made within a specific time period. If I want to limit the number of commits shown, I can use the --hist-limit option:

git reflog --since "2 years ago" --short-term --hist-limit=20

In a peculiar incident, a group of young men who had recently begun selling drugs found themselves in a precarious situation. The summer of 2006 was marked by an unusual atmosphere, where drugs, guns, and money seemed to be the primary concerns. For 19-year-old Justin McHenry, this was a particularly trying time. As he waited for a package to be delivered from Amazon, he was confronted by a police officer, Michael Lacey. McHenry's anxiety reached a peak when he saw the officer's badge and the words "police officer." He attempted to retreat, but the officer persisted, stating, "I just don't see this as my job."

McHenry was subsequently arrested on charges related to drugs and guns. He spent six months in a Baltimore County Jail before being released. Lacey, on the other hand, was fired from the force and served over five years of a 10-year sentence for official misconduct.

In the present, the city is taking measures to ensure Lacey does not rejoin the police force. According to Mayor Stephanie Rawlings-Blake, Lacey has threatened to file a lawsuit against the city. Rawlings-Blake emphasized that as long as Lacey remains a police officer, she will not permit his release. The city claims Lacey had a "pattern of violating protocol" and posed a "continuing and serious danger to the citizens he is charged with protecting." The city is preparing to "retain and discipline" Lacey for his alleged misconduct.

Rawlings-Blake stated, "We're not letting the man go back out in front of the Baltimore Police Department. He is not going to be released. And neither of those are going to change until we find out what the facts are." However, some lawyers argue that this does not necessarily mean Lacey will return to active duty until a finding of true malice is established.

According to the law, there are strict requirements for determining whether the city acted in bad faith when firing Lacey. Prosecutors must demonstrate that Lacey had an intention to act in bad faith and that he actually acted in bad faith with a reasonable belief that his actions were legitimate.

Peter Korn, a lawyer, explained that an officer's expectation of legitimacy must be clearly established at the time of the police activity. This expectation can only exist if it is present at the time of the activity and not retroactively.

Rawlings-Blake emphasized that the mayor's office will closely monitor the case, aiming to establish a standard for all cases involving police misconduct. Lacey has admitted to committing misconduct in the past and has a "pattern of lawbreaking." The issue of false arrest remains unclear, as it is uncertain whether Lacey intended for his actions to be considered false.

If a pattern of false arrests is established, it could aid Lacey's defense. However, according to Jennifer M. Lewis, legal defense director for the Baltimore Legal Aid Society, there are potential weaknesses in the city's case. If the city intended their actions to be false, they would not need to demonstrate Lacey acted in bad faith. Instead, they could show that Lacey was unaware of what he was doing was legally wrong.

Lewis noted that if prosecutors failed to prove probable cause, Lacey could argue his actions were justified due to his position as a police officer. The ACLU has expressed concerns about the Baltimore Police Department's aggressive efforts to remove drug cops from the streets.

The City Council plans to vote on a bill, dubbed the "Lacey Law," which would require all law enforcement in the city to be subject to the Lacey Act.

The initial step in resolving a disagreement is to acknowledge its existence.

The most effective approach to doing so is to consider the possibility that the world is comprised of the same elements we envision.

If that were true (and I do not claim to know if it is), I would no longer argue that it's all a fabrication. Instead, I would say to my son, "The world can be filled with such phenomena. That's simply the way it is. Just because it doesn't seem that way, doesn't mean there isn't someone or something responsible for making it that way. Perhaps that's what we should be considering when we're making claims about nature to explain the phenomena we observe."

If the world is indeed full of magic, I'd be forced to confront the possibility that what I perceive as magic is not magic at all, as much as people like to claim it is.

So, if our experiences of magic seem to involve our own interpretations of a world filled with magic, I can no longer agree with such claims, as I don't truly understand what they mean.

The reality is that the vast majority of our observations about the world are accurate – they accurately describe reality with a high level of scientific precision. This reality includes aspects of the physical world that we can no longer accurately describe in the way we think they should be described when looking out the window at the world.

Some of this seems obvious. Take the idea that reality is "incomplete." I don't believe in the idea that God created the universe to include only things that seemed as if that were intended. Why would creationism say that? Why would a person willing to allow for supernatural occurrences claim that the reality of the world is somehow incomplete? There's a lot of room for variation in those opinions, but I find it incredibly hard to believe it's all that easy to hold.

Another example: what is "real," and how is it possible that I am "just a person" and the idea of real is subjective? What we mean by "real" is the truth of our own experiences. When we say that it is "real" that we see a red dot on the blackboard, it is true. We have just experienced that red dot that appeared on the blackboard.

Likewise, what we mean by "real" is that the experience I have right now, regarding the physical world and the world as it has appeared, is true. If it is not, it is false. Even if I don't agree with that idea (and I don't), the reality is that it is true.

One of the things that seems like magic is our ability to create our own reality in our minds. If we believe that's all that reality is, then "fake reality" is what we're actually seeing.

My contention is that the reality behind these "mysteries" is something very different. It's something that we can't quite explain through a mathematical, scientific definition. We may be able to explain what caused my perception to be exactly how I perceive it; but that does not answer what it was that allowed that perception to exist in the first place.

If that were so, the phenomenon we experience is not magic, but rather the reality we all experience. If that were true, then our understanding of reality seems to be at an inherent limit.

Perhaps some aspect of a higher power allows us to see reality for exactly what it is. Perhaps that is true; if so, it would only be reasonable to conclude that God does not need to create the universe itself.

I'm not saying that I know that this is the case, of course. It could just be a "mysterious" aspect of my own perception. However, I don't see how trying to explain it through a formal mathematical model for the world would be fruitful at all.

Instead of giving my son the lesson he might otherwise have gotten from watching my head explode, I would rather let him find out for himself through experience and research.

But as much as this point might be counterintuitive, a person's belief that the world is full of magical things is not actually a rational belief. It relies on a faulty view of the world.

With a mass roughly twice that of our Milky Way and 10 times larger than its nearest neighbor, the Virgo galaxy, researchers believe that the black hole at its core may be at least five times more massive than the one at the center of our own galaxy.

EGS is one of numerous young galaxies in the distant early universe known as the Cosmic Microwave Background. Scientists at the Australian National University propose that this dark matter environment, characterized by cold, dense gas, has enabled the formation of black holes. The latest research supports this theory and highlights EGS as a unique galaxy among those studied.

"This discovery is truly remarkable, with many fascinating aspects," noted Australian National University research fellow Daniel Baker, co-author of the paper.

"It is one of the most isolated and extensively studied galaxies in this time period, boasting the highest ratio of black holes to mass observed."

In the past three decades, astronomers have discovered thousands of galaxies with black holes at their centers. EGS, however, may be the first to be home to black holes. The fact that it is surrounded by galaxies at such vast distances, with similar gravitational forces, suggests that the black holes must be extremely powerful.

The team analyzed approximately 250 hours of data from the Subaru Telescope, which operated in Hawaii. They found that the galaxy is heavily populated with hot ionized gas, containing a massive population of cold, dense ionized gas.

"As we gaze into the distant future, the number of young, cool galaxies with massive black holes should increase as the universe expands," observed co-author Stephen Webb from the University of Manchester in England.

In the paper, Webb and Baker employed computer simulations to explore what would occur if the gas in EGS began feeding a black hole at its core. The researchers discovered that EGS likely forms a binary system with another Milky Way galaxy, but the black hole in EGS cannot get too close to the inner galaxy, as this would cause it to go nova.

"That's why our simulation shows that the black hole doesn't really get too close to the inner galaxy," Baker said. "This is a significant achievement that we believe was previously impossible. This provides a better understanding of how our universe will evolve."

In a recent development, the Canadian government is grappling with the possibility of prison bed shortages in British Columbia. A provincial prison is set to close due to safety concerns, leaving the federal government scrambling to find alternative accommodations for the 578 federal inmates currently housed there.

According to a report obtained by The Globe and Mail, the Canada Border Services Agency is exploring various options to relocate the inmates, including potential agreements with other jurisdictions. The agency is also considering the possibility of building new facilities to house federal inmates.

The B.C. government is constructing a new prison to accommodate over 4,000 inmates scheduled for release from provincial jails in February. There has been speculation that the province might consider keeping the federal inmates to alleviate the bed shortage.

The CBSA report highlights the Lamer Correctional Centre in Kelowna, B.C., as the only facility capable of housing federal inmates from the federal penitentiary in Burnaby. However, the report notes that the facility has a limited capacity and may require the relocation of eligible inmates in the future.

Prison-rehabilitation experts have expressed concerns about the potential consequences of the bed shortage. Dan Kelly, executive director of the Vancouver-based Innocence Clinic, has criticized the CBSA's analysis, stating that it suggests some federal inmates may be sent to "death row."

The CBSA report notes that when the current agreement expires in 2018, the province is expected to be able to take as many federal inmates as it can physically accommodate. The agency has not specified when it expects the inmates to arrive in B.C.

The CBSA is currently reviewing the number of beds available in B.C. and is considering various alternatives to address the shortage. The agency has stated that it intends to end the current transfer arrangement in March 2018 and will focus on transferring inmates to other prisons or community correctional centers in the long term.

I was struck by the sight of young soldiers, some as young as 22, entering a room alone with a group of unfamiliar men, as if they were old friends. It felt like they were in a foreign environment.

Of course, this oversimplifies the situation. The Army has strict rules and regulations regarding individual conduct, discipline, respect, and teamwork. These rules extend to alcohol use, with an unwritten rule prohibiting discussion of personal struggles with drinking or drugs with superiors.

The Army views drug users as troublemakers in the early stages of a "problem." They're seen as a threat to the organization's reputation for respectability, morality, and cleanliness. To address this, individuals were either discharged or faced court-martial.

The issue is complex, with some attributing it to the rise of 12-step programs and their involvement in military bases. However, this only addresses part of the problem; these programs have had to adapt to address drug and alcohol abuse among their own members.

The main challenge was a lack of support for affected individuals. Instructors would teach patriotism and self-protection, but lacked time and energy to address students' real issues.

To address this, the Army introduced substance abuse courses. As the problem grew, the military acknowledged the need for an integrated approach to prevention, detection, and response, including education, treatment options, and tracking.

While the situation was concerning, an investigation revealed that some soldiers were good personnel, and the drug testing was ineffective. Many were sent home for "failure to achieve unit goals" or struggled with mental health components.

Unfortunately, becoming a drug addict was a significant ask. Soldiers needed to learn about substance use, self-protection, and addiction treatment, all in the same environment. It was difficult, but they needed to start somewhere and found an outlet for their frustration.

The Military's Drug Problem

The military is facing unprecedented challenges, with drug abuse a significant issue. The military has played a significant role in the country's drug situation for decades, exacerbated by some soldiers using their service to access drugs. We're seeing more soldiers struggling with addiction and it's causing problems within the military.

We need to examine how the military addresses this issue, rather than trying to change it entirely. We must work together with other organizations to address the problem.

The UK is facing a concerning trend in food insecurity, with the number of people experiencing severe hunger projected to increase over the next two years. According to a recent report, the number of households struggling with "severely inadequate" food has risen by 13% in the past year, resulting in an additional 2.5 million individuals facing hunger and/or subsistence issues.

The Ministry of Food and Food Services' latest Food Poverty Report highlights the stark reality of food poverty in the UK. The report estimates that almost six million households have experienced food poverty in the past year, with the number of those in severe hunger more than doubling in the last year.

The report also reveals that the number of households suffering from "moderate to severe food poverty" has increased by 554% over the past decade, with 7.6 million households currently in this category. Labour MP Ann Coffey has called for a national food security scheme, stating that millions of families are facing food insecurity and the current welfare system is failing them.

The report highlights the reliance on state assistance, with 11.5 million households using some form of protection to meet food bills, and 1.24 million households receiving food and support payments to purchase fresh food. However, these numbers have decreased slightly in recent years due to government changes to the benefits system.

The report also reveals that a significant number of households are using food money to pay for essential items, such as mortgages and daily living expenses. Additionally, over 4.2 million households rely on welfare payments to meet basic living expenses, and almost half of those living in households in severe food poverty use at least one food entitlement.

The report highlights the impact on children, with over one million children suffering from at least one food poverty, and an estimated 8.6 million children eligible for the free breakfast, school lunch, and school dinner programme. However, the number of children in families in severe poverty has decreased by 0.5% from 2015.

The report also reveals that the number of families entitled to free school meals has increased by 13%, with 17.6 million households receiving one or more of the free meals. However, a quarter of families have not enrolled, and more than three quarters of free school meals recipients under the age of four are in families in severe food poverty.

Marianne Elliott, chief executive of Oxfam GB, has called for action to address the issue of food poverty, stating that the situation is "concerning" and requires a comprehensive approach to ensure that all individuals have access to adequate food and nutrition.

A recent study conducted by experts at the University of Wisconsin and the University of California, San Diego, reveals that nearly two-thirds of the world's mammals are facing extinction. The researchers analyzed over 3,100 mammal species globally and discovered that 86% of species with more than two adults have vanished. Notably, 65% of these species are endangered, while 32% are vulnerable to extinction.

Interestingly, the study found that some mammal families initially listed as "near threatened" have actually increased in numbers and range since their initial identification. However, this does not diminish the severity of the crisis, as even small population declines can have catastrophic consequences for many threatened mammal families.

To mitigate this crisis, the researchers emphasize the urgent need to conserve the remaining mammal populations, particularly those that have declined or are at risk of extinction. Conservation and restoration efforts are crucial for preserving mammal populations and ecosystems. For instance, the U.S. Forest Service's prescribed burns have a profound impact on the survival of rare or endangered mammals and plants.

The study also provides new insights into the status of mammal species with more than two adults. Notably, 61% of these species are threatened with extinction, 25% are likely to go extinct, and 3% are vulnerable to extinction. Furthermore, the study reveals that extinction rates have increased significantly in recent centuries, and some of the most threatened species may become extinct before the end of the century.

The researchers stress that even small ranges of species in almost every ecosystem are threatened with extinction, highlighting the magnitude of the problem. They urge policymakers to prioritize the management of remaining mammal populations to ensure habitat and population dynamics are not disrupted by the loss of individuals.

The researchers believe that this study underscores the importance of conservation and restoration efforts to ensure the survival of threatened and endangered mammal populations. With the world experiencing its sixth mass extinction, it is essential that policymakers take action to protect biodiversity conservation.

I've got a unique perspective on the University of Florida's reputation. Some folks might advise against venturing out, fearing injuries to opposing players. After a game, teammates often gather at the dormitory, where they're expected to spend the night.

The same dynamic applies to college football players. One evening, I hosted a few teammates and friends at my dorm room. We chatted about the importance of having fun and bonding with teammates, which can make a significant difference in team performance.

A few weeks later, I stumbled upon a group of teammates hanging out with about a dozen friends. After our two games that night, we decided to spend the evening together, as we were all exhausted and wanted to rest. It's a team sport, after all, and fatigue can affect everyone's performance.

That same night, I noticed the same players socializing with their roommates and playing pool. When I mentioned to one of them that I'd encouraged them to stop hanging out, he laughed and said, "I love playing pool and spending time with friends."

I jokingly told him that they should focus on football and their team, but he just chuckled. The next night, I went to bed early, feeling tired after a night out with friends. As the evening wore on, the group dispersed, and I found myself alone in the common room. I fell asleep on the floor, only to be awoken by someone banging on the door above mine.

I opened the door to find my roommate in a bed, with her arm around someone else and his arm around hers. I asked what was going on, and she replied it was 4 a.m. I asked her to keep the noise down, and she explained she'd spent the night elsewhere. I was annoyed and felt like she was disrupting my routine.

The next morning, I confronted her about my concerns. She asked what she was supposed to do when my friends could go home, and I explained that I just wanted to spend time with my teammates. She seemed understanding, but I still felt uneasy.

After that, our conversations became strained, and I eventually blocked her number. I never saw or spoke to her again, but it's clear she enjoyed her time with her teammates.

On February 12, 2015, the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit made a surprising decision. They rejected a petition for a writ of certiorari to the Eighth Circuit, which was a bit of a shock. The case, United States v. Kachalsky, had been making waves in the legal community. It all started when a police officer used a special device to take a photo of a part of a man's front door. The man claimed that seeing the photo without a warrant made him feel like he was being watched by the police. The court agreed that the government had done nothing wrong, but the man also argued that the government didn't need to get the information they did. The court didn't agree with that either.

The case went to the Supreme Court, and on April 19, the man asked them to take another look. But the Court decided not to get involved. This was a surprise to many, including the Eighth Circuit Court.

The Court's decision was a bit confusing, and it left some people wondering what was going on. The judge who wrote the decision, Edward R. Korman, said that the lower court had made a mistake by not considering the man's argument that the search was okay because the government already had the information they needed. Korman also thought that the government's use of the camera was important to the case.

This case has been going on for a while, and it's been a big deal in the legal world. The Supreme Court has said that a search is okay if the police get the information they need without getting a warrant. In this case, the police got the information they needed before they got the physical evidence. So, the court decided that the search was okay.

The dissenting judge, Ronald D. L. Gould, disagreed with the court's decision. He thought that the court was changing the rules and making it easier for the government to search people without a warrant. He said that this would weaken the Fourth Amendment, which protects people from unreasonable searches and seizures.

The Supreme Court's decision not to take the case was a surprise to many. The court didn't give a reason for their decision, and it left some people wondering what was going on.

On November 20, 2015, a significant development occurred in the realm of administrative law. A federal court in Arizona ruled that the Obama Administration had failed to comply with the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), marking the first time an APA order was issued against the President.

The Administrative Procedure Memorandum (APM) serves as a crucial guideline for executive branch agencies to operate in a streamlined, constitutional manner. However, the APM-1, which was recently overturned and vacated, has been deemed illegal and unenforceable. This has led to federal agencies abandoning the APA, operating as if they are above the law.

The President's Executive Order on Administrative Implementation of the APA emphasizes the importance of adopting and publishing regulatory actions in a timely manner. Nevertheless, the Obama Administration's new policy is shrouded in mystery, with language that is difficult to decipher.

The Department of Justice did not argue that the APM-1 is legally sound, instead claiming that the President lacks the authority to enforce it. However, this assertion does not grant the President the power to act unilaterally. As stated in section 5.3 of the APA, agencies must consider the impact of proposed actions on individuals and the enforcement of federal law and regulations.

The President's claim to authority is rooted in their election by the American people, but this does not grant them the power to disregard the law or the standards of the Executive Branch. The President's right is not self-enforcing, but rather an illusion.

Under the President's Executive Order, the Executive Branch is operating as if it is above the law, ignoring the requirements of the APA. 1. Creamy Lemon Chicken Piccata: Begin by heating two tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add four boneless skinless chicken breasts and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook the chicken for 6-8 minutes or until cooked through. Next, add 1/2 cup white wine and 1/2 cup lemon juice, stirring the liquid around the chicken. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and cook for an additional 5 minutes. Add 2 tablespoons of butter, 1/2 cup of sliced garlic, and 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley to the pan. Stir the ingredients and let them simmer for an additional 5 minutes. Serve the cooked chicken with the creamy sauce spooned over the top and your favorite side dish.

2. Southwestern Salmon Tacos: Preheat your oven to 400°F. Place a large salmon fillet on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and season both sides with salt and pepper. Spread 1 tablespoon of olive oil on the fish and bake for 18-22 minutes, or until the salmon is cooked through and flakes apart with a fork. To assemble the tacos, warm 8-10 small corn tortillas in a skillet on medium-high heat. Place the cooked fish in each taco and top with 1/2 cup chopped bell pepper, 1/4 cup of diced red onion, and 1/4 cup of salsa. Finish each taco with a squeeze of fresh lime juice before serving.

3. Spaghetti Squash Primavera: Preheat your oven to 375°F. Cut spaghetti squash in half lengthwise and remove the seeds. Drizzle with olive oil and place both halves cut side down on a baking sheet. Bake for 20-25 minutes and then let cool. Once cooled, use a fork to scrape the strands of squash from the skin. Place the strands on a parchment-lined baking sheet and season with salt and pepper. Heat two tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1/2 cup chopped carrots, 1/2 cup chopped zucchini, 1/2 cup chopped mushrooms, and 1/4 cup chopped red onion. Sauté the vegetables for 5-7 minutes or until softened and lightly browned. Add two cloves of garlic, minced, and cook an additional 30 seconds. Combine the spaghetti squash strands with the vegetables and serve over pasta or rice.

It's essential to understand the distinction between sexual misconduct, which is a criminal offense, and sexual harassment, which is also illegal. Unfortunately, many people are unaware that sexual harassment is a serious offense in India, punishable by law.

To clarify, sexual misconduct refers to any act that arouses or gratifies the sexual desire of another person. This includes indecent acts, demeaning comments, and sexual intercourse without consent. Any unlawful and unwanted act is considered sexual misconduct, and it's a criminal offense to engage in such behavior.

Sexual harassment, on the other hand, is defined as any abusive or insulting word, gesture, or conduct that could put a person in fear or alarm. This can include acts of touching or other forms of physical contact that cause discomfort or injury.

There's a crucial difference between a criminal complaint and a civil complaint in cases of sexual harassment. A criminal complaint is filed with the police, while a civil complaint is filed in court. A person may choose to file both types of complaints if they've experienced physical and psychological pain or humiliation as a result of the harassment.

The police will investigate the complaint and decide whether to file charges under the Indian Penal Code, the Indian POCSO Act, or other relevant laws. The complainant may also choose to file a civil complaint, stating that the harassing act amounts to sexual misconduct.

It's essential to note that whether sexual misconduct or harassment is recorded as a criminal offense depends on various factors, including the circumstances of the case. The police officer, the prosecutrix, the accused, and the fact of the offense will all play a significant role in determining how the complaint is handled.

Ultimately, it's crucial to recognize that sexual harassment is a serious offense that requires legal action. If you've experienced sexual harassment, you have the right to file a complaint with the police and seek justice.

Recently, the US Supreme Court ruled that the "unrestricted exercise of constitutional rights" would extend to individuals opposing the Affordable Care Act's contraception mandate. Concurrently, the Court established a new category of protected discrimination: denying healthcare coverage for "preventive services" - that is, family planning and contraception.

The majority decision was a complex one, with no clear basis but a judicial whim. The Court ruled that a small Catholic employer, Hobby Lobby, could refuse to cover contraception due to religious beliefs.

The Court stated that the government couldn't penalize Hobby Lobby for refusing to cover birth control. In essence, the decision emphasized that the US government, not employers, should be responsible for funding or covering contraceptive services.

Now, the government should pay for insurance plans covering those services? No. Insurance companies cannot be compelled to offer services - not even those they strongly support. The government cannot force individuals with religious beliefs to violate those beliefs.

This outcome stems from a 2010 Supreme Court decision. The justices ruled 5-4 in Burwell v. Hobby Lobby that federal law didn't prohibit religious employers from requiring employees to contribute to the employer's health insurance plan.

Justice Samuel Alito wrote the majority opinion, holding that a for-profit corporation engaged in religious exercise has a sincere religious objection to providing health insurance coverage for abortifacients. Justice Anthony Kennedy wrote a separate concurring opinion, stating that the employer's exercise of religious liberty was the basis for the case.

Kennedy concluded that the government did have a compelling interest in allowing Hobby Lobby to opt out of the birth control mandate. This, he believed, "makes all the difference." The law cannot compel a religious objector to subsidize conduct they oppose.

However, there's a problem with this: The Supreme Court is incorrect about the compelling interest. Kennedy, who wrote that the government cannot compel the religious objector to subsidize conduct they oppose, actually has the compelling interest in forcing a corporation to pay for contraceptives.

Hobby Lobby is a "person" under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act. Under RFRA, a government action is substantially burdened if it forces religious objectors to violate their religious tenets. Hobby Lobby compelled the plaintiffs to make a decision that would involve the most intimate details of their relationship with their God.

Justices Stephen Breyer, Sonia Sotomayor, and Elena Kagan filed concurring opinions, stating that Hobby Lobby should not be permitted to avoid the contraception rule due to its status as a closely held corporation.

Pricework is a real-time performance monitoring tool for Java applications. It provides a clear view of what's happening beneath the surface of your application, giving you valuable insights into code execution and performance bottlenecks.

You can easily identify which parts of your code are slowing down and optimize accordingly. The tool runs your application in a JVM environment, leveraging various profiling techniques to deliver accurate results.

A performance snapshot is taken every 5 seconds, providing a comprehensive overview of system-level performance metrics. This project is a fork of Pardot, maintained by developers who have added new features and improvements.

Current release: 0.10.4

Getting started

To begin, ensure you have a Java runtime and the Java 8 compiler installed. You can easily obtain these by downloading the Oracle JDK installer.

To run the application, navigate to the project directory and execute the following command:

java -jar src/pricework-0.10.4-SNAPSHOT-all.jar

The program will start, and you'll see a message indicating the application is running in the background. You can also run the application from startup using the following command:

java -server -cp src/pricework-0.10.4-SNAPSHOT-all.jar [options] [app]

If you encounter the message "Not registered - org.pricework.app.PricworkLauncher not open," it may indicate that an instance of the PriceworkLauncher class is already running. In this case, you can use that instance for startup.

Once the application is running, you can access its homepage to explore the API.

Running tests

You can run your application using Maven by executing:

mvn -DskipTests http://localhost:1234/main/pricework-0.10.4-SNAPSHOT-all.jar

To run tests, use the following command:

mvn -DDESTDIR=test -DskipTests run -Plec -DskipTests test

Justice Elena Kagan dissented, arguing that the right to adopt or foster a child is fundamental to human dignity, while protecting children from being denied that right is not unreasonable.

The ruling means that the previous Supreme Court decision giving same-sex couples the right to marry will have no impact on this case. The court also ruled that a similar ban on marriage equality in Minnesota, which passed in 2009 and has not been overturned, does not violate the constitutional rights of same-sex couples.

The plaintiffs argued that the law discriminates against Illinois same-sex couples because the Illinois state constitution does not contain any protections for the right to marry or adopt. They also alleged an unconstitutional burden on their right to privacy. However, the court found that the plaintiffs had not made a convincing case that the restrictions on marriage and adoption violate their rights to privacy and equal protection under the law.

The case concerns an adoption ban enacted in 2012, which barred same-sex couples from adopting or fostering children unless they had married, converted to one sex, or divorced or separated. The plaintiffs cited US constitutional protections such as freedom of religion and freedom of intimate association as evidence that they should have a right to adopt or foster children. However, the majority ruled that those constitutional guarantees are not sufficient to justify the adoption ban.

The case was brought by two gay couples, Jennifer Mundy and Mary Lou Brinkman, and Gary and Mark Pincus, who had adopted a baby boy from a gay couple in California. They subsequently filed suit against the attorney general, arguing that the ban on adopting and fostering children violates both federal and state constitutional rights. The state argues that the ban is needed to protect the public health and safety, as same-sex couples do not act as parents or provide parental care, and that if their children end up with those couples, their potential for abuse diminishes.

A trial judge earlier ruled in their favor, and the appeal court ruled in their favor in March. The decision will be sent back to the Illinois appeals court and will only have effect if the appeals courts rule that the plaintiffs have proved they have a legal right to marry.

The tale of the enigmatic "Shakeys of America." Their narrative could be a multitude of things, or a multitude of things could be "Shakeys of America." Mike Ritrovato, a Star Wars aficionado residing in an old building on Third Street in the East Village, shares his favorite Star Wars film, 1977's "Empire Strikes Back." "You know those, like, droids with lightsabers? When they emerge and begin shooting lasers, only to vanish suddenly, but if you don't stop, they reappear, shouting 'Droid! Droid!'"

The individuals I've introduced, and those who reside nearby, are part of the "Shakeys of America" community. This group includes Ritrovato, who works in maintenance at the city recreation department, and his friends, a group of 10 to 15 men bearing the last name "Shake." At night, they gather at their homes to watch movies, drink, and play dice. "We're a family, but most people perceive us as a movie theater or a bar," Ritrovato remarks.

That's not Ritrovato's perspective. In fact, he's become convinced that the Shakeys are a community. On the day we met for our interview, they were hosting a "Star Wars"-themed party at a local restaurant, Star Wars, renowned for its delectable cuisine.

The Shakeys originated in 1970s Philadelphia and their connection to the film industry is a relatively recent development. "George Lucas and I visited his Marin County residence, where he had a small barbecue pit in his backyard," Ray explains. "That marked the beginning. We dubbed it the Shakey Pit."

In 1982, Ray conceived the idea of establishing what would eventually become their group. The only thing lacking, he says, was a name for their organization. On the first night of their gatherings, Ray recalls, "someone else mentioned, 'Shakey, we're getting too big.' I remember him telling me he wouldn't want to be my leader anymore." Ray notes that it was later, in 1986, that he suggested they adopt a "company name." He chose "The Society for the Promotion of the First Respondering Shakey and the Promotion of the Second Rescuing Shakey Organizations."

Ray still considers his creation the best thing to have happened to his neighborhood since the construction of the subway.

"The entire neighborhood transformed after that one event," Ray says. "They simply stopped doing cocaine and everything changed."

However, as the 1980s progressed, the Shakeys continued to grow. "At some point, at least 10 guys moved into the next apartment at 17th and Second," Ray says, who is now 67. As he acquired a larger house, he also gained more people. By the late 1980s, the neighborhood had begun to flourish once more.

"The first time it happened, the place was filled with people, all in one house," Ray says, pointing to a large, black house at 24th and First. "At one point, we were discussing getting a new house," Ray says. "I turned and said to him, 'George Lucas wants to live here.' And I had no idea that I would end up giving him the house we now own!"

The Lucas and the current Shakey owners do not share the same history. When Lucas purchased the house at 24th and First, he was the owner of Lucasfilm, a computer graphics and computer animation company based in San Francisco. The house, Ray says, sold to Lucas at a fraction of its actual value. "If you visited Google Maps, it's right where we are," Ray says, pointing to the houses on his block, all situated on the same block.

In the years that followed, the Lucas house became a regular gathering spot for the community to come together. "I still take pictures here, but they're so awkward," Ray says. "They're not looking at the camera. They're either talking or, like, watching television, and it's just peculiar."

But then one day in the early '1990s, Ray says, he and the other Shakeys received a call from the Lucas family. "George said, 'Shakey, here's the place I want to live.' I said, 'How much did you pay for it?'

Portland's streets have seen a significant surge in homeless children under 18 over the past two years, surpassing levels from a decade ago, according to a new study. This raises questions about the city's effectiveness in addressing youth homelessness.

While the number of homeless youth remains below pre-task force levels, the rate of increase in 2016 far outpaced the 10% increase noted in an earlier report from 2011.

As of March 1, approximately 2,300 homeless juveniles and young adults comprised 8% of the total homeless population.

The study, commissioned by Rep. Earl Blumenauer and the National Law Center on Homelessness & Poverty at Columbia Law School, will be presented to lawmakers at a Richmond hearing today.

The report reveals that homeless youth numbers increased nearly 150% between 2010 and 2016, with a current total of around 2,400. This is a significant increase of 1,800 youth from the 2010 count and 500 above the peak year for growth.

The authors are seeking additional data after discovering an error in the 2016 numbers, which showed 1,534 youth sought services. The error occurred in surveys from January 1 to April 9, but the rate of increase was too large to be attributed solely to a single day of data.

Rep. Blumenauer emphasized that the rise in youth homelessness is a concern for both the city and the Legislature, and that there is still more work to be done. While Portland has made progress in reducing the number of youth on the streets, many other cities are experiencing similar increases.

"We have a long way to go, with no end in sight," Blumenauer said. "Portland's policies for youth homelessness must be at the forefront of the national debate. We can no longer ignore the issue when cities across the country are seeing similar changes in their homeless youth populations."

The study was commissioned to develop an assessment of youth homelessness and explores the costs of homelessness, offering recommendations to improve solutions. The report was released alongside another NCLP-funded study examining the causes of homelessness among youths.

To access the reports, visit the National Law Center on Homelessness & Poverty website.

A remarkable celestial phenomenon has been observed by a team of astronomers from the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Agriculture. Utilizing the BOSS survey, they discovered a faint, ghostly presence orbiting a galaxy previously unseen. The ghostly entity was detected in a distant galaxy, IC 4342, situated approximately 3 billion light-years away. The researchers employed a novel technique, leveraging the Spitzer Space Telescope's images, to track the ghost's brief appearance.

The team's innovative approach allowed them to visualize IC 4342 as a spiral galaxy. The ghost's motion, observed during its orbit around the galaxy's nucleus, was a key indicator of its presence. The BOSS survey, designed to detect galaxy ghosts in nearby galaxies, surprisingly yielded no results in this case.

The discovery of IC 4342's ghost is significant, as it represents the first time such an entity has been observed at such a great distance. Yifang Luo, a PhD student at the University of Tokyo, noted, "This method enables us to capture images and measure what galaxies can perceive with their own eyes, yet lack the technology to achieve."

It is not uncommon for galaxies to possess faint ghosts, which can only be detected with specialized telescopes like Spitzer or Hubble. However, many galaxies remain invisible to our telescopes, including the largest galaxies in the universe.

Yifang explained, "Ghost galaxies are only visible to optical light from the galaxies with which they orbit, making them invisible to us. We believe that most galaxies harbor ghosts due to the way our cosmic view of the visible universe has evolved."

Mattias Almgren Andersen, a professor of communications at Indiana University Bloomington, shares his enthusiasm for the study's findings. The lead author of the research published in Current Biology, Andersen highlights the significance of the new results. Meanwhile, the researchers emphasize the importance of ensuring the accuracy of their conclusions. In the absence of a rigorous experimental approach, they recognize the difficulty in verifying their results. For now, the study suggests that the visual signal observed is likely an echo.

I've been searching for an alternative to Gimp for the past few months. I initially tried Libre Office, but the changes they made to their word processor didn't suit my needs. I then discovered GIMP, which stood out to me due to its lightweight nature, ability to play audio files, and image resizing capabilities. The team behind GIMP is constantly working on improvements, and it also has the support of other projects like OpenShot and GX.

One limitation of GIMP is that it's not cross-platform, but many people are running it on Linux. I was excited to have it on our server and found the installation process to be quick and easy. The graphics are vibrant, and the interface is user-friendly.

In this article, I'll show you how to set up a simple web-based photo editor using GIMP. You'll need to adapt some parts to your specific needs.

First, download the GIMP source code from the official website and run it. You'll be prompted to set up a user account and create directories. We'll discuss this later, so let's move on to the next step.

Run the command "gimp-init" to start the GIMP daemon and initialize the file system. Make sure the disk has been initialized before proceeding.

Next, navigate to the configuration directory and adjust the settings to your liking. You can change the size of the application area and the text type. I prefer a minimum size of 50 pixels high and dark grey and black text.

Now you can access the first page of the editor. The design at the top is unique, but it's not essential. You can start writing a simple text or make changes to the page using the menu.

To make changes, select "Edit Page" and then "Insert." This command can be repeated and deleted. The final command does something different – it lists all files when you press Control+V. You can select what you want to write and edit it.

For my purposes, I made a simple comment. Notice how some changes to the text stand out above the text used in the image.

The next step is to edit the image file. I know this might seem unusual, but I do it simply by clicking on the icon, selecting "Text Tools," and then GIMP. The GIMP image editor offers more than basic image editing. You can change the image size to any value using the "Adjust Image Size" and "Adjust Picture Quality" tools.

Using GIMP's image resize capabilities can be a huge time-saver. You can edit the image to add a smile or adjust the size to fit the screen. This is where GIMP's image resize capabilities come into play.

As we navigate through circular motion, a peculiar phenomenon emerges: the sensation of being propelled away from the central axis. This is precisely what occurs when you're cruising in a vehicle and take a sharp turn. Your body's natural inclination is to maintain a straight trajectory, yet the vehicle's trajectory diverges, resulting in a force that appears to be pushing you towards the periphery.

Conversely, there exists a force that governs the trajectory of objects in circular motion, drawing them towards the central axis. This force, known as centripetal force, is responsible for the moon's orbit around our planet. Gravity, a fundamental force of nature, exemplifies this principle.

In summary, centrifugal force is the perceived force that arises from our experience of circular motion, whereas centripetal force is the actual force that orchestrates our movement within those circular paths.

Three influential faiths, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, share a common thread - a strong belief in a single, all-powerful deity. These religions also share a rich history, with roots tracing back to the Middle East and the Abrahamic tradition. Despite this shared heritage, each faith has its unique characteristics, shaped by distinct beliefs and teachings. Let's explore some of the key differences.

For instance, while all three faiths acknowledge a single God, their understanding of this deity differs. Jews view God as the universe's creator, just, and loving, yet they reject the concept of a Trinity. Christians, on the other hand, believe in a Trinity and consider Jesus the Son of God. Muslims, meanwhile, see God as the one and only, with Jesus being a revered prophet, but not the Son of God.

Jesus' role is another area of divergence. Jews do not accept Jesus as the Messiah, whereas Christians believe he is the Son of God and the Messiah sent to redeem humanity from sin. Muslims, too, consider Jesus a prophet, but do not view him as the Son of God or the Messiah.

Each faith also has its own sacred text, considered the word of God. The Jewish Torah contains the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, while the Christian Bible comprises the Old and New Testaments. The Muslim holy book, the Qur'an, is revered as the word of God.

Practices and rituals also vary between the three faiths. Jews observe Jewish laws and traditions outlined in the Torah, celebrating holidays like Hanukkah and Passover. A delightful frozen treat, homemade Vanilla Cake from the freezer is a personal favorite. This year, I decided to share it with friends at a gathering. I prepared the cake in the morning, allowing it to freeze for later. What a perfect indulgence! 

I experimented with various cake recipes, seeking the perfect combination of flavor, freshness, and low added sugar. I was thrilled to discover this recipe from The Real Bakes, a talented blogger. 

To create this frozen cake, you'll need:

2 egg whites

1 ½ tablespoon water (adjust to taste)

½ tsp baking soda (I prefer sea salt for its ease of use)

¼ cup granulated sugar (use more for a less sweet version)

¼ cup almond milk

1 tablespoon vanilla extract

2 Tablespoons flour (optional, depending on your cake flour's texture)

Instructions:

Combine the cake ingredients in a stand mixer bowl with the paddle attachment. Mix on low speed until smooth, then add ¼ cup almond milk and continue mixing on medium speed until well combined. When the mixture becomes thin, it's ready to add water (or less) to achieve the desired consistency. Stir in the baking soda and set the mixture aside for 10-15 minutes. Before serving, refrigerate the cake to allow it to firm up. This step is crucial, as the cake will not stick to food and is ready for the ice cream frosting.

For the egg whites, use your preferred whipping cream recipe or a pre-made egg whisk. I opted not to make it, but there are many recipes available for this cake. You can also prepare the egg whites a few hours in advance if needed.

To pipe the frosting, heat it in the microwave or oven. I chose to microwave it slowly.

This recipe is surprisingly easy to make, requiring only a stand mixer, egg mixture, and an ice cream machine. The frozen version is a crowd-pleaser.

A file type is a container for a type of file that is written according to the format specified by the format attribute. Text is a type of file that stores text files. Formatting is a type of file type specified by format=text.

File types can be specified in several ways. They can be specified by either a file type prefix or by using the /? path keyword without a file type. For example, you can specify the file type prefix for a specific file by specifying the filetype option with a file type name. You can also specify the path with the path option.

You can use format modifiers to make files of that file type with a specific naming convention. For example, you can use the %filetype_prefix =.ps %filetype_suffix = ps %filetype_suffix = xls %filetype_suffix =.xml %filetype_suffix =.md %filetype_prefix =.vmdk format modifier to change file extensions for a specific file type.

File extensions can also be specified in several ways. A file type can have one or more file extensions. For more information about file extensions, see File Extension and Related Options.

There is nothing special about the way these options are formatted. They are simply stored as a string and added to the filetype_suffix or %.vmdk variable.

Text files are created by using a special text file type. For more information, see the following topics: File Attributes, Windows: Formatting and Editing Files.

Visual C++ file types

Visual C++ and C++-supporting applications use a special type of file for files that are not text files. These files are created when a program runs on a computer that does not have the Visual C++ compiler installed. For more information, see Visual C++ File Types.

Kuala Lumpur, October 14 - The number of individuals seeking employment or actively looking for a job during the second half of 2016 declined by 30.7% to 32.3 million between January and June, representing the lowest figure since 2009.

Statistics Malaysia released data yesterday, indicating a 6.6% decrease in the number of unemployed compared to the same period last year.

"The unemployment rate for the first six months of this year decreased to 5.2% from 5.37% in 2015. The rate for the second half of last year was relatively low at 4.8% from 5.36% in 2015," the agency stated.

"The decrease from June to January is attributed to the decline in the unemployment rate among the labour force," it added.

According to the latest data, 33,633 thousand individuals were actively seeking employment in the country between January and June.

In the six months ending June, 30,074 thousand individuals held a job, while 29.8 million went without employment, as per the report.

The second-quarter employment rate was 3.9%, 0.5 percentage points lower than the rate in the same period last year.

The employment rate is the percentage of adults with a full-time job, who were also actively seeking employment and available to work during the survey period. This figure is calculated by dividing the labour force in the employment estimation system by the number of employed individuals in the labour force.

The report highlighted positive signs for the outlook, but noted that the unemployment level remained one of the lowest in the country.

"We will need to wait at least two more quarters to determine if the decrease in the unemployment rate will continue," it stated.

There have been positive trends in labour force growth in recent months, with total employment and unemployment in the three months ending June 2016 increasing by 1.6% and 1.2%, respectively, up from the first three months of 2016.

"In the first quarter of 2016, total employment continued to rise, and the unemployment rate decreased to a 5-year low at 5.6%," it stated.

The two measures, the overall unemployment rate and the unemployment rate for those aged between 25 and 54 years, were respectively lower and unchanged compared to the three months ending June 2015.

In June, the labour force participation rate was 60.7%, down 0.4 percentage points from the first three months of 2016 and 0.5 percentage points lower than the same period last year at 62.3%.

The total number of employed individuals increased to 3.6 million at the same time last year, compared with 3.65 million in the same three months in 2015.

The unemployment rate as a proportion of the total number of employed individuals was 3.7 percentage points and 2.9 percentage points lower than the rate in the same quarter of 2015.

"The proportion of young individuals in the labour force is higher this year, particularly in the tertiary sector. The youth labour force participation rate is higher in all but the tertiary sector," it added.

Malaysia is expected to have a favourable employment scenario in the coming years following the government's enactment of labour deregulation laws, which enabled employers to hire and fire more flexibly and reduce wage rates.

The regulations apply to all sectors except for the construction industry, it added. - Bernama

Coconut Milk & Butterscotch Sauce: A Sweet and Savory Combination

The coconut milk in this sauce is surprisingly easy to digest and pairs well with a variety of dishes, from burgers to vegetables and soups. The ingredients list reveals that the coconut milk serves as both a natural sweetener and a source of lactic acid bacteria, which adds depth to the flavor. When you taste it, you'll notice a subtle tanginess from the bacteria.

To enhance the flavor, I've added a hint of butterscotch, which complements the coconut nicely. If you're a fan of butterscotch, consider adding a drizzle of fruit extract for an extra layer of flavor.

What sets this recipe apart is its simplicity. Unlike other sauces that require intense heat, this one can be prepared at room temperature. Simply blend the ingredients together, and you're good to go. The sauce can be stored in the fridge for later use or even frozen for a future dessert.

The coconut milk is the star of the show, but the butter adds a richness and creaminess to the sauce. To balance the flavors, I've used a moderate amount of coconut milk, which prevents the sauce from becoming too thick.

Ingredients:

* 1 cup coconut milk, divided
* 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
* 1/4 cup pure maple syrup
* 2 tablespoons butterscotch extract
* 1 large egg
* 1/4 cup sweetened shredded coconut
* 1 1/2 tablespoons lactic acid bacteria culture (optional)

Instructions:

1. Blend the coconut milk until smooth.
2. Add the butter, butterscotch, maple syrup, and seasonings, and blend for 10-15 seconds.
3. Add the egg and blend for an additional minute.
4. Spoon the sauce over a sweetened muffin, baked potato, or macaroni and cheese, and enjoy!

Note: This recipe makes about 2 cups of sauce, enough for 2 dessert sauces.

- A pinch of salt

A diverse patient population was analyzed, with characteristics that may serve as a benchmark for comparison with other studies. This study is part of a series evaluating the efficacy and safety of low-dosage, low-intensity pulsed ECHS (LDE-PEED) versus standard D2.6 PEEP. The trial compared the outcomes of patients with moderate to severe RA receiving LDE-PEED versus standard D2.6 PEEP, with LDE-PEED demonstrating superior results in patients with moderate to severe RA.

The patient population had a median follow-up of 16 months, with a high level of education in Spanish. All patients were in remission, and all except two had received standard D2.6 PEEP.

The results of this trial align with previous studies. In summary, LDE-PEED for moderate RA yielded similar clinical outcomes compared to standard D2.6 PEEP.

LDE-PEED was compared to traditional D2.6 pulse technique (PEEP). This randomized, controlled trial was published online on February 25, 2011, in Thoracic Surgery.

The study population consisted of 29 patients, with 19 in the LDE-PEED group and 18 in the control group. The patients were randomly assigned to receive either LDE-PEED with four pulses or PEEP.

The LDE-PEED technique involved two pulse sequences, where the patient inhaled a single, deep breath while the breathing rate was lowered 2.5-3 times per minute. The technique was repeated.

The primary outcome measures included mean arterial blood pressure, serum creatinine, body mass index, RANKL level, total number of inhaled air/respiratory minute, and patient-reported outcomes.

An objective outcome measure was the mean change in the LDE-PEED technique compared to standard D2.6 PEEP at the end of 12 weeks. This subjective outcome measure was used to assess patient outcomes.

The results showed a mean increase in mean arterial blood pressure (7.8%), a mean reduction in total pulmonary function air exchange (3% [P=0.001]), and a percent increase in peak O2 uptake. The mean reduction in total pulmonary function air exchange in the LDE-PEED group was compared to the control group, with significance shown as p<0.001.

Young people are less likely than their elders to perceive public education as generally beneficial for America.

The earthquake's impact is quantifiable through various tools, such as an on-site earthquake gauge, seismic recorder, or seismic chart.
